A10-P POS-A COMMAND SPECIFICATION FOR CODEX / ANDROID IMPLEMENTATION
==============================================================================

Source: A10-P Programmer's Manual, Personal ID Number Pad with EMV Level 2 Transaction Capabilities, BV2 Version, POS-A Specification, PM 0122-C1, Revision 8, dated 2022-04-01.
Generated from uploaded PDF: A10-P_Programmer_s_Manual_BV2_220331.pdf
Generated UTC: 2026-06-27 16:59:48

Purpose of this file
--------------------
This text file reorganizes the A10-P interchange messages/commands into a Codex-friendly implementation reference. It keeps the command IDs, purpose/usage, request/response formats, field tables, error values, and message-flow notes from the manual, while adding an implementation-oriented index and protocol notes.

Critical implementation notes
-------------------------------
1. All control-code tokens such as <STX>, <ETX>, <SI>, <SO>, <FS>, <GS>, <SUB>, <ACK>, <NAK>, and <EOT> represent raw single bytes, not printable ASCII text. Field values are ASCII strings unless the field description says binary or hex string.
2. Two primary frame families are used: <STX>[message ID][data]<ETX>[LRC] for most transaction messages and <SI>[message ID][data]<SO>[LRC] for many administration/maintenance messages.
3. LRC is the XOR of every byte after the start byte (<STX> or <SI>) through and including the end byte (<ETX> or <SO>). Append the resulting one-byte LRC after the end delimiter.
4. After the A10-P sends a message, the host should respond with <ACK> for a valid frame or <NAK> for LRC/receive error. If A10-P receives no response within 5 seconds, it retransmits. After two retransmits without <ACK>/<NAK>, A10-P sends <EOT> and terminates that communication session.
5. Treat PINs, encryption keys, PANs, track data, DUKPT KSNs, and EMV cryptographic material as sensitive. Do not log them in production Android builds.
6. In the command details, source pages refer to the PDF page numbers shown by the manual/PDF.

Control-code byte table
-----------------------
STX = 0x02  beginning of <STX> message frame
ETX = 0x03  ending delimiter of <STX> message frame
ACK = 0x06  acknowledge
SO  = 0x0E  ending delimiter of <SI> message frame
SI  = 0x0F  beginning of <SI> message frame (shown as <SI> in message formats)
NAK = 0x15  invalid frame/LRC error
SUB = 0x1A  message-parameter delimiter
FS  = 0x1C  field separator
GS  = 0x1D  message-ID delimiter
DC1 = 0x11  Z2 inverse mode on
DC2 = 0x12  Z2 inverse mode off

Suggested Android model
-----------------------
Create a FrameCodec with encode(messageId, payload, frameType) and decode(bytes). Represent each command as a typed data class with: commandId, name, frameType, requestFormat, responseFormat, fields, and expectedReplies. Implement transport as a byte stream over USB CDC-ACM or RS-232; the manual lists USB 2.0 full-speed CDC-ACM VID=0x6352/PID=0x294A and RS232 9600 bps, no parity, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit.

Command count extracted: 229 command sections/variants.

COMMAND INDEX
==============================================================================

Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
---------------------------------------------------
001. 02 - Load Master Key (Clear Text) (PDF page 35-38)
     Length: Variable (22 to 58 bytes).
     Format: <SI>02[Key ID][Key value]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Send the key value to the A10-P and save into designated master key slot. A10-P can store 21 master keys (A10-P application only uses 16 of them for backword compatibility); each with a one digit ID. These Master keys are divided into three groups of different functions. Refer to Appendix A for key usage and ID definition. Clear text key injection is only accepted in the "Key Injection" session of the system manager; which is enabled by dual-password authentication. This function should be used only in security-controlled environment with HSM. Refer to Appendix A for detailed information. The algorithm of the injected key is defined by the...
002. 02 - Load Master Key (TR-31 Bundle) (PDF page 39-40)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <SI>02[Key ID][TR-31 Key Bundle]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Send the encrypted and MACed key bundle (ANSI TR-31: 2018 format) to the A10-P and save into the designated master key slot. A10-P will use the key transport key (key slot #F) to validate and decrypt the key bundle. If key management scheme is set to TDES, A10-P will use TDES algorithm to do validation and decryption.
003. 04 - Check Master Key (PDF page 41-42)
     Length: Variable (6 or 7) bytes for request frame. Variable (6 or 22) bytes for response frame.
     Format: <SI>04[key ID][get attr]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>04[response code][attr]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Check if the specified master key exists, and optionally get its TR31 attributes.
004. 05 - Load Serial Number (PDF page 43)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <SI>05[string]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Load the A10-P with the serial number given in the message frame. The A10-P will send the whole message frame back to the host as a confirmation of good reception. If the LRC is good but the echoed serial number is incorrect the host should then send an <ACK> to confirm or an <EOT> to cancel this serial number loading process. Follow the standard <NAK> process if an invalid LRC is detected.
005. 06 - Get Serial Number (PDF page 44)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes for the requesting message, Variable for the response message.
     Format: <SI>06<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>06[string]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to get the serial number of the A10-P. The A10-P will send the serial number previously loaded or a string of 16 '0's as the serial number if it has not been loaded. The serial number will be displayed on the LCD.
006. 07 - Test Crypto Implementation (PDF page 45-46)
     Length: Fixed 53 bytes for DES test.
     Format: <SI>07[master key][clear text][cipher text]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>07[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to validate the DES implementation of A10-P. Test result will be shown on the A10-P display and a response code will be returned for remote diagnostic.
007. 08 - Select Active Master Key (PDF page 47)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>08[KeyID]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to select an "active" master key from one of the 10 possible PIN encrypting master keys previously loaded using message 02. The active master key will be used in the following transactions.
008. 09 - Communication Test (PDF page 48-49)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes for the requesting message, fixed 16 bytes for the response message.
     Format: <SI>09<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>09<SUB>PROCESSING<SO>[LRC] (response frame) <SI>09[response code][LRC] (Result frame)
     Usage: This message is used to test communication link between the host and the A10-P. Both host and A10-P can initiate a communication test. The initiating party should send the requesting message; the other party should respond with the response message that should be ACKed if received correctly. After verifying that the response message is correct, the initiating party should send back the same response message and the receiving party should acknowledge this message. The test results are shown on the A10-P display.
009. 11 - A10-P Device Connection Test (PDF page 50)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <SI>11<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to ensure that the A10-P attached to the host is working normally. The A10-P will respond an ACK (or NAK if LRC is incorrect) within one second.
010. 12 - Select Prompt Language (PDF page 51-52)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>12[language index]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>12[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to select the A10-P prompt message table for different languages. The English prompt table is resident as default and its index number is '0'. Other prompts can be updated and selected and the A10-P will select the corresponding code page for display. NOTE. The order of the supported language may be different from this manual as the prompt message module changes. Refer to the response from A10-P through message 1F.
011. 13 - Adjust COM1 Baud Rate (RS-232 version only) (PDF page 53-54)
     Length: Variable, 6~7 bytes.
     Format: <SI>13[baud code][mode]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>13[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message will change the communication baud rate and transmit mode of the A10-P for later operations. The setting is kept in the non-volatile memory. The baud rate will be changed after the message flow ends.
012. 14 - Enable/Disable Timer Display (PDF page 55)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>14[E/D]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>14[Status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to enable/ disable the system timer display of the A10-P.
013. 15 - Adjust LCD Backlight And Contrast Level (PDF page 56-57)
     Length: Fixed 8 bytes for the request message. Fixed 8 bytes for the response message.
     Format: <SI>15[backlight]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>15[backlight status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message will set the backlight and contrast level of the LCD display.
014. 16 - Remote self-test request (PDF page 58)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <SI>16<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>16[Response]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is reserved for backward compatilibity, user of the A10-P should use message 20 to get the real meaningful remote diagnostic information.
015. 17 - Request random number (PDF page 59)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <SI>17<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>17[RndBlk]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to request the A10-P to generate an 8-byte random number block. This random number is generated by the hardware TRNG (True Random Number Generator) that is certified with sufficient security.
016. 18 - Set PIN pad local time (PDF page 60-61)
     Length: Fixed 20 bytes.
     Format: <SI>18[YYYY][MM][DD][W][HH][MM][SS]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>18[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message sets the A10-P local time.
017. 19 - Query Firmware Version (PDF page 62-64)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes (request frame) / Variable (response frame).
     Format: <SI>19[part]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>196[options]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>19.[Version].[SubVer].[hash]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to query the A10-P firmware version number and the firmware check sum value.
018. 1C - Query Hardware Capability (PDF page 65-66)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes (request); variable (response).
     Format: <SI>1C<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1C[string]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to query the peripheral capability of the A10-P.
019. 1F - Query Usable Prompt Table (PDF page 67-68)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes (request frame); variable (response frame).
     Format: <SI>1F<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1F[Prompt_List]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to query the usable A10-P prompt message table list. The list will be represented as 2-character country codes defined by ISO 3166.
020. 1G - Test Prompt Table (PDF page 69)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>1G[option]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to show prompt table message on LCD display.
021. 1J - Turn ON/OFF LCD Backlight (PDF page 70-71)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>1J[option]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1J[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message can control the global backlight on or off for the LCD display of the A10-P. By default, A10-P will turn on its LCD backlight when it receives PIN entry or a clear text entry message such as 70 or Z50, and turn it off when those functions exit. By sending message "1J1", A10-P will keep the LCD backlight turned on until message "1J0" is issued.
022. 1K - Turn ON/OFF LCD Power-save mode (PDF page 72-73)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>1K[option]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1K[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: For power consumption saving, this message can automatically adjust the backlight of the A10-P to darker level after several seconds. The backlight level will return to the level set before when a key strobe is pressed, a message of PIN entry or a key entry is received.
023. 1M - Setup Keypad Beeper (PDF page 74-75)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <SI>1M[option]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1M[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to enable or disable the beeper in response to the key press.
024. 1P - Control Beeper (PDF page 76-77)
     Length: Fixed 15 bytes for request frame, and 6bytes for response frame.
     Format: <SI>1P<SUB>[count]<FS>[duration]<FS>[interval]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>1P[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to customize the behavior of beeper. The command runs once, user has to issue this command whenever user needs sound.
025. M03 - Load Permanent Unit Serial Number (PDF page 78-79)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <SI>M03[PUSN][Slot]<SO>[LRC] (response frame) <SI>M03[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to load the permanent unit serial number (PUSN) into the PIN pad. PIN pad supports 8 PUSN slots for customer.
026. M04 - Read Permanent Unit Serial Number (PDF page 80-84)
     Length: Fixed 6(7) bytes.
     Format: <SI>M04[Slot]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>M04[Status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame) <SI>M04[PUSN]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to query the permanent USN inside the PIN pad.

Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
----------------------------------------------------
027. T01 - Terminal Configuration Setup (PDF page 85-87)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T01[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Host can use this command to send the terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times. The A10-P will save those data internally and utilize them during the transaction. The A10-P will send message T02 (Terminal Configuration Setup Response) to the host as a response. The functions of Message T01 and Message T51 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.
028. T02 - Terminal Configuration Setup Response (PDF page 88)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T02[Result][Reason][Err Msg][Err Tag Number]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The response message of message T01. The functions of Message T02 and Message T52 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.

     Usage: Host can use this command to send the Certification Authority Public key data to the A10-P. Each command can only setup one key but this command can be sent many times. The A10-P will save those key data inside and use those data during the transaction. A10-P will send message T04 (Certification Authority Public Key Setup Response) to the host. The data is installed into the A10-P via this message and it will then be saved into its internal storage structure with a name as the concatenation of the values in the [RID] and [PKI] fields. For example, the value in the [RID] field is "A000000003" and the value in the [PKI] field is "90", then t...
030. T04 - Certification Authority Public Key Setup Response (PDF page 93)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T04[Sequence][Result][Reason][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The response message of message T03. The functions of Message T04 and Message T54 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.
031. T05 - EMV Application Configuration Setup (PDF page 94-97)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T05[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[AID]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>T05[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Host can use this command to send out the EMV application configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times but each command is only used for one application. A10-P will save those data internally and use those data during the transaction. A10-P will send message T06 (EMV Application Configuration Setup Response) to the host. For the data installed into A10-P via this message will be saved in the internal storage structure with a name same as in the [AID] field.
032. T06 - EMV Application Configuration Setup Response (PDF page 98)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T06[Resp][Reason][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The response message of message T05.
033. T07 - Data Format Table Setup (PDF page 99-100)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T07[Clear]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P will check the consistency of the TLV object from the terminal via messages T01 and T05. The terminal can add more TLV format checking rules into the A10-P. A10-P will send message T08 (Data Format Setup Response) to the host as the response.

     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T08[Resp][Reason][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The response message of message T07.
035. T09 - EMV Config Data Query Message (PDF page 102)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>T09[Config Type]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T0B[Config Type]<SUB>[ID List]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

039. T11 - Application Select (PDF page 106)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>T11<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P performs an application select on the active smart card. A10-P will prompt the user to insert its card if the card has not yet be engaged. A10-P will send message T12 (Application Selection Response) to host as a response.
040. T12 - Application Select Response (PDF page 107-108)
     Length: Variable, depending on the length of returned application name.

     Usage: The message contains the name of the final selected application on the smart card to be sent to the host. In general, the application name conforms to the EMV 4.3 level 2 specification. Refer to these standards for more detailed information.

The A10-P will prompt the user to arrange the appropriate entries when informed, like confirmation or enter the PIN code. A10-P will send message T16 (Start Transaction Response) to the host as a response.      Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T17[OnlineRes]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>T17[OnlineRes]<SUB>[ARC]<SUB>[IAD]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

063. T31 - Extract Information on Smart Card (non-EMV transactions) (PDF page 138)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>T31<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: PIN Pad performs the application selection, initiate application processing and read application data on the active smart card. All information will be stored in RAM temporarily but it is not retrievable until host sends out the message T3C to force the transaction declined or host sends out the message T35 to complete the transaction, and then the host will be able to get the information by message T21. PIN Pad will also prompt the user to insert a smart card if the card has not yet presented. PIN Pad will send the message T12 (Application Selection Response) to host.

Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages

     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T51[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Host can use this command to send terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times.      Format: Format not explicitly extracted - see detailed spec.
     Usage: In A10-P, Message T53 is as same as Message T03. They have the same format, but only Message ID is different. In other words, PCD CAPK and ICC CAPK are the same. Using Message T53 to setup CAPK will have the same result by using Message T03. For the detailed format and usage, please refer to Section 6 Message T03.

     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>T77<SUB>[PAN][<SUB>[PAN Seq. No.]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

Section 9 - Online Transaction Messages with Master/Session Keys (MK/SK)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
124. 70 - PIN entry request (MK/SK) (PDF page 255-258)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>70.[Account]<FS>[session key][Amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Display prompt to invite user to input PIN. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and send message 71. [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key. Notes: User Interactive Sequence: The prompts on the LCD of each phase are as following. After message 70 received Total Amount (The display language can be selected) $xxx.xx Enter PIN Push "ENTER" After user presses first digit PIN: (Each * represents one digit...
125. 71 - Encrypted PIN Block Response (MK/SK) (PDF page 258-260)
     Length: Fixed 27 bytes for TDES PIN block and 6 bytes for error code frame.
     Format: <STX>71.[fkey][PIN len][fmt][PIN blk][LRC] (response frame) <STX>71[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Send the entered PIN to the host in encrypted format.
126. 72 - PIN Entry Cancel (PDF page 261)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>72<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Cancel the current transaction that is waiting for user's input and return the A10-P to the IDLE state. The commands that can be canceled by message 72 include 70, Z60, Z62 (for both MK/SK and DUKPT), 60, 62, Z42, Z50, Q1, Q8, Q9, QK. If the A10-P receives message 72 while processing the user input such as swipe card, enter a PIN or keying in data, It will respond with <EOT> to acknowledge that the operation is canceled.
127. 7G - PIN Change Request (MK/SK) (PDF page 262-263)
     Length: Varible
     Format: <STX>7G.[Account]<FS>[session key][Amount] <FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC]
     Usage: Display prompt and accept customer PIN input for PIN change process. A10 will then wait till the PIN entered and [ENTER] key is pressed twice to make sure the both entered PIN are matched. After ENTER key is pressed, the string "PROCESSING" will be displayed until the CLEAR key is pressed. During this period, A10 will not process any message other than the CANCEL message (message 72).
128. Z60 - PIN entry request with external prompt (MK/SK) (PDF page 264-265)
     Length: Variable 48 to 77 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z60.[account]<FS>[session key]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message must be preceded by a display command (Z2 or Z3) with PIN entry authenticated prompt. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
129. Z62 - PIN entry request with customized prompt (MK/SK) (PDF page 266-267)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>Z62.[account]<FS>[session key][minPIN][maxPIN] [null flag][prompt1]<FS>[prompt2]<FS>[proc prompt]<FS> [timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message directs PIN pad to display "prompt1" and "prompt2" strings, and polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
130. Z64 - Query Key Check Value (KCV) (PDF page 268)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z64[KeyID]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message will export the KCV of the specified master key. KCV is calculated as following: 1. Use [KeyID] specified key as encryption key. 2. Use "0000000000000000" (8 bytes zero) as data. 3. If the encrypt key is single length (8 bytes), use TDES algorithm to encrypt the data. 4. Take leftmost 3 bytes as KCV, output KCV as message Z65.
131. Z65 - Key Check Value Response (PDF page 269)
     Length: Variable. 13 bytes for KCV, or 8 bytes for error code.
     Format: <STX>Z65[KeyID][KCV]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is the response of Z64. If [KeyID] specified in Z64 is pointing to a valid master key, the KCV will be sent. Otherwise a question mark '?' will be sent.
132. Z66 - Message Authentication Code (MAC) Request (PDF page 270-272)
     Length: Variable 14 to 270 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z66[PktType][SeqNo][KeyId]<FS>[SessionKey]<FS> [SecKeyId]<FS>[Message] <ETX> [LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to generate the MAC codes according to the algorithm specified in ANSI X9.19 (ISO 9797-1). User can send ASCII strings or hexadecimal strings to the A10-P by message Z66 to generate its MAC. User can also breakdown a long message into multiple Z66 messages with ascending sequence numbers to generate a MAC. Notes: Message Length: A onetime message that can be up to 224 characters (equal to 112 bytes when send as a hexadecimal string because 2 characters form 1 byte). Multiple messages can have sequence numbers from 00 to 99. Thus the maximum capacity of message Z66 is 22,400 characters (or 11,200 bytes in binary mode)....
133. Z67 - Message Authentication Code (MAC) Response (PDF page 273-275)
     Length: Fixed 7 (status only) or 23 (with MAC) bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z67[status][MAC]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The A10-P generated MAC response. It contains the status codes or MAC.

Section 10 - Online Transaction Messages with DUKPT
---------------------------------------------------
134. 60 - Pre-authorization PIN Entry Request (PDF page 276-277)
     Length: Variable 13 to 24 bytes.
     Format: <STX>60[account]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Message 60 and 62 forms the sequence of pre-authorization transaction (authorize before purchase amount decided.) This message must be preceded by a display command (Z2 or Z3) with PIN entry authenticated prompt. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
135. 62 - Pre-authorization Amount Authorization Request (PDF page 278)
     Length: Variable 7 to 15 bytes.
     Format: <STX>62[DC Ind][amount]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Display prompts and accept the customer PIN input. The following prompts will be displayed: "Total Amount $xxx.xx" "Enter - Confirm" "Cancel - Decline" xxx.x is the content of the amount field, with length between 4 to 8 positions. The A10-P will then wait until either the CAN or ENTER key is pressed. If the ENTER key is pressed, the A10-P will respond with a positive confirmation. If the CAN key is pressed, the A10-P will respond with a negative confirmation. During this period, the A10-P will not process any message other than the message 72 (cancel transaction).
136. 63 - Pre-authorization Amount Authorization Response (PDF page 279)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>63[Confirm] <ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Send the Authentication Code and confirms thetransaction amount to the host.
137. 70 - PIN Entry Request (DUKPT) (PDF page 280-281)
     Length: Variable 21 to 40 bytes.
     Format: <STX>70[account]<FS>[DC Ind][amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Display prompt to invite user to input PIN. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT> - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
138. 71 - Encrypted PIN Block Response (DUKPT) (PDF page 282-283)
     Length: Variable 32 to 42 bytes.
     Format: <STX>71<fkey flag>[Key Serial#][PIN][LRC] (response frame) <STX>71[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Send the entered PIN to the host in encrypted format.
139. 72 - PIN Entry Cancel (PDF page 284)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>72<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Cancel current transaction and return the A10-P to IDLE state. This message is used to interrupt the command in process. If A10-P receives message 72 while processing the user input such as swipe card, enter PIN or key-in data, it will respond with <EOT> to acknowledge that the operation is canceled.
140. Z60 - PIN entry request with external prompt (DUKPT) (PDF page 285-286)
     Length: Variable 15 to 28 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z60.[account]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message must be preceded by a display command (Z2 or Z3) with PIN entry authenticated prompt. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
141. Z62 - PIN entry request with customized prompt (DUKPT) (PDF page 287-288)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>Z62.[account]<FS>[minPIN][maxPIN][null flag] [prompt1]<FS>[prompt2]<FS>[proc prompt]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message directs PIN pad to display "prompt1" and "prompt2" strings, and polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71, and display [procPrompt]. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key..
142. 76 - PIN Entry Test Request (PDF page 289)
     Length: Variable 19 to 34 bytes.
     Format: <STX>76[account]<FS>[DC Ind][amount]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is designed to perform the continuous DUKPT PIN entry test. A10-P will generate the encrypted PIN block using specified account and default PIN: 1234.
143. 7A - KSN output format (PDF page 290)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>7A[KSN_format] <ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message sets the key serial number (KSN) format of message 71 (DUKPT frame). Format 0 is the original mode (strips leading 'F' of KSN) which is compatible with PP690, PP790SE and A10-P. Format 1 is full mode (output full 20 characters of KSN).
144. 90 - Load DUKPT Initial Key (Key Set 1) (PDF page 291-292)
     Length: Fixed 57 bytes for clear text format; 109 (format B) or 149 (format D) bytes for the TR-31 format .
     Format: <STX>90[IPEK][KSN]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear Text) <STX>90[TR-31 Key Block]<ETX>[LRC] (Encrypted)
     Usage: Load the first set of DUKPT initial key and serial number key to the A10-P. Consequent keys will be generated using the provided data. Clear text mode message 90 is only accepted when key injection mode is enabled by dual password authentication. Use it only in security-controlled environment with HSM. Refer to Appendix A Specification for detailed information. All existing keys in the A10-P will be erased when the first message 02 or 90 is sent in a new clear text key injection session.
145. 91 - Load Initial Key Response (PDF page 293)
     Length: Variable (max 7 bytes.)
     Format: <STX>91[Status][Error code]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Confirmation of the initial key loading. A10-P will show a message "IPEK n loaded" (n = 1 or 2) to confirm the successful loading of the initial key of set 1 or set 2 visually.
146. 94 - Load DUKPT Initial Key (Key Set 2) (PDF page 294-295)
     Length: Fixed 57 bytes for clear text format; 109 (format B) or 149 (format D) bytes for the TR-31 format.
     Format: <STX>94[IPEK][KSN]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear Text) <STX>94[TR-31 Key Block]<ETX>[LRC] (Encrypted)
     Usage: Load the second set of DUKPT initial key and serial number key to the A10-P. Consequent keys will be generated using the provided data.
147. 96 - Select Active Key Set (PDF page 296)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>96[keyset]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Select the active key set for the following transactions. This parameter will be saved and lasts until the next message 96 is received or the DUKPT life cycle ends.
148. 98 - Check DUKPT Keyset Status (PDF page 297)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>98[keyset][Key Info Query]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Check the status of the specified DUKPT keyset. Response message 99.
149. 99 - DUKPT Keyset Status Response (PDF page 298-299)
     Length: 6 or 15bytes.
     Format: <STX>99[status][usage]<FS>[mode]<FS>[algorithm]<FS> [KCV]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Response of the DUKPT keyset status.

Section 11 - Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages

150. Z0 - Move Display Cursor (PDF page 300)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.

This message cannot be used to abort PIN entry or data entry session, use message 72 in such situation.. This command also reset the magnetic card swiping commands Q1, Q8, Q9.

     Usage: This message directs PIN pad to display authenticated prompt string specified by ID number, for data entry command (Z42, Z50), or PIN entry (Z60, 60) until the following situations: - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad. - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1).

This message does not have <SUB> character because it will always clear the screen.

158. Z42 - Read Key Code (PDF page 318)
     Length: Variable 7 to 9 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z42[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Once A10-P receives this command, it begins polling the functional key array until time out happens as specified in [timeout]. If A10-P receives the Z2 / Z3 authenticated frame before message Z42, it will return any key pressed by the user as ASCII key codes via message Z43. Else it will return only the function key codes (F1, F2, F3, CAN, CLR, ENTER), and reject the numerical keys (0 to 9). Multiple key presses or combined key presses will be discarded. Abort input: Issue message 72 to abort the operation.
159. Z43 - Read Key Code Response (PDF page 319)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z43[Keycode]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This is the response frame of message Z42.
160. Z50 - String Entry Request (PDF page 320-322)
     Length: Variable 10 to 12 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z50[echo flag][timeout][max entry]<US><DI>[<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message requests a string of key inputs to be entered from the PIN pad. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of the following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT> - Times out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds).
161. Z51 - String Entry Response (PDF page 323)
     Length: Variable, maximum 55 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z51[string]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This is the response frame of message Z50.
162. Z7 - Turn ON/OFF CANCEL Message Display (PDF page 324)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z7[option]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: When a CANCEL message is received or a CANCEL key is pressed to cancel a current transaction, the A10-P will display the "TRANSACTION CANCELLED" message. This display could be turned ON or OFF using message Z7.
163. Z8 - Set Idle Prompt (PDF page 325)
     Length: Variable: 5 to 21 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z8[prompt]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The A10-P will display an idle prompt when it is in IDLE state. The host can change this idle prompt via message Z8. If the prompt field is filled with a null string, then the A10-P will use the default prompt after receiving this null string command.
164. Z9 - Turn ON/OFF LCD Backlight (optional) (PDF page 326-327)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Z9[option]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message can control the global backlight ON or OFF for the LCD of A10-P with backlight option. By default, A10-P will turn on its LCD backlight when it receives PIN entry or clear text entry message such as 70, and turns it off when those function exit.

Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
----------------------------------------------------------
165. I00 - Query Primary Smart Card Presence (PDF page 328)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes (request frame) / 7 bytes (response frame).
     Format: <STX>I00<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>I00[response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Upon receiving a query card packet, A10-P will check whether the card is present in the primary card reader or not. If a card exists in the reader, A10-P will reply with the code 'F'. Otherwise, the code '0' is used instead.
166. I01 - Primary Smart Card Cold Reset (PDF page 329)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I01<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P performs a cold reset on the active smart card. If the operation is successful, A10-P will send out message I02 with the "Answer to Reset" (ATR) of the smart card to the host. Otherwise, message I0F bearing the error code is sent back.
167. I02 - Primary Smart Card ATR Response (PDF page 330)
     Length: Variable, depending on the specification of the smart card..
     Format: <STX>I02[ATR]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The message contains the "Answer to Reset" (ATR) of the smart card to be sent to the host. In general, the ATR conforms to the ISO 7816-3 or EMV 4.3 Book 1 standard. See these standards for more detailed information.
168. I04 - Primary Smart Card Deactivate (PDF page 331)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I04<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Upon receiving the card deactivate packet, A10-P sets the active smart card into the deactivate state. If the operation is successful, A10-P will reply the same packet to confirm. Otherwise, message I0F with the error code will be sent.
169. I06 - Primary Smart Card C-APDU (PDF page 332)
     Length: Variable 14 to 530 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I06[C-APDU]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The C-APDU (application protocol data unit) is the data to be sent to the active smart card. A10-P 's smart card reader will handle with base protocols such as T=0 and T=1, and the programmer needs onlysending out the APDU. In general, A10-P will reply message I07 (response APDU from card) to the host in 1 second. For any error, A10-P will send back message I0F with an error code .
170. I07 - Primary Smart Card R-APDU (PDF page 333)
     Length: Variable 10 to 530 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I07[R-APDU]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: After the smart card processes the Command-APDU, it puts the result into the Response-APDU. A10-P packs the Response-APDU into this message packet and send it to the host.
171. I08 - Smart Card Offline PIN Verification (EMV) (PDF page 334-335)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear-text mode) <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<FS>RSA public Exp]<FS>[RSA public Modulus]<ETX>[LRC] (Cipher-text mode)
     Usage: User could apply message I01 ~ I06 to implement his EMV transaction flow. In EMV transaction flow, user could apply this message to implement the offline PIN verification operation defined by EMV Co. User applies this message to make PIN pad ask cardholder enter his PIN on PIN pad and then PIN pad will send the PIN block (in clear -text or cipher-text) to IC card. For secure consideration, user will not get any information about cardholder's PIN, user can only get the PIN verification result from PIN pad. In PIN verification operation, PIN pad will issue "Get Challenge" command to get random number from smart card for PIN encryption.
172. I09 - Response of Smart Card Offline PIN Verification (EMV) (PDF page 336)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I09[Response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: PIN pad will return the result of PIN verification operation. For EMV rule, it's recommended that terminal applies next CVM if get response equal to 'C', 'E', and 'S', terminates EMV transaction if get response equal to 'D' and 'F'.
173. I0F - Error Codes (PDF page 337)
     Length: Fixed 8 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I0F[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: This message contains the error code indicating what's going on with the erroneous situation. The error code list is as follows: "01" - ATR error or NO smart card. "02" - APDU data length is not enough. "03" - ICC/SAM card not powered yet, use I01 first. "04" - The alphanumeric value in the APDU data unit is out of range. "05" - Current smart card reader doesn't have card in. "06" - Smart card interface switch failed. "07" - A10-P Smart card module timed out. "08" - Smart card APDU command failed. "09" - This parameter is not supported by A10-P. "0A" - This unit does not have the corresponding peripheral (ICC reader or SAM).
174. I11 - SAM slot Cold Reset (PDF page 338)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I11<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P performs a cold reset on the active SAM interface. If the operation is successful, A10-P will sendmessage I12 with the "Answer to Reset" (ATR) of the smart card to the host. Otherwise, message I0F bearing the error code is sent back.
175. I12 - SAM slot ATR Response (PDF page 339)
     Length: Variable, depending on the specification of the smart card..
     Format: <STX>I12[ATR]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: The message contains the "Answer to Reset" (ATR) of the SAM card to be sent to the host. In general, the ATR conforms to the ISO 7816-3 or EMV 2000 level 1 standard. See these standards for more detailed information..
176. I14 - SAM slot Card Deactivate (PDF page 340)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I14<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Upon receiving the card deactivate packet, A10-P sets the active smart card into the deactivate state. If the operation is successful, A10-P will reply the same packet to confirm. Otherwise, message I0F with the error code will be sent.
177. I15 - SAM Select Interface (PDF page 341)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I15[IF_code]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P sets the active interface of the smart card reader. If the operation succeeds, A10-P will reply the same packet to confirm. Otherwise, message I0F with error code is sent. All SAM slot commands will be sent to the card via this active interface.
178. I16 - SAM slot C-APDU (PDF page 342)
     Length: Variable 14 to 530 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I16[C-APDU]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The C-APDU (application protocol data unit) is the data to be sent to the active smart card. A10-P 's SAM reader will handle with base protocols such as T=0 and T=1, and the programmer only needs sending out the APDU. In general, A10-P will reply message I17 (response APDU from card) to the host in 1 second. For any error, A10-P will send back message I0F with an error code.
179. I17 - SAM slot R-APDU (PDF page 343)
     Length: Variable 10 to 530 bytes.
     Format: <STX>I17[R-APDU]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: After SAM card processes the Command-APDU, it puts the result into the Response-APDU. A10-P packs the Response-APDU into this message packet and send it to the host.
180. Q1 - Start MSR Reading (PDF page 344)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q1<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The A10-P arms the MSR for read and displays the "SWIPE CARD" prompt on its LCD until a card is swiped through the reader slot, or message Z1 (reset state) is received, or message 72 is received, or the CAN key is pressed. After the magnetic stripe card is swiped, A10-P will collect and decode the card data and do formatting designated by message Q6. The data will be output to the host by message 81 and the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" message is displayed.
181. Q2 - Transaction Completed (PDF page 345)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q2<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Indicate that a transaction is completed. The A10-P displays a "Thank You" message for three seconds and then goes into the IDLE state.
182. Q3 - Ignore Card Swipe (PDF page 346)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q3<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The host should send this message Q3 after receiving the card data and decided not to accept another card temporarily. Upon receiving this message, the A10-P will display the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" prompt and ignore any card swipe.
183. Q4 - Enable/Disable Magnetic Card Reader (PDF page 347)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q4[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: All tracks are disabled by default (after each re-power on the A10-P). The host can use this message to enable or disable the magnetic card reader of the A10-P. Only track 2 is enabled if the [flag] field contains '0'. All tracks will be enabled if the [flag] field contains a '2'.
184. Q5 - Set MSR Retry Count (PDF page 348)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q5[RetryCount]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This command sets a retry count for the MSR swipe initiated by message Q1. If A10-P cannot decode any data from the latest swipe, the retry count is larger than "0", and the timeout has not reached yet, the A10-P will show "BAD READ" on the LCD and waits for the next swipe, until times out or the retry counter reaches the maximum. This setting will be kept in the battery powered memory and is effective all the time.
185. Q6 - Set MSR Data Output Format (PDF page 349)
     Length: 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q6.[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This command is used to set the MSR track data (message 81) output format.
186. Q7 - MSR Mode Query (PDF page 350-351)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes for request, 6 bytes for response.
     Format: <STX>Q7<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>Q7[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This command will query the MSR processing option.
187. Q8 - Start PCD Reading for Track Equivalent Data (PDF page 352)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q8<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The A10-P arms the PCD for contactless reading and display the "TAP CARD" prompt on its LCD until a contactless card is taped, the Z1 message (reset state) is received, or the CAN key is pressed. After the contactless card is tapped, the A10-P will output the MSR track equivalent data to the host by message 83.
188. Q9 - Start Dual Interface Reading (MSR and PCD) (PDF page 353)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>Q9<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: The A10-P arms both MSR and PCD, and displays the prompt "SWIPE / TAP CARD" on its LCD until a card is tapped or swiped through the reader slot, or message Z1 (reset state) is received,or the CAN key is pressed. If a magnetic card is swiped, A10-P will collect and decode the card data and do formatting designated by message Q6. The data will be output to the host by message 81 and display the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" message. If a contactless card is tapped, A10-P will output the MSR track equivalent data to the host by message 83 and display the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" message.
189. QA - Enable/Disable Contactless Card Reader (PDF page 354)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>QA[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: All the tracks are disabled by default (after each re-power on A10-P). The host can use this message to enable or disable the contact-less card reader of the A10-P. Only track 2 is enabled if the [flag] field contains '0'. Both tracks will be enabled if the [flag] field contains a '2'.
190. QB - Control MSR Auto Arm Mode (PDF page 355)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>QB[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: If the 'auto arm' is turned on, the A10-P will return the magnetic card data on each swipe under the idle mode (The terminal does not have to issue message Q1 for each card swipe). If this functionality is turned off, the terminal has to issue message Q1 to get the magnetic card data. Note. If the card tracks are all disabled (refer to message Q4), the terminal will always get the null magnetic card data.
191. QC - Control PCD Auto Arm Mode for Track Equivalent Data (PDF page 356)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>QC[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: If the 'auto arm' is turned on, the A10-P will return the contactless track equivalent data on each tap under the idle mode (the terminal does not have to issue message Q8/Q9 for each card tap). If this functionality is turned off, the terminal has to issue message Q8/Q9 to get the contactless card data. Note. If the card tracks are all disabled (refer to message QA), the terminal will always get the null contactless card data
192. QD - Set PCD Track Equivalent Data Output Format (PDF page 357)
     Length: Fixed 7 bytes.
     Format: <STX>QD.[flag]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This command sets the PCD track equivalent data (message 83) output format.
193. QF - Enable card swipe with JPEG (PDF page 358-359)
     Length: Fixed 7 to 22 bytes for request frame, and 6 bytes for response frame.
     Format: <STX>QF<FS>[JPEG filename]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>QF[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This command message function is the same as message Q1, but the PIN pad LCD can display specified JPEG file of message QF.
194. QG - Enable card tap with JPEG (PDF page 360-361)
     Length: Fixed 7 to 22 bytes for request frame, and 6 bytes for response frame.
     Format: <STX>QG<FS>[JPEG filename]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>QG[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This command message function is the same as message Q8, but the PIN pad LCD can display specified JPEG file of message QG.
195. QH - Enable card swipe/tap with JPEG (PDF page 362-363)
     Length: Fixed 7 to 22 bytes for request frame, and 6 bytes for response frame.
     Format: <STX>QH<FS>[JPEG filename]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>QH[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This command message function is the same as message Q9, but the PIN pad LCD can display specified JPEG file of message QH.
196. QI - Get Contactless Tag Data (PDF page 364-365)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>QI[control][DOL]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: A10-P will retrieve the data that listed on the DOL after the MSD data read. A10-P will send message QJ (Get Contactless Tag Data Response) to the host as a response.
197. QJ - Get Contactless Tag Data Response (PDF page 366-367)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>QJ[Pkt NO.][Total Pkt]<FS>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame) <STX>QJ[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame).
     Usage: The message contains the contactless tag data to be sent to the host as a response.
198. QK - Start Multiple Interface Detection (MSR, ICC, PCD) (PDF page 368-369)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes for request, 6 or 7 bytes for response.
     Format: <STX>QK<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>QK[Res][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This command will poll MSR/ICC/PCD, until detected, 72 message or Z1 message (reset state) received or CAN key pressed. If A10-P detects MSR/ICC/PCD, it will send the message to the host as a response. If Res is '1', then send message Q1 to read the track data. If Res is '2', then send message T11 to start an ICC EMV transaction. If Res is '3', then send message Q8 to read the track equivalent data or send message T61 to start a PCD EMV transaction.
199. 81 - MSR Card Data (PDF page 370-377)
     Length: Variable, depending on the card image in buffer.
     Format: <STX>81.[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<FS> [BIN record]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear text / encrypted data) <STX>81$[IV]<ETX>[LRC] (MK/SK Initial Vector) <STX>81#[KSN] <ETX>[LRC]...
     Usage: A10-P uses this message to send back the information read from the last card swipe. The card data is transmitted in ASCII string as defined by the ISO 7811 format specification. Under different types, the A10-P returns the card data in different formats. If message Q4 is issued and the A10-P is set as track 2 only, the returned message 81 will only contain track 2 data without a field separator. For PTS only firmware, the track data is always in clear text. For PTS + SRED firmware, the track data will be encrypted, except those PAN number listed in the BIN exception table. Refer to "account data security" for the obfuscation and encryption...
200. 83 - PCD Track Equivalence Data (PDF page 378-379)
     Length: Variable, depending on the card image in buffer.
     Format: <STX>83.[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear text / encrypted data) <STX>83$[IV]<ETX>[LRC] (MK/SK Initail Vector) <STX>83#[KSN] <ETX>[LRC] (DUKPT Key seria...
     Usage: Refer to message 81

Section 13 - Display Functionality Messages
-------------------------------------------
201. B1 - Font Size Selection (PDF page 380-381)
     Length: Fixed 6.
     Format: <STX>B1[Font Size]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>B2[Response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: A10-P supports 4 font sizes: 12, 16, 24, 30, 48, and 60 pixel height. Use this message can change the displayed font size. Please note that only low-page characters (<0x80) can be displayed, high-page characters should be encoded using UTF-8 code.
202. B3 - Font Color (Foreground / Backgroud) Selection (PDF page 382)
     Length: Fixed 17 bytes.
     Format: <STX>B3[Foreground][Background]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>B4[Response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Use this message to set the new colors of the font and background. The format is RR/GG/BB.
203. BB - Screen Saver Setting (PDF page 383-384)
     Length: Fixed 9 bytes.
     Format: <STX>BB[Waiting Time][Screen Saver Type]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>BC[Response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: A10-P has the screen saver functionality. This message is used to select one of screen savers and set the waiting time. Message BD is called to enable the screen saver. While A10-P is in idle (without receiving messages, keystrokes, or screen touch) passing the period of time specified in [Waiting Time], the screen saver will be activated. The minimum waiting time should be greater than or equal to 5 seconds. Screen saver - Jpeg Show: display all jpeg pictures in rotation (at least one JPEGimage should be loaded into the A10-P).Screen saver will be launched each time in rotation.
204. BD - Enable / Disable Screen Saver (PDF page 385)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>BD[Op]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>BE[Response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Use this message to enable / disable the screen saver.
205. BF - Screen Saver Preview / Stop Preview (PDF page 386-387)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>BF[Op]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Use this message to launch the screen saver directly or turns it off. User can also issue other messages to turn off the screen saver.

     Usage: This message is used to select or unselect the JPEG files from the terminal's display list.

     Length: Variable 6 to 540 bytes for the request frame, and variable 5 to 44 bytes for the response frame.
     Format: <STX>J3[FileName_1]<FS>[FileName_2]<FS>... [FileName_N-1]<FS>[FileName_N]<ETX>[LRC] (where the value of 'N' is the total number of the JPEG files) (request frame) <STX>J3[Status...
     Usage: This message is used to delete the JPEG files from the terminal's display list.

     Length: Variable 22 to 538 bytes for the request frame, and fixed 6 bytes for the response frame.

212. J6 - Play JPEG File (PDF page 400)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>J6<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to play the JPEG files that have been selected from the terminal. Those selected JPEG files will be displayed sequentially until an operation (pressing any key, or receiving message 72 or Z1) that changes the display.

     Length: Variable 6 ~ 20 bytes.
     Format: <STX>J7[Jpeg Name]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>J7[Result]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to set a JPEG file as the idle logo.

In order to successfully enable the customized idle logo, A JPEG file has to be loaded as the customized idle logo using message J4 and set by J7.
215. J9 - Show JPEG File (PDF page 403)
     Length: Variable 6 ~ 20 bytes.

     Length: Variable 22 to 538 bytes for the request frame, and fixed 6 bytes for the response frame.
     Format: <STX>JA[PktType][SeqNo]<FS>[Size][Data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>JA[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to download a bitmap file for boot logo from the terminal to the A10-P.

Section 15 - White List Configuration Messages
----------------------------------------------
217. ED - Load BIN Exception Table (PDF page 406-407)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>ED.[Signature data]<FS>[BIN Exception Table]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This message is used to load the BIN exception table (white list that excludes from encryption) to the reader. The reader will create a temporary buffer to collect all data, and then use the application public key to verify the signature. (Since the application public key is issued by the UIC, the acquirer needs to request UIC to sign the BIN exception table.) If verification succeeds, reader will replace the original BIN Exclusion Table; if verify failed, reader will abandon this data and return error code in the EE packet.
218. EE - BIN Exception Table Loading Response (PDF page 408)
     Length: Fixed 6 bytes.
     Format: <STX>EE[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is the response of message ED.
219. EF - Get Check Digits of BIN Exception Table (PDF page 409-413)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes for request / fixed 13 bytes for response.
     Format: <STX>EF<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>EF[status].[check digits]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: This message is used to get the "check digits" of the current white list. Check digits are the leftmost 3 bytes of BIN Exception Table's SHA 1 hash, represented in hexadecimal string.

Section 16 - Remote Key Loading Messages
----------------------------------------
220. R1 - Exchange Certificate Request (PDF page 414)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>R1[CER]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Initiate the certificate exchange by sending CERHOST, RKL to PIN pad. The certificate is RSA PKCS#7 enveloped PEM (data is base 64 encoded with the "-----BEGIN PKCS7-----" and "-----END PKCS7-----" marks). This command will initialize an "RKL session". During RKL session, only R series command and "72" command can be accepted by PIN pad.
221. R2 - Exchange Certificate Request Response (PDF page 415-416)
     Length: 125 bytes.
     Format: <STX>R2[TP][LRC] (response frame) <STX>R2[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Response of message R1
222. R3 - PIN Pad Certificate Request (PDF page 417)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>R3<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Get the CERPINPad, RKL from PIN pad. This command must be issued in RKL session.
223. R4 - PIN Pad Certificate Response (PDF page 418)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>R4[RA][CERPIN Pad][LRC] (response frame) <STX>R4[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Response of message R3
224. R5 - Remote Key Loading Request (PDF page 419-421)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>R5[Key ID][Signed data][LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Send Remote Key Loading request with validation information. This command must be issued in RKL session..
225. R6 - Remote Key Loading Response (PDF page 422-424)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>R6[Signed data][LRC] (response frame) <STX>R6[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
     Usage: Response of message R5
226. R7 - Remote Key Loading Complete (PDF page 425)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>R7<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: Indicate the remote key loading process is complete. This command ends the RKL session.
227. R8 - Remote Key Loading Complete Response (PDF page 426)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>R8[status][LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Response of message R7
228. R9 - Load CA Certificate Request for RKL Verification (PDF page 427)
     Length: Variable.
     Format: <STX>R9.[CER data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
     Usage: This command loads CERHOST, intermediate to PIN pad for later RKL request usage. The certificate is RSA PKCS#7 enveloped PEM (data is base 64 encoded with the "-----BEGIN PKCS7-----" and "-----END PKCS7-----" marks). This command does not need to be in RKL session.
229. RA - Load Certificate Request for RKL Verification Response (PDF page 428)
     Length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Format: <STX>RA[status][LRC] (response frame)
     Usage: Response of message R9
