[001] COMMAND 02 - Load Master Key (Clear Text)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 35-38
Format summary: <SI>02[Key ID][Key value]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)
Message length: Variable (22 to 58 bytes).
Purpose/usage summary: Send the key value to the A10-P and save into designated master key slot. A10-P can store 21 master keys (A10-P application only uses 16 of them for backword compatibility); each with a one digit ID. These Master keys are divided into three groups of different functions. Refer to Appendix A for key usage and ID definition. Clear text key injection is only accepted in the "Key Injection" session of the system manager; which is enabled by dual-password authentication. This function should be used only in security-controlled environment with HSM. Refer to Appendix A for detailed information. The algorithm of the injected key is defined by the...

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 02 - Load Master Key (Clear Text)
    Format:           <SI>02[Key ID][Key value]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
                      <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)

    Message length: Variable (22 to 58 bytes).
    Usage:            Send the key value to the A10-P and save into designated master key slot. A10-P can
                      store 21 master keys (A10-P application only uses 16 of them for backword
                      compatibility); each with a one digit ID. These Master keys are divided into three
                      groups of different functions. Refer to Appendix A for key usage and ID definition.

                      Clear text key injection is only accepted in the "Key Injection" session of the system
                      manager; which is enabled by dual-password authentication. This function should be
                      used only in security-controlled environment with HSM. Refer to Appendix A for
                      detailed information.
                      The algorithm of the injected key is defined by the key management scheme, if the
                      usage and mode are not designated. A10-P will apply default value for them. Refer to
                      Appendix A for detailed information.
                      Change key management scheme will erase all existing keys in the A10-P.
                      All existing keys in the A10-P will be erased when the first message 02 or 90 is sent in
                      a new key injection session.
    Compatibility:    The user of UIC PP790SE and PP791 shoud note:
                      1. The "key transport key" usage is changed to "K1" instead of "K0" in accordance to
                      the new ANSI TR-31: 2018 standard.

    Message element:
                                          Request fame (HOST to A10-P)
                        Field           Length                 Value and description

                   <SI>               1             <0F>
                   02                 2             Message ID
                   [Key ID]           1             ['0' to '9', 'B' to 'G']
                   [Key value]        16 or 32      Hexadecimal string for key value.
                                      or 48         In DES scheme, 16 characters (single length) .
                                                    In TDES scheme, 32 characters (double
                                                    length) or 48 characters (triple length) keys
                                                    are allowed.
                           <FS>       1             Field separator.
                                                    (Optional, only available in clear text format
                                                    frame if the following [Usage] and [Mode]
                                                    exist)
                   [Usage]            2             (Optional: ANSI TR-31 key usage for clear
                                                    text frame.)
                                                    Available values are:
                                                    "K0" for key encryption. (id 0 ~ 9, B ~ G)
                                                    "K1" for key transport key. (id F)
                                                    "P0" for PIN encryption. (id 0 ~ 9)
                                                    "M3" for MAC calculation. (id B ~ E)
                                                    "M1" for MAC calculation. (id B ~ E)
                                                    "D0" for data encryption. (id G)
                   [Mode]             1             (Optional: ANSI TR-31 key mode for clear
                                                    text frame.)
                                                    Available values are:
                                                    'D' for decryption only. (K0 / K1 keys)
                                                    'E' for encryption only (P0 / D0 keys)
                                                    'G' for MAC generation only (M1 / M3 keys)
                                                    'V' for MAC verification only (M3 keys)
                   <SO>               1             <0E>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                              Response fame - Error message (A10-P to HOST)
                        Field           Length                 Value and description

                   <SI>               1             <0F>
                   02                 2             Message ID

                   ?                1
                   [Err msg]        1             '2': Key duplicated with existing keys.
                                                  '3': Internal fail: fail to allocate memory.
                                                  '4': Internal fail: fail to read key structure.
                                                  'E': Incompatible key usage.
                                                  'F': Key injecton operating limit reached.
                   <SO>             1             <0E>
                   [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                    Message 02 (request
                                                     ->
                    frame)
                                                     <-       <ACK> /<NAK>/<EOT>
                                                             Processing request.
                                                             If format error, send <EOT> and
                                                             end.
                                                     <-
                                                             If format and MAC correct, send
                                                             Message 02 (echo of request
                                                             frame).
                    Verify echo frame.
                    If verify ok, send
                    <ACK>.
                    If packet LRC error, send
                                                     ->
                    <NAK>.
                    If the host wants to
                    cancel the key loading
                    procedure, send <EOT>.
                                                             Save the key value and send
                                                     <-
                                                             <EOT>
```

[002] COMMAND 02 - Load Master Key (TR-31 Bundle)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 39-40
Format summary: <SI>02[Key ID][TR-31 Key Bundle]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Send the encrypted and MACed key bundle (ANSI TR-31: 2018 format) to the A10-P and save into the designated master key slot. A10-P will use the key transport key (key slot #F) to validate and decrypt the key bundle. If key management scheme is set to TDES, A10-P will use TDES algorithm to do validation and decryption.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 02 - Load Master Key (TR-31 Bundle)
    Format:               <SI>02[Key ID][TR-31 Key Bundle]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
                          <SI>02?[error code]<SO>[LRC] (error frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:                Send the encrypted and MACed key bundle (ANSI TR-31: 2018 format) to the A10-P
                          and save into the designated master key slot.
                          A10-P will use the key transport key (key slot #F) to validate and decrypt the key
                          bundle.    If key management scheme is set to TDES, A10-P will use TDES algorithm
                          to do validation and decryption.

    Compatibility:        The users of UIC PP790SE and PP791 shoud note:
                          1. TR-31 Bundle single DES keys are no longer supported due to the evolution of the
                          PCI security standards.
                          2. The "key transport key" usage is changed to "K1" instead of "K0" in accordance to
                          the new ANSI TR-31: 2018 standard.

    Message element:
                                            Request fame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field          Length                 Value and description

                     <SI>               1             <0F>
                     02                 2             Message ID
                     [Key ID]           1             ['0' to '9', 'B' to 'G']
                     [TR-31 Key         Var.          ANSI TR-31: 2018 key bundle. Refer to
                     Bundle]                          Appendix A for detailed information.
                     <SO>               1             <0E>
                     [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                Response fame - Error message (A10-P to HOST)
                           Field          Length                 Value and description

                     <SI>               1             <0F>
                     02                 2             Message ID
                     ?                  1
                     [Err msg]          1             '2': Key duplicate.
                                                      '3': Internal fail: fail to allocate memory.
                                                      '4': Internal fail: fail to read key structure.
                                                      '7': Fail to decrypt the key value.
                                                      'A': TR31 format error.
                                                      'B': Insecure key inject. (New key is longer

                                                   than the key used to protect it.)
                                                   'C': Fail to verify the MAC value.
                                                   'D': KLK does not exist.
                                                   'E': Incompatible key usage.
                                                   'F': Key injecton operating limit reached.
                                                   'Z': Fatal Error.
                    <SO>              1            <0E>
                    [LRC]             1            Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST                 Direction                      A10-P

               Message 02 (request frame)           ->
                                                    <-         <ACK> /<NAK>/<EOT>
                                                              Processing request.
                                                              If format error, send <EOT> and end.
                                                    <-
                                                              If format and MAC correct, send
                                                              Message 02 (echo of request frame).
               Verify echo frame.
               If verify ok, send <ACK>.
               If packet LRC error, send
               <NAK>.                               ->
               If the host wants to cancel the
               key loading procedure, send
               <EOT>.
                                                    <-         Save the key value and send <EOT>
    Example:
    Refer to Appendix A for the detailed example of the TDES generation.
    TDES TR-31 Examples
```

[003] COMMAND 04 - Check Master Key
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 41-42
Format summary: <SI>04[key ID][get attr]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>04[response code][attr]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable (6 or 7) bytes for request frame. Variable (6 or 22) bytes for response frame.
Purpose/usage summary: Check if the specified master key exists, and optionally get its TR31 attributes.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 04 - Check Master Key
    Format:                <SI>04[key ID][get attr]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
                           <SI>04[response code][attr]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable (6 or 7) bytes for request frame.
                           Variable (6 or 22) bytes for response frame.
    Usage:                 Check if the specified master key exists, and optionally get its TR31 attributes.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                            Field           Length                Value and description

                  <SI>                     1            <0F>
                  04                       2            Message ID
                  [key ID]                 1            Master key ID   (0 to 9, B to G)
                  [get attr]               1            <Option>, 1: query key information
                  <SO>                     1            <0E>
                  [LRC]                    1            Checksum

                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                            Field              Length              Value and description

                  <SI>                     1             <0F>
                  04                       2             Message ID
                  [response code]          1             0 Master key not loaded
                                                         F Master key loaded
                  [attr]                   6             2bytes key usage +
                                                         <FS> +
                                                         1byte Mode of use +
                                                         <FS> +
                                                         1byte Algorithm
                  <SO>                     1             <0E>
                  [LRC]                    1             Checksum

Message flow:
                           HOST               Direction                A10-P

                  Message 04 (request)            ->
                                                          <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                  <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                          <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                          Check requested   key slot
                                                  <-
                                                          Message 04 (response)
                  <ACK> (Good echo)
                  <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                  <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                  <-       <EOT>
```

[004] COMMAND 05 - Load Serial Number
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 43
Format summary: <SI>05[string]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Load the A10-P with the serial number given in the message frame. The A10-P will send the whole message frame back to the host as a confirmation of good reception. If the LRC is good but the echoed serial number is incorrect the host should then send an <ACK> to confirm or an <EOT> to cancel this serial number loading process. Follow the standard <NAK> process if an invalid LRC is detected.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 05 - Load Serial Number
    Format:              <SI>05[string]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length:        Variable.
    Usage:               Load the A10-P with the serial number given in the message frame. The A10-P will
                         send the whole message frame back to the host as a confirmation of good reception. If
                         the LRC is good but the echoed serial number is incorrect the host should then send
                         an <ACK> to confirm or an <EOT> to cancel this serial number loading process.
                         Follow the standard <NAK> process if an invalid LRC is detected.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field          Length                Value and description

                  <SI>                   1             <0F>
                  05                     2             Message ID
                  [string]               0 to 16       Alphanumeric string (0~9, A~Z, a~z)
                  <SO>                   1             <0E>
                  [LRC]                  1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                             HOST                  Direction                   A10-P

                  Message 05                          ->
                                                               <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                      <-        <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                               <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                               Message 05 (echo frame) or <EOT>
                                                      <-
                                                               indicating error.
                  <ACK> (Good echo)
                  <NAK> (Bad LRC)                     ->
                  <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                               (Stores serial number)
                                                      <-
                                                               <EOT>
```

[007] COMMAND 08 - Select Active Master Key
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 47
Format summary: <SI>08[KeyID]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to select an "active" master key from one of the 10 possible PIN encrypting master keys previously loaded using message 02. The active master key will be used in the following transactions.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 08 - Select Active Master Key
    Format:           <SI>08[KeyID]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
    Usage:            This message is used to select an "active" master key from one of the 10 possible PIN
                      encrypting master keys previously loaded using message 02. The active master key
                      will be used in the following transactions.
    Note:             Confirm the key existence before issuing 08: message 08 is not responsible to
                      check if [KeyID] has a valid master key. Use message 04 before message 08.
    Message element:
                                        Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                            Field         Length             Value and description

                     <SI>               1             <0F>
                     08                 2             Message ID
                     [KeyID]            1             0~9, one of Master key id.
                     <SO>               1             <0E>
                     [LRC]              1             Checksum
    Message flow (compatible with UIC PP791 BV2 for A10-P BV2/VEL):
                             HOST               Direction                    A10-P

                   Message 08                       ->
                                                    <-        <ACK>/<NAK>/<EOT>
                                                             Success:
                                                             <SI>080<SO>
                                                    <-        Fail:
                                                             <SI>081<SO>
                                                             Key index > 9
                   <ACK> (Good echo)
                   <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
                   <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-        <EOT>
    Message flow (compatible with UIC PP79SE BVA for A10-P BVP):
                             HOST               Direction                    A10-P

                   Message 08                       ->
                                                    <-        <ACK>/<NAK>/<EOT>
                                                               Set active master key.
                                                    <-        If key ID error, error message will
                                                             be displayed.
                                                    <-        <EOT>
```

[008] COMMAND 09 - Communication Test
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 48-49
Format summary: <SI>09<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>09<SUB>PROCESSING<SO>[LRC] (response frame) <SI>09[response code][LRC] (Result frame)
Message length: Fixed 5 bytes for the requesting message, fixed 16 bytes for the response message.
Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to test communication link between the host and the A10-P. Both host and A10-P can initiate a communication test. The initiating party should send the requesting message; the other party should respond with the response message that should be ACKed if received correctly. After verifying that the response message is correct, the initiating party should send back the same response message and the receiving party should acknowledge this message. The test results are shown on the A10-P display.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 09 - Communication Test
    Format:             <SI>09<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
                        <SI>09<SUB>PROCESSING<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
                        <SI>09[response code][LRC] (Result frame)

    Message length: Fixed 5 bytes for the requesting message, fixed 16 bytes for the response message.
    Usage:              This message is used to test communication link between the host and the A10-P.
                        Both host and A10-P can initiate a communication test. The initiating party should send
                        the requesting message; the other party should respond with the response message
                        that should be ACKed if received correctly. After verifying that the response message
                        is correct, the initiating party should send back the same response message and the
                        receiving party should acknowledge this message. The test results are shown on the
                        A10-P display.
    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <SI>              1             <0F>
                   09                2             Message ID
                   <SO>              1             <0E>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

                                       Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <SI>              1             <0F>
                   09                2             Message ID
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   [Test string]     10            ASCII string "PROCESSING"
                   <SO>              1             <0E>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

                                          Result frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <SI>              1             <0F>
                   09                2             Message ID
                   [response         1             '0': Test Success
                   code]                           'F': Test Failed.
                   <SO>              1             <0E>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message 09 (request)           ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message 09 (response frame)
                    <ACK> (Good echo)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    Message 09 (response)          ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message 09 (result frame)
                    <ACK> (Good echo)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       <EOT>
```

Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to select the A10-P prompt message table for different languages. The English prompt table is resident as default and its index number is '0'. Other prompts can be updated and selected and the A10-P will select the corresponding code page for display. NOTE. The order of the supported language may be different from this manual as the prompt message module changes. Refer to the response from A10-P through message 1F.

```text
                        languages. The English prompt table is resident as default and its index number is '0'.
                        Other prompts can be updated and selected and the A10-P will select the
                        corresponding code page for display.
    NOTE.               The order of the supported language may be different from this manual as the prompt
                        message module changes. Refer to the response from A10-P through message 1F.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field           Length                Value and description

                   <SI>                1             <0F>
                   12                  2             Message ID
                   [language           1             Language code
                   index]                            '0': English (default)
                                                     '1': Spanish
                   <SO>                1             <0E>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

                         Field           Length                Value and description

                   <SI>                1             <0F>
                   12                  2             Message ID
                   [status]            1             Status:
                                                     '0': Success
                                                     'F': prompt index value error.
                   <SO>                1             <0E>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum
```

[011] COMMAND 13 - Adjust COM1 Baud Rate (RS-232 version only)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 5 - Administration and Maintenance Messages
Source PDF page(s): 53-54
Format summary: <SI>13[baud code][mode]<SO>[LRC] (request frame) <SI>13[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable, 6~7 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message will change the communication baud rate and transmit mode of the A10-P for later operations. The setting is kept in the non-volatile memory. The baud rate will be changed after the message flow ends.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 13 - Adjust COM1 Baud Rate (RS-232 version only)
    Format:              <SI>13[baud code][mode]<SO>[LRC] (request frame)
                         <SI>13[status]<SO>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable, 6~7 bytes.
    Usage:               This message will change the communication baud rate and transmit mode of the
                         A10-P for later operations. The setting is kept in the non-volatile memory. The baud
                         rate will be changed after the message flow ends.
    Note:                If the [mode] parameter is not specified, the default transmit mode is N, 8, 1.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                             Field             Length              Value and description

                    <SI>                      1             <0F>
                    13                        2             Message ID
                    [baud code]               1             ASCII character
                                                            '1' = 1200bps
                                                            '2' = 2400bps
                                                            '3' = 4800bps
                                                            '4' = 9600bps
                                                            '5' = 19200bps
                                                            '6' = 38400bps
                                                            '7' = 57600bps
                                                            '8' = 115200bps
                    [Transmit mode]           1             ASCII character
                    (optional)                              '1' = None parity, 8-bit, 1 stop bit
                                                            '2' = Even parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit
                                                            '3' = Odd parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit

                                                            0x41 = None parity, 8-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                            with XON-XOFF flow control
                                                            0x42 = Even parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                            with XON-XOFF flow control
                                                            0x43 = Odd parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                            with XON-XOFF flow control

                                                            0x81 = None parity, 8-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                            with RTS flow control
                                                            0x82 = Even parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,

                                                              with RTS flow control
                                                              0x83 = Odd parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                              with RTS flow control

                                                              0xC1 = None parity, 8-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                              with RTS/XON-XOFF flow control
                                                              0xC2 = Even parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                              with RTS/XON-XOFF flow control
                                                              0xC3 = Odd parity, 7-bit, 1 stop bit,
                                                              with RTS/XON-XOFF flow control
                    <SO>                        1             <0E>
                    [LRC]                       1             Checksum

                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                               Field             Length              Value and description

                    <SI>                        1             <0F>
                    13                          2             Message ID
                    [status]                    1             ASCII character
                                                              '0' for success
                                                              '1' for parameter error
                    <SO>                        1             <0E>
                    [LRC]                       1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                                  HOST                Direction                  A10-P

                      Message 13 (request)                ->
                                                                     <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                          <-          <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                     <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                          <-          Message 13 (response)
                      <ACK> (Good LRC)
                      <NAK> (Bad LRC)                     ->
                      <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                          <-          <EOT>
                                                                     (Change the communication
                                                                     baud rate and save the
                                                                     setting)
```

```text
Section 6           Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
EMV Level2 transaction messages are divided into 2 groups. One group are the EMV-configuration data
operation messages (T01, T03, T05, T07, T09, T0B) and the other group are the EMV-transaction messages
(T11, T13, T15, T17, T19, T1C, T21, T25, T27, T29).

The issuing sequence of the ICC EMV transaction messages is controlled by the A10-P.                An invalid
sequence will terminate that ICC EMV transaction. In the beginning of an ICC EMV transaction, the user has
to issue message T11 to make the A10-P to negotiate with the card and generate a candidate list of
EMV-applications that are supported both by the A10-P and the card.       It will then automatically select the
application with the highest priority or the one selected by the user (according to the terminal configuration
data installed in the A10-P), and then return the EMV-application name. Message T15 is used for the
terminal-side to transmit transaction information such as the amount to be used by the A10-P to complete the
transaction with the card if the transaction does not need to be authorized online. The terminal can issue
message T1D to transmit additional transaction data to the A10-P for ICC EMV transaction.       Examples are
online response data and magnetic stripe card track data. Message T17 is applied if the transaction needs to
be authorized online. The terminal-side will transmit necessary information via this message to the A10-P to
complete the rest of transactional steps. If the response from the host contains issuer script (see EMV), the
terminal-side will issue message T19 to send these scripts into the A10-P. Then the A10-P will issue these
scripts at appropriate time to the card. Message T1C is used to terminate an ICC EMV transaction. Finally,
message T21 is used for terminal-side to get the transaction information throughout the EMV transaction.

The terminal can apply the same set of Txx messages for handling a complete ICC EMV transaction but for
turning out the transaction must be changed to magnetic stripe card processing. According to EMV rule, if the
terminal fails to read the IC card, the transaction could be switched to the magnetic stripe card transaction.
Because of the different types of magnetic stripe cards, the magnetic stripe card processing should be taken
by the terminal. The terminal can issue message Q1 provided by the A10-P to let the user to swipe his card
and then issue message 70 to complete a magnetic stripe card transaction. In this situation, the terminal will
get the T11 response message that indicates a failed IC card read. The terminal should then issue message
T1D, T15 and T17 to the A10-P for batch data capture. The flow chart for changing to magnetic stripe card
processing can be found in the "Overall Contact EMV level 2 transaction flow reference" section.

The meanings of the error codes in the [Err Message] are listed below:
    Error Code                                                Error Description
```

[027] COMMAND T01 - Terminal Configuration Setup
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 85-87
Format summary: <STX>T01[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Host can use this command to send the terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times. The A10-P will save those data internally and utilize them during the transaction. The A10-P will send message T02 (Terminal Configuration Setup Response) to the host as a response. The functions of Message T01 and Message T51 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T01 - Terminal Configuration Setup
    Format:               <STX>T01[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:                Host can use this command to send the terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This
                          command can be sent many times. The A10-P will save those data internally and
                          utilize them during the transaction. The A10-P will send message T02 (Terminal
                          Configuration Setup Response) to the host as a response. The functions of Message
                          T01 and Message T51 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.

    Message element:
                                            Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field          Length                 Value and description

                     <STX>              1             <02>
                     T01                3             Message ID
                     Pkt No.            1             Decimal. Packet sequence number (1 ~ 9) (ex.
                                                      2)
                     Total Pkts         1             Decimal. Total packets (1 ~ 9) (ex. 8).
                     <SUB>              1             <1A>
                     DO                 Var.          Data Object, format as below
                     <ETX>              1             <03>
                     [LRC]              1             Checksum
    Data Object Format: each data object is delimited by <SUB>, and each field inside each data
    object is delimited by <FS>.

    Data Format: (Please also refer to EMV 4.3 BOOK3, section 4.3)
  Format                                                      Description
     1       a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
     2       b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
     3       an - Alphanumeric data      (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
     4       ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
     5       cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
     6       n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
     7       var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

   Note. User has to follow the restriction specified in the EMV 4.3 BOOK3, Annex A and Appendix C
           of this document to load the configuration data. The A10-P will check if the length of each
           configuration data item is consistent. Any inconsistent data item will make the data loading
           fail.

    Note. If the data format is '2' (binary), '5' (compressed numeric), '6' (numeric) or '7'(variable data),
           it cannot be allocated in message T01 directly. It should be transferred into a hexadecimal
           string and then allocated in message T01.

    Example: (Clear the terminal configuration data and then setup the new data.)
    Merchant Category Code: 0000 (Numerical)
    Terminal ID:           SmartPOS (Ascii)
    UI Capability:         0x01 (binary)

    <STX>T0111<SUB>9f15<FS>6<FS>0000<SUB>9f1c<FS>3<FS>SmartPOS<SUB>
    FFFF8101<FS>2<FS>01<ETX>[LRC]

    Special Tag for A10-P: 0xFFFF8101, 0xFFFF81013
            Name                             Description                        Format        Tag            Length
      Terminal UI          0: Make A10-P selects the highest priority             b      FFFF8101        1
      Capability           application and ask for the user's confirmation.
                           1: Make A10-P provides a list of candidate
                           applications.
      MSR Processing       A10-P will store transaction data according to         b      FFFF81013       var
      Batch Tag List       the tag list while the transaction is performed as
                           MSR processing. Ex, for tag list (829F365F3
                           09F399F029F03), the A10-P will store the
                           transaction data of tag numbers 0x82, 0x9F36,
                           0x5F30, 0x9F39, 0x9F02 and 0x9F03.
    These data objects are defined in EMV 4.3 BOOK3, Annex A without tag values. The tag values are
    defined by UIC.

    The A10-P will check if the terminal downloads the minimum set of terminal-related information
    into itself. The download process will fail if there is not enough data in this message. Please refer
    to Appendix D for the minimum set of terminal-related data

    Message flow:
                              HOST             Direction                A10-P

                    1st Message T01                ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       1st Message T02
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    2nd Message T01                ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       2nd Message T02
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    ...                              ...       ...
                    Last one Message T01           ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Last one Message T02
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text

    Format:           Plain Text (Key Format: 1)
                      <STX>T03[Op code][RID][PKI][Hash Algo][Hash][PK Algo]
                      [PK Leng] [PK Exponent]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                      <STX>T03[Op code][PK Modulus]<ETX> (request frame)

    Format:           Certificate (Key Format: 2(PEM) or 3(DER))
                      <STX>T03[PktType][SeqNo]<SUB>[RID][PKI]<FS>[Cert]<ETX>[LRC]
                      (request frame)
                      <STX>T03[PktType][SeqNo]<SUB>[Cert]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            Host can use this command to send the Certification Authority Public key data to the
                      A10-P. Each command can only setup one key but this command can be sent many
                      times. The A10-P will save those key data inside and use those data during the
                      transaction. A10-P will send message T04 (Certification Authority Public Key Setup
                      Response) to the host. The data is installed into the A10-P via this message and it will
                      then be saved into its internal storage structure with a name as the concatenation of
                      the values in the [RID] and [PKI] fields. For example, the value in the [RID] field is
                      "A000000003" and the value in the [PKI] field is "90", then the A10-P will save these
                      data and give an ID as "A00000000390". The functions of Message T03 and Message
                      T53 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.
    Key Format:       There are three types of key format. '1' is plain text format, which is [RID][PKI][Hash
                      Algo][Hash][PK Algo][PK Leng][PK Exponent][PK Modulus]. '2' is PEM certificate
                      format, which is [RID][PKI][PEM certificate]. '3' is DER certificate format, which is
                      [RID][PKI][DER certificate with HEX String format].

    Message element:
    1st Packet (Plain Text Public Key):
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T03               3             Message ID

                   [RID]             10            Hexadecimal string, the left 5 bytes of
                                                   Registered Application Provider ID
                   [PKI]             2             Public Key Index, hexadecimal string. (Refer
                                                   to EMV 4.3, tag '9F22')
                   [Hash             2             Hash Algorithm Index, hexadecimal string
                   Algorithm]                      '01': SHA-1. Now, A10-P accepts only '01'.
                   [Hash]            40            Hash checksum, hexadecimal

                   [PK               2             Public Key Algorithm, hexadecimal string
                   Algorithm]                      '01': RSA digital signature. Now, A10-P only
                                                   accepts '01'.
                   [PK Leng]         2             Public Key Modulus length, hexadecimal
                                                   string, for example:
                                                   '80' = 128 bytes = 1024 bits
                   [PK Exponent]     1             Public Key Exponent
                                                   '1': 3
                                                   '2': 216+1
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    2nd Packet (Plain Text Public Key):
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T03               3             Message ID
                   [Op code]         1             2: Load second part of RSA public key
                   [PK Modulus]      Var           Public    Key       Modulus,    presented       in
                                                   hexadecimal, data length = 2*[PK Leng bytes]
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    PEM certificate:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T03               3             Message ID
                   [PktType]         1             '0': Initial or middle packet of CA public
                                                   keys.
                                                   '1': Single or last packet of CA public keys.
                   [SeqNo]           1             The packet sequence number, starting from
                                                   '0'.
                   <SUB>             1             <1A> as delimiter
                   [RID]             10            Hexadecimal string, the left 5 bytes of
                                                   Registered Application Provider ID
                   [PKI]             2             Public Key Index, hexadecimal string. (Refer
                                                   to EMV 4.3, tag '9F22')
                   <FS>              1             <1C> as delimiter
                   [certificate]     Var.          Base64 encoded string.
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    DER certificate:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field         Length                Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    T03               3             Message ID
                    [PktType]         1             '4': Initial or middle packet of CA public
                                                    keys.
                                                    '5': Single or last packet of CA public keys.
                    [SeqNo]           1             The packet sequence number, starting from
                                                    '0'.
                    <SUB>             1             <1A> as delimiter
                    [RID]             10            Hexadecimal string, the left 5 bytes of
                                                    Registered Application Provider ID
                    [PKI]             2             Public Key Index, hexadecimal string. (Refer
                                                    to EMV 4.3, tag '9F22')
                    <FS>              1             <1C> as delimiter
                    [certificate]     Var.          DER certificate content with Base64 encoded
                                                    string format.
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum
    Message flow:

                    2nd Message T03                  ->

                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
```

[033] COMMAND T07 - Data Format Table Setup
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 99-100
Format summary: <STX>T07[Clear]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: A10-P will check the consistency of the TLV object from the terminal via messages T01 and T05. The terminal can add more TLV format checking rules into the A10-P. A10-P will send message T08 (Data Format Setup Response) to the host as the response.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T07 - Data Format Table Setup
    Format:             <STX>T07[Clear]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:              A10-P will check the consistency of the TLV object from the terminal via messages
                        T01 and T05. The terminal can add more TLV format checking rules into the A10-P.
                        A10-P will send message T08 (Data Format Setup Response) to the host as the
                        response.

    Message element:
                                            Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field          Length                   Value and description

                     <STX>              1             <02>
                     T07                3             Message ID
                     [Clear]            1             '1': Clear existing Data Format file
                     <SUB>              1             <1A>, Optional, only if [DO] exist
                     [DO]               Var.          Data Object, format as below
                     <ETX>              1             <03>
                     [LRC]              1             Checksum

    Format of Data Objects:
     The Data Objects for T07 shall include five data fields delimited by <FS>: [Tag#] <FS> [Format] [Min
    Len] [Max Len] [Flag]. Each data object is delimited by a <SUB> to construct multiple <DO>s. If the [Flag]
    is '0', the data object will accept the length of value within [Min Len] and [Max Len]; if the [Flag] is '1', the
    data object will only accept either the [Min Len] or [Max Len] as valid length.

    Example: (setup new data format.)

              Tag          Data Format         Min Len Max Len Or Flag

              5F88                 4             02           1A     0 (data length is 2 ~ 26 bytes)

              5F99                 2             08           0B     1 (data length is 8 bytes or 11 bytes)

    <STX>T071<SUB>5F88<FS>4021A0<SUB>5F99<FS>2080B1<ETX>[LRC]

    In this example, A10-P will check if the length of data with tag value 5F99 is 8-byte or 11-byte. It will
    check if the length of data with tag value 5F88 is more than 1-byte and less than 27-byte.

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction               A10-P

                    Message T07                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message T08
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[038] COMMAND T0C - Response of Delete EMV Configuration Data Message.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 105
Format summary: <STX>T0C[Config Type][Status]<SUB>[Del Result]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: The response message of message T0B.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T0C - Response of Delete EMV Configuration Data Message.
    Format:            <STX>T0C[Config Type][Status]<SUB>[Del Result]<ETX>[LRC]
                       (response frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             The response message of message T0B.

    Message element:
                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field           Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    T0C                 3             Message ID
                    [Config Type]       1             1: CA public key.
                                                      2: EMV application data.
                    [Status]            1             0: Delete OK
                                                      1: Fatal error.
                                                      2: Format error.
                                                      3: No CA public key or EMV application data
                                                      exists.
                    <SUB>               1             <1A>, Optional, if Status is 0.
                    [Del Result]        Var.          Optional, if Status is 0.
                                                      0: the ID deletion is successful.
                                                      1: the ID deletion is failure.
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Checksum

    [Del Result]: It's the concatenation of the results for the delete operation on the indicated ID. There is a
    <FS> between each result. If the delete operation is successful (when A10-P finds out the matched one
    and delete it successfully), the result is 0. If there is no such ID as the terminal specified, the result is 1.

    Ex. Terminal issues message T0B to erase the EMV application data with ID "A0000000102020",
    "A0000020" and "A0000000103030". Now the A10-P keeps the EMV application data with ID
    "A0000000103030" only.
    The data in the [Del Result] field will be "1<FS>1<FS>0".

    Message flow:      Please refer to message T0B.
```

```text
                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T12               3             Message ID
                   Status            1             0:OK
                   [Application      10-32         EMV application is selected successfully.
                   Name]                           Format: Hexadecimal string. The content of

                                                   is selected.

                         Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T12               3             Message ID
                   Status            1             1:Fail
                   [Reason]          1             1:Fatal Error
                                                   2:Command Format Error
                                                   3:Transaction Canceled
                                                   4: MSR processing.
                   [Err Message]     8             Optional, if Reason = '1'Hex String
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    NOTE. According to the EMV Level2's rule, if the IC card cannot be read, A10-P will return message
            "T1214" to indicate that the terminal should apply magnetic stripe card processing. In this
            situation, the terminal should issue message Q1 to get the magnetic stripe data and issue
            message T1D to inform the A10-P on the magnetic stripe card data element. Message T15 is
            used to transmit the necessary data records (amount, transaction type, and so on...) for the
            A10-P to complete this transaction.

    Message flow:     Please refer to message T11.
```

[043] COMMAND T16 - Transaction Response
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 112-113
Format summary: <STX>T16[Status][Reason][Err Message][Result]<SUB> <Advice Need><Reversal Need><Financial Need><ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T16 - Transaction Response
    Format:           <STX>T16[Status][Reason][Err Message][Result]<SUB>
                      <Advice Need><Reversal Need><Financial Need><ETX>[LRC]
                      (response frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            The message contains the transaction result on the smart card to be sent to terminal.

    Message element:
                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field           Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   T16                 3             Message ID
                   [Status]            1             0:OK; 1:Fail
                   [Reason]            1             Optional. (If Status = 1)
                                                     1:Fatal Error
                                                     2:Command Format Error
                   [Err Message]       8             Optional, if Reason = '1'Hex String
                   [Result]            2             Optional. (If Status = 0)
                                                     'Y1': Offline Approved,
                                                     'Z1': Offline Declined
                                                     'Y3': Unable to go online,
                                                             Offline Approved
                                                     'Z3': Unable to go online, Offline Decline.
                                                     'Y4': Online Approved
                                                     'Z4': Online Decline
                                                     'A1': Online Authorize Request,
                                                     'A4': Application reselection.
                   <Reversal           1             0: Terminal does not need to send a reversal to
                   Need>                             the host for this transaction
                                                     1: Terminal should send a reversal to the host
                                                     for this transaction.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Note: If the [Result] is 'A1', then the terminal should send the online authorization request to the issuer
           host.   After that is done, send message T17 to the A10-P to continue the transaction. (See EMV
           4.3, book 3, chap 9, figure 7)
    Note: If the transaction is switched to MSR processing, T16 will always return "A1" in the [Result] field.

    Note: If the previous selected application on the IC card cannot perform the transaction (for example, this
           application has blocked) but has another application ID within this IC card, the A10-P will respond
           'A4' to let the terminal knows and the terminal can issue message T13 to select another
           application ID and issue message T15 to re-start the transaction. Please refer to the paragraph of
           "Ref. 5 Packet command flow for first EMV application is blocked" in the section of "Overall EMV
           Level 2 transaction flow reference".

    Message flow:     Please refer to message T15.
```

[048] COMMAND T1D - Transaction/Configuration Data Overwrite
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 119-120
Format summary: <STX>T1D<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: The terminal can use this command to update transaction/configuration data of the A10-P in run time. This command can be sent multiple times if needed. A10-P will save those data internally and use those data during the transaction. As a response the A10-P will send the message T1E to the terminal. [Notes] 1. T1D will temporarily override the transaction/configuration data (which were set by the previous configuration commands) within this transaction. Those previously configurations will be resumed in the new transaction. 2. Any erroneous transaction data update may fail the transaction process. 3. For the issuer returned authorization da...

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T1D - Transaction/Configuration Data Overwrite
    Format:             <STX>T1D<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:              The terminal can use this command to update transaction/configuration data of the
                        A10-P in run time. This command can be sent multiple times if needed. A10-P will save
                        those data internally and use those data during the transaction. As a response the
                        A10-P will send the message T1E to the terminal.
    [Notes]
                      1. T1D will temporarily override the transaction/configuration data (which were set by
                           the previous configuration commands) within this transaction. Those previously
                           configurations will be resumed in the new transaction.
                      2. Any erroneous transaction data update may fail the transaction process.
                      3. For the issuer returned authorization data such as ARC, IAD, or issuer scripts should
                           use message T17 to send to the A10-P in order to complete the EMV transaction.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T1D               3             Message ID
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>, Optional, only if [DO] exists
                   DO                Var.          Data Object, format as below
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Data Object:
        Each <DO> shall include three data fields: [Tag#] || [Format] || [Value], and each field shall delimit
    with a <FS>. Each data object is delimited by a <SUB> to construct multiple <DO>s. The [tag#] defined
    in EMV 4.3 Book3 Annex A and specific [tag#] defined at Appendix C of this manual have the
    pre-defined data format and length range. These [tag#] must follow up with these rules, otherwise the
    A10-P will reject this data setup. Any customer defining [tag#] number shall use message T07 to
    pre-define the data format and length range before using message T1D to load the data.

    Data Format: (Please also refer to EMV 4.3 BOOK3, section 4.3)
     Format                                                  Description
        1      a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
        2      b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
        3      an - Alphanumeric data    (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
        4      ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
        5      cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
        6      n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
        7      var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

    Example:
    (If the IC card cannot be read, the terminal will switch to MSR processing and then load these data into
    the A10-P.)
    Service Code:          0211 (Numeric)
    PAN:          123456789022334455(Compressed Numeric)
    Terminal sends,
    <STX>T1D<SUB>5F30<FS>6<FS>0211<SUB>5A<FS>5<FS>123456789022334455<ETX>[LRC]

    Message flow:
                             HOST                Direction                  A10-P

                    Message T1D                      ->
                                                                 <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     <-           <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                 <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                     <-           Message T1E
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[053] COMMAND T25 - Get Batch Data
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 125-126
Format summary: <STX>T25<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to get the batch data (EMV).

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T25 - Get Batch Data
    Format:           <STX>T25<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
    Usage:            This message is used to get the batch data (EMV).

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length              Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T25               3             Message ID
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    In each issuing of message T25, the A10-P will return one record in the batched data via message T26.
    The terminal can keep issuing message T25 until the A10-P returns a message to indicate that there is
    no more record in the batch data.

    User can load a tag list of batch data into the A10-P, and the A10-P will search the corresponding values
    according to the tag list and store it as a transaction record. Please refer to Appendix C for more details.

    Note. If there is no more memory space for batch data, the EMV transaction will turn out to be failed.
    Please issue message T23 to release the memory space.
    Note. A10-P can store at most 1000 transaction records.

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message T25                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message T26 (T262)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    Message T25                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message T26 (T262)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    ...                              ...       ...
                    Message T25                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message T26 (T261)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)                       A10-P erases batch data.
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[054] COMMAND T26 - Response of Get Batch Data message
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Source PDF page(s): 127
Format summary: <STX>T26[Status][record of Batch data]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Return the batch data to the terminal.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T26 - Response of Get Batch Data message
    Format:            <STX>T26[Status][record of Batch data]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             Return the batch data to the terminal.

    Message element:
                                        Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field         Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    T26               3             Message ID
                    Status            1             0: No more record.
                                                    1: It is the last record inside the A10-P.
                                                    2: There is still record existing inside the
                                                    A10-P.

    [EMV Tag Number (1 ~ 4 byte)] || [Length (1byte)] || [Value] || [EMV Tag Number (1 ~ 4 byte)] || [Length
    (1byte)] || [Value] || ...[EMV Tag Number (1 ~ 4 byte)] || [Length (1byte)] || [Value]. A10-P can save            up
    to 256 bytes of data as one record. The right part of data will be ignored if the length record is greater
    than 256 bytes.

    one record is 0x9F02 || 06 || 000000001100 || 5A || 10 || 1122334455667 7889900AABBCCDDEEFF,

```

```text
    record is 0x9F02 || 06 || 000000001100 || 5A || 10 || 11223344556677889900AABBC
    CDDEEFF,                        the                      terminal                       will                   see
    "9F02060000000011005A1011223344556677889900AABBCCDDEEFF" in the [Batch data] field.

    Message flow: Please refer to message T29
```

[059] COMMAND T2B - Get Online authorization Data with multi packets
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 6 - Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 132-133
Format summary: <STX>T2B[control]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 6 or 7 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: Issue this message to get the (EMV) data for online authorization.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T2B - Get Online authorization Data with multi packets
    Format:           <STX>T2B[control]<ETX>[LRC]                 (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 6 or 7 bytes.
    Usage:            Issue this message to get the (EMV) data for online authorization.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T2B               3             Message ID
                   [control]         1             Optional, as acknowledgment of multiple
                                                   packets
                                                   '0' = ready for next packet
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    If the EMV transaction must be authorized online, issue message T2B from the A10-P to get the
    necessary data for online authorization. If the transaction must be authorized online, the user can load a
    tag list of online authorization data into the A10-P. The latter will search for the corresponding values
    according to the tag list and returns it as the transaction record.

    Message flow:
                             HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                    Message T2B
                                                    ->
                    (1st packet)
                                                            <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                            <EOT> if LRC error after 2 retries.
                                                    <-       Message T2C (1st packet)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    Message T2B
                    (2nd packet) with               ->
                    [control] = '0'
                                                            <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                            <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-       Message T2C (2nd packet)
                    ...                                ...    ...
                    Message T2B (final)             ->
                                                            <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                            <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                            Message T2C
                                                    <-
                                                            (final packet) with [PktType] = '1'.
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T2C - Response of Get Online authorization Data message with multi packets
    Format:            <STX>T2C[PktType][SeqNo]<SUB>[record                       of       online   authorization
                       data]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             Return the online authorization data to the terminal.
    Message element:
                                        Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field          Length                Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   T2C                3             Message ID
```
