```text
    search the corresponding values according to this tag list and returns a series of data objects with TLV
    (tag || length|| value) format as below:
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] || [Length (2byte)] || [Value] <SUB>
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] || [Length (2byte)] || [Value] <SUB>
    ........
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] || [Length (2byte)] || [Value]
    When the A10-P responds to these data objects, it will convert their values from binary value to a hex
    decimal string if the data object format is "b" or "cn" or "n".
    For example:
```

[063] COMMAND T31 - Extract Information on Smart Card (non-EMV transactions)

Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: PIN Pad performs the application selection, initiate application processing and read application data on the active smart card. Section 7             Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
```text
Contactless EMV Level2 transaction messages are divided into 2 groups. One group are the
EMV-configuration data operation messages (T51, T53, T55, T75, T77) and the other group are the
EMV-transaction messages (T61, T63, T65, T6C, T71 and T73).

The issuing sequence of the PCD EMV transaction messages is controlled by the A10-P. An invalid
sequence will terminate that PCD EMV transaction. Message T61 is used for the terminal-side to transmit
transaction information such as the amount to be used by the A10-P to complete the transaction with the card
if the transaction does not need to be authorized online. Message T71 is applied if the transaction needs to
be authorized online. The terminal-side will transmit necessary information via this message to the A10-P to
complete the rest of transactional steps. If the response from the host contains issuer script (see EMV Book),
the terminal-side will issue message T73 to send these scripts into the A10-P. Then the A10-P will issue
these scripts at appropriate time to the card. Message T6C is used to terminate an EMV transaction. Finally,
message T65 is used for terminal-side to get the transaction information through out the PCD EMV
transaction. The transaction flow can be referred in the "Overall Contactless EMV level 2 transaction flow
reference" section.

The meanings of error codes in the [Err Message] are listed below:

    Error Code                                             Error Description
00000003            Service not accepted.
00000F9B            Store configuration data error.
8FFF0001            Out of memory.
8FFF0002            Parameter error.
8FFFFF02            Tag's data format error.
8FFFFF03            Some mandatory tags are not configured well.
8FFFFFF0            Command format error.
8FFFFFF1            The sequence of EMV transaction command is erroneous.
8FFFFFF2            Terminal fundamental data is missing.
8FFFFFF3            Authentication failed.
8FFFFF1A            Authentication key expired.
8FFFFF1B            Terminal configuration data is missing.
8FFFFF1C            No configuration data of EMV application or the data is missing.
8FFFFFF4            The storage space of batch data capture is full.
8FFFFFF5            No terminal configuration data, EMV application configuration data or CA public key.
A2000001            Application initial conditions are not satisfied.
A2000002            The generated cryptogram is not allowed.
A2000007            The specified instruction ID    is not recognized.
A200000A            The type    of the requested application cryptogram is incorrect.
A200000C            The status response code (SW1 SW2) is          not '9000'.
A200000D            The Generate AC command is called more than 2 times in the current transaction.
A200000E            The AIP mandatory data is missing in the card response data .
A200000F            The AFL mandatory data is missing in the card response data .
A2000010            The response template from the card is incorrect.
A2000011            The format of AFL is incorrect.
A2000013            A redundant data output from the card is not allowed.
A2000014            Missing mandatory data in the card response data .
EFFFFFFF            EMV transaction cancelled.
DFFFFFFF            EMV forced abort.
FFFF0001            There is an error when parsing the TLV list data.
FFFFFFFF            The contactless card does not respond data.
```

[070] COMMAND T51 - PCD Terminal Configuration Setup
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 154-156
Format summary: <STX>T51[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Host can use this command to send terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times. A10-P will save those data internally and apply them during the transaction. A10-P will send the message T52 (Terminal Configuration Setup Response) to the host as the response. The functions of Message T51 and Message T01 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T51 - PCD Terminal Configuration Setup
    Format:             <STX>T51[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:              Host can use this command to send terminal configuration data to the A10-P. This
                        command can be sent many times. A10-P will save those data internally and apply
                        them during the transaction. A10-P will send the message T52 (Terminal Configuration
                        Setup Response) to the host as the response. The functions of Message T51 and
                        Message T01 are exactly the same and can be used alternately.

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field        Length                 Value and description

                     <STX>            1             <02>
                     T51              3             Message ID
                     [Pkt No.]        1             Decimal. Packet sequence number (1 ~ 9)(ex.
                                                    2)
                     [Total Pkts]     1             Decimal. Total packets (1 ~ 9)(ex. 8).
                     <SUB>            1             <1A>
                     [DO]             Var.          Data Object, format as below
                     <ETX>            1             <03>
                     [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Data Object Format: each data object is delimited by <SUB>, and each field inside each data
    object is delimited by <FS>.

    Data Format: (Please also refer to the EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4,)
  Format                                                    Description
     1       a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
     2       b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
     3       an - Alphanumeric data (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
     4       ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
     5       cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
     6       n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
     7       var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

   Note. User has to follow the restriction specified in the EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4, and
           Appendix E of this document to load the configuration data. A10-P will check if the length
           of each configuration data item is consistent. Any inconsistent data item will make the data
           loading fail.
    Note. If the data format is '2' (binary), '5'(compressed numeric), '6'(numeric) or '7'(variable data),
           it cannot be allocated in message T51 directly. It should be transferred into a hexadecimal
           string and then allocated in message T51.

    Example: (Clear the terminal configuration data and then setup the new data.)
    Merchant Category Code: 0000 (Numerical)
    Terminal ID:                 SmartPOS (Ascii)

    <STX>T5111<SUB>9f15<FS>6<FS>0000<SUB>9f1c<FS>3<FS>SmartPOS<ETX>[LRC]

    A10-P will check if the terminal downloads the minimum set of terminal-related information into itself. The
    download process will fail if there is not enough data in this message. Please refer to Appendix F for the
    minimum set of terminal-related data.

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    1st Message T51                ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       1st Message T52
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    2nd Message T51                ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       2nd Message T52
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    ...                              ...       ...
                    Last one Message T51           ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Last one Message T52
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[074] COMMAND T55 - PCD Application Configuration Setup
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 160-162
Format summary: <STX>T55[Pkt No.][TotalPkts]<SUB>[TXN]<SUB>[KID]<SUB>[AID]<SUB> [DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>T55[Pkt No.][Total Pkts]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Host can use this command to send out the EMV application configuration data to the A10-P. A10-P will send message T56 (EMV Application Configuration Setup Response) to the host. ```text

```text
    Format:           <STX>T55[Pkt No.][TotalPkts]<SUB>[TXN]<SUB>[KID]<SUB>[AID]<SUB>
                      [DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Usage:            Host can use this command to send out the EMV application configuration data to the
                      A10-P. This command can be sent many times but each command is only used for one
                      application. A10-P will save those data inside and use them during the transaction.
                      A10-P will send message T56 (EMV Application Configuration Setup Response) to the
                      host. The data installed into the A10-P via this message will be saved       in the internal
                      storage structure with a name same as in the [AID] field.

                   <SUB>             1             <1A>

                   <ETX>             1             <03>

                                            Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                            Field        Length                 Value and description

                      <STX>             1            <02>
                      T55               3            Message ID
                      [Pkt No.]         1            Decimal. Packet sequence number (2 ~ 9) (ex.
                                                     2).
                      [Total Pkts]      1            Decimal. Total packets (2 ~ 9)(ex. 8).
                      <SUB>             1            <1A>

                      [LRC]             1            Checksum

    Format of Data Objects:
    Each data object shall include                three data    fields delimited    by <FS>: [Tag#]<FS>[Format
    Code]<FS>[Value]. Each data object is delimited by a <SUB> to construct multiple <DO>s. The [tag#] is

    Format                                                     Description
       1        a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
       2        b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations

       4        ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
       5        cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
       6        n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
       7        var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

           Appendix E of this document to load the configuration data. A10-P will check if the length of

    Note. If the data format is '2' (binary), '5'(compressed numeric), '6'(numeric) or '7'(variable data),

    <SUB>40000043<FS>6<FS>000000008000<SUB>9F7A<FS>2<FS>01<ETX>[LRC]

    The A10-P will check if the terminal downloads the minimum set of EMV Application-related information

    Appendix F for the minimum set of EMV Application-related data.

    Message flow:
                             HOST              Direction                A10-P

                                                   <-

                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)

                    Last one Message T55           ->

                                                   <-
                                                           Last one Message T56
```

```text

    Format:             <STX>T59[Config Type][control]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 7 or 8 bytes.
    Usage:              Get the group ID of the PCD application data or the CA public key stored in the A10-P.
```

[079] COMMAND T5C - Response of Delete PCD Configuration Data Message.

Source PDF page(s): 167

Message length: Variable.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T5C - Response of Delete PCD Configuration Data Message.
    Format:            <STX>T5C[Config Type][Status]<SUB>[Del Result]<ETX>[LRC]
                       (response frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             The response message of message T5B.

    Message element:
                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field           Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    T5C                 3             Message ID
                    [Config Type]       1             0: Unknow type.
                                                      1: CA public key.
                                                      2: EMV application data.
                    [Status]            1             0: Delete OK
                                                      1: Fatal error.
                                                      2: Format error.
                    <SUB>               1             <1A>, Optional, if Status is 0.
                    [Del Result]        var            The results of the delete operation on the
                                                      indicated ID
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Checksum

    [Del Result]:
    It's the concatenation of the results for the delete operation on the indicated ID. There is a <FS> between
    each result. If the delete operation is successful (when A10-P finds out the matched one and delete it
    successfully), the result is 0. If there is no such ID as the terminal specified, the result is 1.

    Ex. Terminal issues message T5B to erase the EMV application data with ID "A0000000102020",
    "A0000020" and "A0000000103030". Now the A10-P keeps the EMV application data with ID
    "A0000000103030" only.
    The data in the [Del Result] field will be "1<FS>1<FS>0".

    Message flow:
        Refer to message T5B.
```

[082] COMMAND T5F - PCD DRL Configuration Setup.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 170-171
Format summary: <STX>T5F<SUB>[AID]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Host can use this command to send DRL(Dynamic Reader Limit) configuration data to the A10-P. This command can be sent many times. A10-P will save those data internally and apply them during the transaction. A10-P will send the message T5G (PCD DRL Configuration Setup Response) to the host as the response.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T5F - PCD DRL Configuration Setup.
    Format:           <STX>T5F<SUB>[AID]<SUB>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            Host can use this command to send DRL(Dynamic Reader Limit) configuration data to
                      the A10-P. This command can be sent many times. A10-P will save those data
                      internally and apply them during the transaction. A10-P will send the message T5G
                      (PCD DRL Configuration Setup Response) to the host as the response.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T5F               3             Message ID
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   AID               2~32          EMV Application ID, refer to EMV
                                                   Contactless Specifications v2.4, Hex decimal
                                                   string.
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   [DO]              Var.          Data Object, format as below
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Format of Data Objects:
    Each data object shall include three data fields delimited by <FS>: [Tag#]<FS>[Format Code]<FS>
    [Value] Each data object is delimited by a <SUB> to construct multiple <DO>s. The [tag#] defined in
    EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4, section 4.3.

    Data Format: (Please also refer to EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4)
  Format                                                   Description
     1      a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
     2      b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
     3      an - Alphanumeric data    (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
     4      ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
     5      cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
     6      n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
     7      var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

    Message flow:
                             HOST               Direction                   A10-P

                    Message T5F                     ->
                                                              <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                              <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-         Message T5G
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[086] COMMAND T61 - Start Transaction
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 175-178
Format summary: <STX>T61<SUB>[AmtAuth]<SUB>[AmtOther]<SUB> [CurExponent][CurCode]<SUB>[TranType]<SUB>[TranInfo]<SUB> [Account Type]<SUB>[Force Online]<SUB> [Encrypted Session key]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: After receiving message T61, the A10-P will perform a complete EMV transaction (the flow will cover from 'Initiate Application' through 'Completion', see EMV Contactless Specifications 2.4, book A, chap 5.3, figure 5-2 - Logical Architecture). A10-P will send message T62 (Start Transaction Response) to the host as the response.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T61 - Start Transaction
    Format:           <STX>T61<SUB>[AmtAuth]<SUB>[AmtOther]<SUB>
                      [CurExponent][CurCode]<SUB>[TranType]<SUB>[TranInfo]<SUB>
                      [Account Type]<SUB>[Force Online]<SUB>
                      [Encrypted Session key]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            After receiving message T61, the A10-P will perform a complete EMV transaction
                      (the flow will cover from 'Initiate Application' through 'Completion', see EMV
                      Contactless Specifications 2.4, book A, chap 5.3, figure 5-2 - Logical Architecture).
                      A10-P will send message T62 (Start Transaction Response) to the host as the
                      response.

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   T61               3             Message ID
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   [AmtAuth]         12            Optional: Numerical string (include digits
                                                   after decimal point) to describe the "Amount
                                                   Authrozied" used in the purchase transaction.
                                                   Map to EMV tag '0x9f02'
                                                   Ex: "000000012345" means 123.45 if
                                                   [CurExponent] is set to '2'.
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   [AmtOther]        12            Optional: Numerical string (include digits
                                                   after decimal point) to describe the "Amount,
                                                   Other" used in the special transaction, such as
                                                   the "cashback" amount. Map to EMV tag
                                                   '0x9f03'
                   <SUB>             1             <1A>
                   [CurExponent]     1             Numerical digit ('0' to '3') to describe the
                                                   "Transaction Currency Exponent", which is
                                                   the count of digits after the decimal point.
                                                   Map to EMV tag '0x5f36'
                   [CurCode]         3             Numerical string to describe the "Transaction
                                                   Currency Code". Map to EMV tag '0x5f2a'.
                                                   Ex: USD = "840"

                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [TranType]       2             Numerical string to indicate the type of
                                                  transaction, presented by the first two digits of
                                                  the ISO 8583:1987 field 3 (processing code.)
                                                  Map to EMV tag '0x9c'
                                                  Ex.
                                                  "00" - purchase,
                                                  "01" - cash advance,
                                                   "09" - purchase with cashback,
                                                   "20" - refund.
                                                  The actual values to be used are defined by
                                                  the relevant payment system.
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [TranInfo]       2             Hexadecimal string to indicate the private
                                                  parameter "Transaction Info". Map to private
                                                  tag '0xFFFF8109'
                                                  Allowable values:
                                                   "80" - Cash (cash advance)
                                                   "40" - Goods
                                                   "20" - Services
                                                  "10" - Cashback
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Account         2             Account Type, Map to EMV tag '0x5f57'
                   Type]                          Allowable values (ref. EMV v4.3 book3
                                                  Annex G)
                                                  "00" - Default
                                                  "10" - Savings
                                                  "20" - Cheque / Debit
                                                  "30" - Credit.
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Force Online]   1             '1': Force this transaction to be authorized
                                                  online.   Valid only if the terminal
                                                  configuration enables the capability to support
                                                  online authorization.
                                                  '0': Run the default EMV authorization flow
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Encrypted       16 or 32      Optional, DES or TDES session key that is
                   Session key]     or 48         used to encrypt the PIN block when CVM
                                                  asks for online PIN verification. If this session

                                                   key is not entered, A10-P will use an actived
                                                   PIN encryption key (the key usage is P0) or an
                                                   actived DUKPT to encrypt the PIN block.
                    <SUB>            1             <1A>,Optional, only if [DO]    exists
                    DO               Var.          Data Object, format as below
                    <ETX>            1             <03>
                    [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Format of Data Objects:
    Each data object shall include            three data      fields delimited    by <FS>: [Tag#]<FS>[Format
    Code]<FS>[Value]. Each data object is delimited by a <SUB> to construct multiple <DO>s. The [tag#] is
    defined in the EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4. There are also some private tags defined in
    Appendix E.

    Data Format: (Please also refer to EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4)
  Format                                                   Description
     1      a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
     2      b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
     3      an - Alphanumeric data (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
     4      ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
     5      cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
     6      n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
     7      var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

   Note. User has to follow the restriction specified in EMV Contactless Specifications v2.4 and
           Appendix E of this document to load the configuration data. A10-P will check if the length of
           each configuration data item is consistent. Any inconsistent data item will make the data
           loading fail.
    Note. If the data format is '2' (binary), '5'(compressed numeric), '6'(numeric) or '7'(variable data),
           it cannot be allocated in message T61 directly. It should be transferred into a hexadecimal
           string and then allocated in message T61.

    Example:
    Balance Read Before Gen AC:           000000 (Numeric)
    Balance Read After Gen AC:            000000 (Numeric)
    [DO]:
    DF8104<FS>6<FS>000000<SUB>DF8105<FS>6<FS>000000

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message T61                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Start Transaction Response.
                                                   <-
                                                           Message T62
```

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T62 - Start Transaction Response
    Format:            <STX>T62[Status][Reason][Err Message][Result]<ETX>[LRC]
                       (response frame)
    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             The message contains the transaction result on the smart card to be sent to the
                       terminal.

                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field           Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    T62                 3             Message ID
                    [Status]            1             0:OK; 1:Fail

                                                      1:Fatal Error
                                                      2:Command Format Error
                    [Err Message]       8             Optional, if Reason = '1'Hex String
                                                      '00000007':     Please see note.
                    [Result]            2             Optional. (If Status = 0)
                                                      'Y1': Offline Approved,
                                                      'Z1': Offline Declined
                                                      'Y3': Unable to go online,
                                                              Offline Approved
                                                      'Z3': Unable to go online, Offline Declined.
                                                      'Y4': Online Approved

                                                      'Y8': Unable to go online,
                                                              Offline Approved With Signature

                                                      'A1': Online Authorize Request
                                                      'B0': Try another interface.

           and After      that, the terminal shall send message T71 to the A10-P to continue the transaction.
    Note: For special error code, if the [Status] is '1', [Reason] is '1', [Err Message] is '00000007', the
           terminal shall send message T61 to Start Transaction.
    Message flow:
        Refer to message T61.
```

Format summary: <STX>T64[Pkt NO.][Total Pkt][DO]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame) <STX>T64[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message T64 - Get the Transaction Result Data Response
    Format:           <STX>T64[Pkt NO.][Total Pkt][DO]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
                      <STX>T64[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            The message contains the transaction result data to be sent to the host.

    Message element:
                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field           Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   T64                 3             Message ID
                   [Pkt NO.]           1             Decimal. Packet sequence number (1 ~ 9).
                   [Total Pkt]         1              Decimal. Total packets (1~9).
                   [DO]                Var.          Data Object: each data object is expressed in
                                                     the TLV format with an <FS> delimit in each
                                                     field, and <SUB> is used to delimit each
                                                     object. For example:
                                                     9F12<FS>0F<FS>CREDITO DE
                                                     VISA<SUB>9A<FS>06<FS>050806<SUB>
                                                     .......
                   <ETX>               1             <03>

    or
                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field           Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   T64                 3             Message ID
                   [Status]            1             F: Query fail or data empty.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Data Object:
    A10-P will return a series of data objects listed on the [DOL] fields in the message T64 with TLV (tag ||
    length|| value) format as below:

    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value] <SUB>
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value] <SUB>
    ........
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value].

    Note:   When the A10-P responds these data objects, it will convert        from binary values to a hex
            decimal string if the data object format is "b" or "cn" or "n".

    Message flow:
        Refer to message T63.
```

```text
                                                   Map to EMV tag '0x5f36'
                   [CurCode]         3             Numerical string to describe the "Transaction
                                                   Currency Code". Map to EMV tag '0x5f2a'.
                                                   Ex: USD = "840"

                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [TranType]       2             Numerical string to indicate the type of
                                                  transaction, presented by the first two digits of
                                                  the ISO 8583:1987 field 3 (processing code.)
                                                  Map to EMV tag '0x9c'
                                                  Ex.
                                                  "00" - purchase,
                                                  "01" - cash advance,
                                                   "09" - purchase with cashback,
                                                   "20" - refund.
                                                  The actual values to be used are defined by
                                                  the relevant payment system.
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [TranInfo]       2             Hexadecimal string to indicate the private
                                                  parameter "Transaction Info". Map to private
                                                  tag '0xFFFF8109'
                                                  Allowable values:
                                                   "80" - Cash (cash advance)
                                                   "40" - Goods
                                                   "20" - Services
                                                  "10" - Cashback
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Account         2             Account Type, Map to EMV tag '0x5f57'
                   Type]                          Allowable values (ref. EMV v4.3 book3
                                                  Annex G)
                                                  "00" - Default
                                                  "10" - Savings
                                                  "20" - Cheque / Debit
                                                  "30" - Credit.
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Force Online]   1             '1': Force this transaction to be authorized
                                                  online.   Valid only if the terminal
                                                  configuration enables the capability to support
                                                  online authorization.
                                                  '0': Run the default EMV authorization flow
                   <SUB>            1             <1A>
                   [Encrypted       16 or 32      Optional, DES or TDES session key that is
                   Session key]     or 48         used to encrypt the PIN block when CVM
                                                  asks for online PIN verification. If this session

                                                       key is not entered, the A10-P will use an
                                                       actived PIN encryption key (the key usage is
                                                       P0) or an actived DUKPT to encrypt the PIN
                                                       block.
                      <SUB>              1             <1A>,Optional, only if [DO]    exists
                      DO                 Var.          Data Object, format as below
                      <ETX>              1             <03>
                      [LRC]              1             Checksum

       Format Codes for Data Object Elements:
    Format                                                      Description
   1            a - Alphabetic data (a ~z, A~Z)
   2            b - unsigned binary numbers or bit combinations
   3            an - Alphanumeric data       (a ~z, A~Z, 0~9)
   4            ans - Alphanumeric Special data (Characters defined in ISO8859)
   5            cn - Compressed numeric data (0~9, left justify, pad hexadecimal 'F's. Ex. 12 34 56 12 3F FF)
   6            n - Numeric data (0~9, right justify, pad leading hexadecimal zeroes. Ex. 00 00 00 01 23 45)
   7            var - Variable data (Any bit combination)

       Notes on Data Objects field:
       If the data format is '2' (binary), '5' (compressed numeric), '6' (numeric) or '7' (variable data), the [value]
       corresponding to each format cannot be sent with the format directly in message T81. It shall be
       converted to a hexadecimal string. A pad character has to be added at the end if this tag# has odd
       characters. The pad char 'F' is used for format 'cn', and '0' is used for formats 'b' or 'n'.

       Example:
       Balance Read Before Gen AC:              000000 (Numeric)
       Balance Read After Gen AC:               000000 (Numeric)
       [DO]:
       DF8104<FS>6<FS>000000<SUB>DF8105<FS>6<FS>000000

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction               A10-P

                    Message T81                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-       Message T12/T16/T62
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[103] COMMAND SIG - Signals to the Terminal
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 7 - Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Source PDF page(s): 203-210
Format summary: <STX>SIG[Control][PktNo][SeqID][DataType][Timeout] <SUB>[Data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Initiated by Device during EMV transaction for external user interface request or send DET signal. The terminal should handle the request with Display and Keypad, or receive and match DET to get DEK, then return the result to the Device within the timeout.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message SIG - Signals to the Terminal
    Format:           <STX>SIG[Control][PktNo][SeqID][DataType][Timeout]
                      <SUB>[Data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            Initiated by Device during EMV transaction for external user interface request or send
                      DET signal. The terminal should handle the request with Display and Keypad, or
                      receive and match DET to get DEK, then return the result to the Device within the
                      timeout.

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   SIG                3             Message ID
                   [Control]          1             '0': (transmitter side) more packets follow.
                                                    '1': (transmitter side) the last packet.
                                                    '2': (receiver side) ready for the next packet.
                                                    '3': (receiver side) acknowledge the last
                                                    packet.
                   [PktNo]            1             '0' ~ '9', The packet number (increment on
                                                    transmitter side).
                   [SeqID]            2             "00" ~ "FF", the sequence number increments
                                                    on each SIG packet on both sides for
                                                    handshaking purpose.
                                                    Reset on power-on, rollover to "00" after
                                                    reaching "FF".
                   [DataType]         2             "00": Clear screen.
                                                    "03": Display text and get function key.
                                                    "04": Function key input (response of 03.)
                                                    "07": Display and select Application ID.
                                                    "08": Selected AID (response of 07.)
                                                    "09": Display and select language.
                                                    "0A": Selected language (response of 09.)
                                                    "0B": Data Exchange Kernel (DEK Signal)
                                                    "0C": Data Exchange Terminal (DET Signal,
                                                    response of 0B)
                                                    "FF": Host error or times out.
                   [Timeout]          2             Hex string represents the waiting time for

                                                      response, in seconds. Available value: "01" ~
                                                      "FE".
                                                      "00": No waiting time and no need response
                                                      SIG packet.
                                                      "FF": Wait forever for response.
                    <SUB>               1             <1A> as delimiter
                    [Data]              Var.          Data field, see description below.
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Check value

    [Data] format for type "00" (clear screen) (reserved word):

                    Field           Length                          Value and description

           [Data]                   0          The "clear screen" have an empty data field.
                                               The terminal should clear its display.

    [Data] format for type "03" (display text and get function key) (reserved word):

                    Field           Length                          Value and description

           [Data]                   Var.       The message field includes ASCII text messages to be shown
                                               on external UI.
                                               The terminal should display the message and collect a single
                                               function key (ENTER / CANCEL,) or responds a "type FF"
                                               packet for error situation.

    [Data] format for type "04" (function key input) (reserved word):

                    Field           Length                          Value and description

           [Data]                   1          '0': ENTER key pressed.
                                               '1': CANCEL key pressed.

    [Data] format for type "07" (display and select Application ID) (reserved word):

                 Field          Length                              Value and description

        [Data]                  Var.        [AppName1]<FS>[AppName2]<FS>...
                                            Each AppName is a string that identifies application in the IC card.
                                            The terminal should parse the AID list and allow the user to select
                                            one AID for following EMV transaction, or responds a "type FF"
                                            packet for error situation.

    [Data] format for type "08" (selected AID) (reserved word):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  Var       The exact AID string that user chose.

    [Data] format for type "09" (display and select language) (reserved word):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  Var.      [LangID1]<FS>[LangID2]<FS>...
                                             Each LangID is a two-character ISO639-1 language code, or
                                             "Default" that allows the terminal to determine its preferred
                                             language.
                                             The terminal should parse the LangID list and allow the user
                                             to select one supported language for following EMV
                                             transaction, or responds a "type FF" packet for error
                                             situation.

    [Data] format for type "0A" (selected language) (reserved word):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  Var       The exact language ID string that user chose.

    [Data] format for type "0B" (Data Exchange Kernel (DEK Signal)):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  Var       <SUB>[Tag#]<FS>[Length Code]<FS>[Value]...

    [Data] format for type "0C" (Data Exchange Terminal (DET Signal)):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  Var       <SUB>[Tag#]<FS>[Length Code]<FS>[Value]...

    [Data] format for type "FF" (host error or timed out) (reserved word):

                    Field          Length                         Value and description

           [Data]                  1         '0': Timeout happened.
                                             '1': User aborted.
                                             '2': Other error on the host side.

    Message Flow (signals that does not require response):
                            HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                   T61                             ->
                                                   <-       Message SIG
                   <ACK> if LRC ok.                ->
                   <NAK> if LRC error.

    Message Flow (signals that require response):
                            HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                   T61                         ->
                                               <-           Message SIG (request)
                   <ACK> if LRC ok.            ->
                   <NAK> if LRC error.
                   Message SIG (response)      ->
                                               <-           <ACK> / <NAK>

    Example:
    This example is the captured transmission for AID / language selection by card holder. The terminal
    configuration needs to be modified to enable these features. <ACK> / <NAK> characters are omitted. For
    MCL data exchange:
                             HOST               Direction              A10-P

                   T61                             ->
                                                   <-        SIG10000BFF<1C>FF810400DF8
                                                            10603DF8112
                   SIG10010C00<1C>DF8              ->
                   1120182
                                                   <-        SIG10000BFF<1C>FF810404820
                                                            20000DF810600
                   SIG10010C00<1C>DF8              ->
                   1100100DF81100100DF
                   81100100DF81100100D
                   F81100100DF81100100
                   DF81100100DF8110010
                   0DF81100100DF811001
                   00DF81100101DF81120
                   55A5F209F12
                                                   <-        SIG10000BFF<1C>FF81040D5A
                                                            0854133390000015139F1200
                   SIG10010C00<1C>                 ->
                                                   <-        T620A1

    Note: SIG occurs only between T61 and T62. The rest of the transaction process after this is according
    to other situations (e.g. T71, T63, T65).

Overall Contactless EMV Level 2 transaction flow reference

    A10-P provides one complete EMV Level 2 transaction with online or offline approval by various possible
    command flows. To force the A10-P to leave the command flow, you can either press the [CANCEL] key
    or send message T6C to the A10-P.

    Ref. 1      Packet command flow for transaction with offline approval

                            HOST               Direction               A10-P

                    T61 (Start Transaction)        ->
                                                           T62 (Start Transaction Response)
                                                   <-
                                                           [Result] = 'Y1' or 'Z1'
                    T65 (Get online data
                                                   ->
                    from A10-P)
                                                           T66 (Online authorization data
                                                   <-
                                                           response)
                    T63 (Get Transaction
                                                   ->
                    Result's Data)
                                                           T64 (Get Transaction Result Data
                                                   <-
                                                           Response)

    Ref. 2      Packet command flow for transaction with online approval

                            HOST               Direction               A10-P

                    T61 (Start Transaction)        ->
                                                           T62 (Start Transaction Response)
                                                   <-
                                                           [Result] = 'A1'
                    T65 (Get online data
                                                   ->
                    from A10-P)
                                                           T66 (Online authorization data
                                                   <-
                                                           response)
                    T63 (Get Transaction
                                                   ->
                    Result's Data)
                                                           T64 (Get Transaction Result Data
                                                   <-
                                                           Response)
                    Go Online
                    T71     (Send    Online
                                                   ->
                    Authorized Code)
                                                   <-       T62 (Start Transaction Response)
                    T63 (Get Transaction
                                                   ->
                    Result's Data)
                                                           T64 (Get Transaction Result Data
                                                   <-
                                                           Response)

Section 8           MIFARE Card Messages
    This chapter describes the commands of the MIFARE cards. The A10-P supports the MIFARE classic,
    Ultralight and DESFire cards. All MIFARE cards are compliant to the ISO/IEC 14443-1, 2 and 3
    standards. The MIFARE DESFire card supports the ISO/IEC 14443-4 protocol (also called "T=CL"
    protocol).
```

Section: Section 8 - MIFARE Card Messages
Source PDF page(s): 222-223
Format summary: <STX>P07[Sector number][Key type][key value]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame 1) <STX>P07[Sector number][Key number][key type]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame 2) <STX>P07[Result][Reason]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Before any memory operation can be carried out, the card has to be selected and authenticated.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message P07 - MIFARE Classic Card Authentication
    Format:           <STX>P07[Sector number][Key type][key value]<ETX>[LRC]
                      (request frame 1)
                      <STX>P07[Sector number][Key number][key type]<ETX>[LRC]
                      (request frame 2)
                      <STX>P07[Result][Reason]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
    Message length: variable.
    Usage:            Before any memory operation can be carried out, the card has to be selected and
                      authenticated.

    NOTE:             If the [Key type] and [Key value] is empty in the request frame 1, the A10-P will use key
                      value with "FFFFFFFFFFFF" and key type with 'A'.

    Message element:
                                          Request1 frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length                   Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   P07                3             Message ID
                   [Sector            2             The sector number.
                   number]                          Decimal string: 00~39.
                   [Key type]         1             (optional)
                                                    Determine which card type to authenticate.
                                                    Format: 'A' or 'B'.
                   [Key value]        12            (optional)
                                                    The card will be authenticated with this key
                                                    value.
                                                    Format: hexadecimal string.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                            Request2 frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field           Length                   Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    P07                 3             Message ID
                    [Sector             2             The sector number.
                    number]                           Decimal string: 00~39.
                    [Key number]        3             The key stored in the A10-P.
                                                      Decimal string: 000~255.
                    [Key type]          1             Determine which card type to authenticate.
                                                      Format: 'A' or 'B'.
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Checksum

                                          Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field           Length                   Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    P07                 3             Message ID
                    [Result]            1             '0': Success.
                                                      '1': Fail.
                    [Reason]            1             Optional: if [Result] = '1'
                                                      '1': Format error.
                                                      '2': Sequence error.
                                                      '3': Key authentication fail.
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST               Direction                    A10-P

                    Message P07
                                                       ->
                    (request frame)
                                                                   <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                       <-           <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                   <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                       <-           Message P07 (response frame)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                    ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[124] COMMAND 70 - PIN entry request (MK/SK)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 9 - Online Transaction Messages with Master/Session Keys (MK/SK)
Source PDF page(s): 255-258
Format summary: <STX>70.[Account]<FS>[session key][Amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and send message 71. [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key. Notes: User Interactive Sequence: The prompts on the LCD of each phase are as following. After message 70 received Total Amount (The display language can be selected) $xxx.xx Enter PIN Push "ENTER" After user presses first digit PIN: (Each * represents one digit...

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 70 - PIN entry request (MK/SK)
    Format:            <STX>70.[Account]<FS>[session key][Amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC]
                       (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             Display prompt to invite user to input PIN.
                       The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens:
                       [ENTER] key pressed;             PIN pad validates input and send message 71.
                       [CAN] key pressed;               PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>.
                       Message 72 received;             PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>.
                       Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.

    Notes:             User Interactive Sequence: The prompts on the LCD of each phase are as following.

                       After message 70 received                        Total Amount
                       (The display language can be selected)           $xxx.xx
                                                                        Enter PIN
                                                                        Push "ENTER"
                       After user presses first digit                   PIN:
                       (Each * represents one digit)                    ****
                       If [ENTER] pressed                               PIN PAD
                                                                        PROCESSING
                                                                        (Until [CLR] pressed or new command
                                                                        received, can be turned off by message Z7)
                       If [CAN] pressed                                 Transaction
                                                                        Cancelled
                                                                        (Return to idle prompt after 3 seconds, can be
                                                                        turned off by message Z7)

                       PIN length: According to the ANSI X9.8 standard, the length of the PIN should be
                       between 4 to 12 digits. If the user inputs less than 4 digits and then press ENTER,
                       A10-P will beep for error and continue to wait for the user's input. After the user inputs
                       the 13th character, the A10-P will beep for error, conserves the PIN characters 1st to
                       12th, and wait for the ENTER.

                       This message has implemented the countermeasure to prevent an exhaustive PIN
                       determination attack. See Appendix A for details.

                       Master key must be selected before starting the transaction: A10-P will warn and
                       refuse message 70 if message 08 was not issued before.

                       The key and algorithm that used to encrypt the PIN block:

                                    Session Key            8 bytes (16 chars) or    24 bytes (48 chars)
                       Active Master Key                   16 bytes (32 chars)      Session key
                                                           Session key
                           TDES "K0" (24 bytes)            Use MK to decrypt SK     Use MK to decrypt SK
                                                           Use SK to encrypt PIN    Use SK to encrypt PIN
                           TDES "P0" (24 bytes)            SK must be "0"           SK must be "0"
                                                           Use MK to encrypt PIN    Use MK to encrypt PIN
                           TDES "K0" (16 bytes)            Use MK to decrypt SK     Error.
                                                           Use SK to encrypt PIN
                       TDES "P0" (8 or 16 bytes)           SK must be "0"           Error.
                                                           Use MK to encrypt PIN

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>            1             <02>
                    70               2             Message ID
                    .                1             <2E>, delimiter
                    [Account]        8..19         Card account number
                    <FS>             1             <1C>, field separator
                    [session key]    16 or 32      Session key encrypted by the active master
                                     or 48         key. The operating mode to decrypt the
                                                   session key will be ECB.
                                                   Format: hexadecimal string.
                                                   This field should be all zeros if the active
                                                   master key is usage "P0"
                    [Amount]         4 to 12       Amount of goods to be displayed on the
                                                   A10-P.
                                                   Accepts digit character ('0' ~ '9'), minus ('-'),
                                                   comma (',') and decimal point ('.')
                    <FS>             1             (optional) <1C>, field separator
                    [timeout]        1             (optional) ASCII characters from '1' to '9'
                                                   which is the timeout value in units of 30
                                                   seconds. Default = 9x30 = 270 seconds.
                    <ETX>            1             <03>
                    [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST             Direction                    A10-P

                    Message 70                       ->
                                                                 <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                                 <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                     <-
                                                                 <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                                 Prompt user to enter PIN.
                                                                 Message 71 or <EOT> when input
                                                     <-
                                                                 times out or [CAN] is pressed
                    <ACK> (Good echo)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                                 Display "PIN PAD
                                                                 PROCESSING" until [CLEAR] is
                                                                 pressed or another message is
                                                                 received.
```

```text
Message 71 - Encrypted PIN Block Response (MK/SK)

                    [fkey]             1            Always '0' (This field is kept to retain the old

                                                              Message 71 or <EOT> when input
                                                     <-
                                                              times out or [CAN] is pressed
                    <ACK> (Good echo)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                              Display processing prompt

    Error codes:
                   Code                                     Meaning
                     '0'    Null Account input field.
                     '1'    Key value error.
                            (session key value conflicted with the usage of the active master key,
                            or session key length longer than the active master key)
                     '2'    Account number shorter than 8 digits.
                     '3'    Account number longer than 19 digits.
                     '4'    Account number has character(s) other than '0'-'9'.
                     '5'    Session key format error.
                     '6'    Timeout value error
                     '7'    No more DES operation within 60 minutes (refer to Appendix A)
                     '8'    Amount string format error originated from Message 70
                            PIN count, Accept Null PIN flag, and Prompt string format error
                            originated from Message Z62
                     '9'    Active master key not exists
                     'A'    Active master key usage incorrect (non K0 or P0 key)
                     'B'    Key storage access error
                     'C'    Memory buffer allocation error
                     'E'    Data length error in a field.
                     'G'    Specified file not found or authentication error.
```

[126] COMMAND 72 - PIN Entry Cancel
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 9 - Online Transaction Messages with Master/Session Keys (MK/SK)
Source PDF page(s): 261
Format summary: <STX>72<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 5 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: Cancel the current transaction that is waiting for user's input and return the A10-P to the IDLE state. The commands that can be canceled by message 72 include 70, Z60, Z62 (for both MK/SK and DUKPT), 60, 62, Z42, Z50, Q1, Q8, Q9, QK. If the A10-P receives message 72 while processing the user input such as swipe card, enter a PIN or keying in data, It will respond with <EOT> to acknowledge that the operation is canceled.

[130] COMMAND Z64 - Query Key Check Value (KCV)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 9 - Online Transaction Messages with Master/Session Keys (MK/SK)
Source PDF page(s): 268
Format summary: <STX>Z64[KeyID]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 7 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message will export the KCV of the specified master key. KCV is calculated as following: 1. Use [KeyID] specified key as encryption key. 2. Use "0000000000000000" (8 bytes zero) as data. 3. If the encrypt key is single length (8 bytes), use TDES algorithm to encrypt the data. 4. Take leftmost 3 bytes as KCV, output KCV as message Z65.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z64 - Query Key Check Value (KCV)
    Format:            <STX>Z64[KeyID]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 7 bytes.
    Usage:             This message will export the KCV of the specified master key.
                       KCV is calculated as following:
                       1. Use [KeyID] specified key as encryption key.
                       2. Use "0000000000000000" (8 bytes zero) as data.
                       3. If the encrypt key is single length (8 bytes), use TDES algorithm to encrypt the data.
                       4. Take leftmost 3 bytes as KCV, output KCV as message Z65.
    Example:           TDES key "0123456789ABCDEF FEDCBA9876543210" will have KCV as "08D7B4".

    Message element:
                                         Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field        Length                   Value and description

                    <STX>            1             <02>
                    Z64              3             Message ID
                    [KeyID]          1             '0' ~ '9', 'A' ~ 'G',
                                                   The ID of master keys.
                    <ETX>            1             <03>
                    [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST              Direction                      A10-P

                    Message Z64                     ->
                                                                 <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-            <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                 (<EOT> after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-            Message Z65
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[132] COMMAND Z66 - Message Authentication Code (MAC) Request

Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to generate the MAC codes according to the algorithm specified in ANSI X9.19 (ISO 9797-1).
