Notes: Message Length: A onetime message that can be up to 224 characters (equal to 112 bytes when send as a hexadecimal string because 2 characters form 1 byte). Multiple messages can have sequence numbers from 00 to 99. Thus the maximum capacity of message Z66 is 22,400 characters (or 11,200 bytes in binary mode)....

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z66 - Message Authentication Code (MAC) Request
    Format:            <STX>Z66[PktType][SeqNo][KeyId]<FS>[SessionKey]<FS>
                       [SecKeyId]<FS>[Message] <ETX> [LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable 14 to 270 bytes.
    Usage:             This message is used to generate the MAC codes according to the algorithm specified
                       in ANSI X9.19 (ISO 9797-1). User can send ASCII strings or hexadecimal strings to
                       the A10-P by message Z66 to generate its MAC. User can also breakdown a long
                       message into multiple Z66 messages with ascending sequence numbers to generate a
                       MAC.

    Notes:             Message Length: A onetime message that can be up to 224 characters (equal to 112
                       bytes when send as a hexadecimal string because 2 characters form 1 byte). Multiple
                       messages can have sequence numbers from 00 to 99. Thus the maximum capacity of
                       message Z66 is 22,400 characters (or 11,200 bytes in binary mode).
                       Multiple messages: When using multiple messages, [KeyId], [SessionKey] and
                       [SecKeyId] must be the same. [Message] must be a multiple of 8 characters (or 16
                       characters in binary mode), or else A10-P will generate a wrong MAC.
                       MAC algorithm: A10-P generates the TDES MAC according to ISO9797-1 algorithm 3.
                       (Padding with 0s. Initial vector = 0. Refer to Appendix A point 10 for the algorithm
                       details.)
                       Session Key: The value of the session key determines the usage of the specified
                       master keys.
                        Usage of 1st      Usage of 2nd     Value of session key   MAC Key
                        Key ID            Key ID
                        "K0"              N/A              Non-zero               Session key (decrypted by
                                                                                  master key specified by [KeyID]
                                                                                  using TDES ECB mode.)
                        "M3"              N/A              Zero                   Master key specified by
                        (mode G)                                                  [KeyId].
                                                                                  If the specified key is mode 'V',
                                                                                  this is for the MAC verification
                                                                                  and cannot be used to generate
                                                                                  the MAC for message Z66 .
                        "M1"              "M1"             Zero                   Master key specified by
                        (mode G)                                                  [KeyId] as left key, and
                                                                                  master key specified by
                                                                                  [SecKeyId] as right key.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field          Length                     Value and description

                    <STX>              1             <02>
                    Z66                3             Message ID
                    [PktType]          1             '4' = ASCII last or only packet.
                                                     '5' = ASCII first or middle of multiple packets.
                                                     '6' = Binary last or only packet.
                                                     '7' = Binary first or middle of multiple
                                                     packets.
                    [SeqNo]            2             '00' to '99'; for onetime only packet, set to 00.
                    [KeyId]            1             (Optional) Master key to use, range = 'B' to
                                                     'E'. If this    field is blank, the MAC master
                                                     key will be the selected key 0 ~ 9.
                    <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                    [SessionKey]       32            Session key to be decrypted bythe Master key
                                                     pointed by [KeyId].
                                                     Format: hexadecimal string.
                                                     This field should be all zeros if the selected
                                                     key is usage "M1" or "M3"
                    <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                    [SecKeyId]         1             (Optional) If first [KeyId] points to key with
                                                     "K0" or "M3" usage, this field should be
                                                     omitted.
                    <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                    [Message]          1-224         ASCII string or Hexadecimal string to be
                                                     MACed.
                    <ETX>              1             <03>
                    [LRC]              1             Checksum

    Message flow: (Onetime only packets)
                              HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message Z66 (type 4,6)          ->
                                                             <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-        <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                             <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-        Message Z67 (with MAC)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)

    Message flow: (Multiple packets)
                              HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message Z66
                                                    ->
                    (Seq'00' and types 5,7)
                                                             <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-        <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                             <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-        Message Z67 (with status code '1')
                    <ACK> / <NAK> /
                                                    ->
                    <EOT>
                    Message Z66
                                                    ->
                    (Seq'01'--'98', types 5,7)
                                                    <-        <ACK> / <NAK> / <EOT>
                                                    <-        Message Z67 (with status code '1')
                    .....................                       ........       .........................................
                    Message Z66
                    (Sequence# larger than          ->
                    last packet, types 4,6)
                                                    <-        <ACK> / <NAK> / <EOT>
                                                    <-        Message Z67 (with MAC)
                    <ACK> / <NAK> /
                                                    ->
                    <EOT>
```

```text
Section 10            Online Transaction Messages with Derived
Unique Key Per Transaction (DUKPT)
    The following messages are designed for the Derived Unique Key Per Transaction (DUKPT) key
    management scheme described in ANSI X9.24: 2009.

    message formats.

        90      Load First Initial Key Request
        91      Load Initial Key Response
```

Format summary: <STX>70[account]<FS>[DC Ind][amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable 21 to 40 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: Display prompt to invite user to input PIN. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT> - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 70 - PIN Entry Request (DUKPT)
    Format:            <STX>70[account]<FS>[DC Ind][amount]<FS>[timeout]<ETX>[LRC]
                       (request frame)

    Message length: Variable 21 to 40 bytes.
    Usage:             Display prompt to invite user to input PIN.
                       The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of following criteria happens:
                       - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71.
                       - [CAN] key pressed;            PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>.
                       - Message 72 received;          PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>
                       - Timed out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds); Acts as [CAN] key.
    NOTE:              User Interactive Sequence: The prompts on the LCD of each phase are as the
                       following.

                       After message 70 received                       Total Amount
                       (The displayed language can be selected)        $xxx.xx
                                                                       Enter PIN
                                                                       Push "ENTER"
                       After user press first digit                    PIN:
                       (Each * represents one digit)                   ****
                       If [ENTER] pressed                              PIN PAD
                                                                       PROCESSING
                                                                       (Until [CLR] pressed or new command
                                                                       received, can be turned off by message Z7)
                       If [CAN] pressed                                Transaction
                                                                       Cancelled
                                                                       (Return to idle prompt after 3 seconds, can be
                                                                       turned off by message Z7)

                       PIN length: According to the ANSI X9.8 standard, the length of the PIN should be
                       between 4 to 12 digits. If the user inputs less than 4 digits and then press ENTER, the
                       A10-P will beep for error and continue to wait for the user's input. When the user inputs
                       the 13th character, the A10-P will beep for error, conserves PIN characters 1st to 12th,
                       and waits for the ENTER.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length               Value and description

                    <STX>              1           <02>
                    70                 2           Message ID
                    [Account]          8..19       Primary account number
                    <FS>               1           <1C>, field separator
                    [DC Ind]           1           D/C: Debit/Credit Indicator
                    [Amount]           4 to 12     Amount of goods to be displayed on the
                                                   A10-P.
                                                   Accepts digit character ('0' ~ '9'), minus ('-'),
                                                   comma (',') and decimal point ('.')
                    <FS>               1           (optional) <1C>, field separator
                    [timeout]          1           (optional) ASCII characters from '1' to '9'
                                                   which is the timeout value in units of 30
                                                   seconds. Default = 9x30 = 270 seconds.
                    <ETX>              1           <03>
                    [LRC]              1           Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST             Direction                   A10-P

                    Message 70                      ->
                                                              <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                              <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                              Message 71 or
                                                    <-         <EOT> when [CAN] is pressed or
                                                              input times out.
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                              Display "PIN PAD
                                                              PROCESSING" until CLEAR is
                                                              pressed or another message
                                                              received.
```

[138] COMMAND 71 - Encrypted PIN Block Response (DUKPT)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Format summary: <STX>71<fkey flag>[Key Serial#][PIN][LRC] (response frame) <STX>71[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
Message length: Variable 32 to 42 bytes.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 71 - Encrypted PIN Block Response (DUKPT)
    Format:             <STX>71<fkey flag>[Key Serial#][PIN][LRC] (response frame)
                        <STX>71[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)

    Message length: Variable 32 to 42 bytes.
    Usage:              Send the entered PIN to the host in encrypted format.

    Message element:
                                       Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>             1             <02>
                   71                2             Message ID
                   [fkey flag]       1             Always '0' (This field is kept to retain the old
                                                   model compatibility.)
                   [Key Serial#]     10..20        Hex string representing key serial number
                                                   corresponding to the derived key.
                                                   The leading 'F' character may be stripped
                                                   (can be controlled by message 7A).
                                                   For DUKPT Z62 command: if null PIN is
                                                   entered, this field is empty.
                   [PIN]             16            Encrypted PIN block
                                                   Format: hexadecimal string.
                   <ETX>             1             <03>
                   [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Error codes:
                   Code                                   Meaning

                    '0'    Null Account input field.

                    '2'    Account number shorter than 8 digits.

                    '3'    Account number longer than 19 digits.

                    '4'    Account number have characters other than '0'-'9'.

                    '5'    [D/C ind] field not exists or format error.

                    '6'    Timeout value error.

                           Amount string format error originated from Message 70
                    '8'    PIN count, Accept Null PIN flag, and Prompt string format error
                           originated from Message Z62

                    'A'    No DUKPT key injected

                    'B'    Flash read/write error

                    'C'    Memory buffer allocation error

                    'F'    DUKPT operation limit (1 million) reached, program stops.

    Message flow:
        Refer to message70 (DUKPT).
```

[139] COMMAND 72 - PIN Entry Cancel
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 10 - Online Transaction Messages with DUKPT
Source PDF page(s): 284
Format summary: <STX>72<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 5 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: Cancel current transaction and return the A10-P to IDLE state. This message is used to interrupt the command in process. If A10-P receives message 72 while processing the user input such as swipe card, enter PIN or key-in data, it will respond with <EOT> to acknowledge that the operation is canceled.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text

     Format:              <STX>72<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

     Message length: Fixed 5 bytes.
     Usage:               Cancel current transaction and return the A10-P to IDLE state. This message is used
                          to interrupt the command in process. If A10-P receives message 72 while processing
                          the user input such as swipe card, enter PIN or key-in data, it will respond with <EOT>
                          to acknowledge that the operation is canceled.

     Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                           Field         Length               Value and description

                     <STX>             1             <02>
                     72                2             Message ID
                     <ETX>             1             <03>
                     [LRC]             1             Checksum

     Message flow:
                                           In Idle mode (normal condition)
                               HOST               Direction                   A10-P

                     Message 72                       ->
                                                                <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                      <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)

OR
                               In PIN/data entry mode (cancel/abort the session)
                               HOST               Direction                   A10-P

                     Message 72                       ->
                                                                <EOT> if the A10-P is in
                                                      <-         PIN/Data entry mode or waiting
                                                                for tapping/swiping card.
```

[144] COMMAND 90 - Load DUKPT Initial Key (Key Set 1)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 10 - Online Transaction Messages with DUKPT
Source PDF page(s): 291-292
Format summary: <STX>90[IPEK][KSN]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear Text) <STX>90[TR-31 Key Block]<ETX>[LRC] (Encrypted)
Message length: Fixed 57 bytes for clear text format; 109 (format B) or 149 (format D) bytes for the TR-31 format .
Purpose/usage summary: Load the first set of DUKPT initial key and serial number key to the A10-P. Consequent keys will be generated using the provided data. Clear text mode message 90 is only accepted when key injection mode is enabled by dual password authentication. Use it only in security-controlled environment with HSM. Refer to Appendix A Specification for detailed information. All existing keys in the A10-P will be erased when the first message 02 or 90 is sent in a new clear text key injection session.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 90 - Load DUKPT Initial Key (Key Set 1)
    Format:             <STX>90[IPEK][KSN]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear Text)
                        <STX>90[TR-31 Key Block]<ETX>[LRC] (Encrypted)

    Message length: Fixed 57 bytes for clear text format; 109 (format B) or 149 (format D) bytes for the
                        TR-31 format .
    Usage:              Load the first set of DUKPT initial key and serial number key to the A10-P. Consequent
                        keys will be generated using the provided data.
                        Clear text mode message 90 is only accepted when key injection mode is enabled by
                        dual password authentication. Use it only in security-controlled environment with HSM.
                        Refer to Appendix A Specification for detailed information.
                        All existing keys in the A10-P will be erased when the first message 02 or 90 is sent in
                        a new clear text key injection session.

    Note:               The following is the VISA required key serial number format:
                        4'F' characters, a 6-digit keyset identifier, with a 5-digit device ID, followed by a '0',
                        i.e. "FF FF kk kk kk dd dd d0 00 00"

    Message element:
                                          Clear text frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field         Length                Value and description

                   <STX>              1            <02>
                   90                 2            Message ID
                   [IPEK]             32           Initial PIN encryption key.
                                                   Format: hexadecimal string.
                   [KSN]              20           Key serial number used in generating
                                                   consequent keys.
                                                   Format: hexadecimal string.
                   <ETX>              1            <03>
                   [LRC]              1            Checksum

                                            Encrypted frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>             1              <02>
                    90                2              Message ID
                    [TR-31 Key        104 or         TR-31 key block with an optional header
                    Block]            144            block that contains the KSN.
                                                     See Appendix A for details.
                    <ETX>             1              <03>
                    [LRC]             1              Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST               Direction                   A10-P

                    Message 90                   ->
                                                                <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                 <-              <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                 <-              Message 91
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)              ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
    Example:
    Clear Text
    IPEK key to be loaded:                   ABCDEF0123456789FEDCBA9876543210
    KSN:                                     FFFF9876543210E00000
    The resulting 90 message :
    <STX>90ABCDEF0123456789FEDCBA9876543210FFFF9876543210E00000<ETX>[LRC]
    TR-31 Key Block
    Key Block Protecting Key:                AA55AA55AA55AA55 3434343434343434
    IPEK key to be loaded:                   ABCDEF0123456789 FEDCBA9876543210
    KSN:                                     FFFF9876543210E00000
    Key Block Header:                        B0104B1TX00N0100 KS18FFFF9876543210E00000
    Padded IPEK:                             0080 ABCDEF0123456789 FEDCBA9876543210 30111D18CC4C
    Derived KBEK:                            3C50E1B7962F2171DC8643F1D923ABF7
    Derived KBMK:                            46FBEEB64EAE26A650952DA4F6DD8325
    CMAC of (KBH + Padded key data), using KBMK:               93C3D5EBC6C407E4
    Use CMAC as IV to do TDES CBC encryption on padded key data, using KBEK:
    Encrypted key data:                      C86E6E3B24544F97C629FB0E0586A0285D35BA78E9B13FB
    Result:      <02>90B0104B1TX00N0100KS18FFFF9876543210E00000EC86E6E3B24544F9
    7C629FB0E0586A0285D35BA78E9B13FB93C3D5EBC6C407E4<03>
```

```text
                         [KCV]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: 6 or 15bytes.

    Message element:
                                          Response frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field           Length                Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    99                  2             Message ID
                    [status]            1             '0': Key not exists.
                                                      'F': Key exists and operative.
                                                      'E': Key inoperative.

                                                      always 'X'

                                                      always 'T'

                    [KCV]               6             (Optional), Hex string represents KCV
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Check value

    Message flow:
        Refer to message 98.

Section 11             Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages
The display prompts of the A10-P are built-in and digitally signed with the A10-P application to ensure it's
integrity and authenticity.
These commands have fixed display prompts:
-    Start IC card transaction (T11, T15, T33)
-    Start RFID transaction (T61, Q8)
-    Swipe Magnetic Stripe Card (Q1)
-    Combined card transaction (Q9, QK)
-    Standard PIN entry (70)
These commands have selectable display prompts:
-    Non-PIN data entry (Z42, Z50): The prompt can be selected from Appendix G (Z2/Z3 authenticated
     mode)
-    PIN entry with external prompts (Z60)
-    PIN entry with customized prompts (Z62)
The host application can also command A10-P to display any string on the LCD, but if the prompt string is not
MAC authenticated, the PIN entry or data entry function will be disabled.

Z2 / Z3 Authenticated mode with fixed prompt
    To enable messages Z42 and Z50, the user has to issue Z2 / Z3 messages with a prompt ID supported
    by the A10-P (See Appendix G). These prompts are verified to make sure users will not expose sensitive
    information (such as PIN) accidentally.

    For security reason, to issue the authenticated frame of Z2 / Z3 at the first time, the <SUB> flag is
    mandatory. After the Z2 authenticated mode is entered, the A10-P will accept two kinds of Z2 packet:
    1. Z2 packet in normal mode, without the <SUB> flagand contains only digits (0~9)
    2. Z2 packet in authenticated mode, without the <SUB> flag.
    For example, issuing Z2<GS>005<SUB> and Z2<GS>016 will show "PLEASE ENTER DRIVER
    LICENSE" on the screen.

Z2 / Z3 PIN entry mode with fixed prompt
    To enable message Z60, the user has to issue Z2 / Z3 messages with a prompt ID supported by the
    A10-P dedicated for PIN entry (See Appendix H). These prompts are verified to make sure users will not
    misunderstand the PIN entry request message as other non-sensitive data. Also prompt1 and prompt2 of
    message Z62 will be checked to see if they are listed in this prompt table. If not, the A10-P will reject
    message Z62.

    Messages other than Z2, Z3, Z42, Z50, and Z60, or any unsuccessful Z2 / Z3 messages (wrong prompt
    ID, format error, Z2 message including non decimal characters), will make the A10-P leaving the Z2 / Z3
    authenticated mode to avoid attack.
```

[152] COMMAND Z2 - Display String

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z2 - Display String
    Format:            <STX>Z2<SUB><VT>[LinePosition]<INV><US><DI>[string]<ETX><LRC>
                       (Request frame, normal)

    Message length: Variable, 6 to 70 bytes.
    Usage:             This message directs PIN pad to display specified string until following the situations:
                       - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad.
                       - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as
                       message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1).
    Notes:             This message can be used to display authenticated prompts for data entry if following
                       criteria are satisfied:
                       - If the specified string, after stripping non-alphabet characters (00h~40h, 5Bh~60h,
                       7Bh to 7Fh), is matching any one of the fixed prompts on the "Fixed prompts for Z2 /
                       Z3 authenticated mode", the string will be treated as "authenticated", and then
                       message Z42 and Z50 will be enabled.
                       - If PIN pad is already displaying unauthenticated message, <SUB> will be needed in
                       order to accept authenticated message.
                       - If <SUB> does not exist, and [string] contains digits ('0' to '9') only, the authenticated
                       state of previous Z2 will be preserved.

    Message element:
                               Z2 request frame (normal mode) (HOST to A10-P)
                        Field            Length                   Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   Z2                  2             Message ID
                   <SUB>               1             <1A> (optional)
                                                     If <SUB> exists, A10-P will clear the screen
                                                     contents.
                   <VT>                1             <0B>(Optional)
                                                     User can add this code to set line position
                                                     value as below.
                    [LinePosition]     2             (Optional) reply on <VT>
                                                     Line position value (ASCII) where show
                                                     message to display.
                   <INV>               1             (optional)
                                                     <11>:Inverse mode enable.
                                                     <12>:Inverse mode disable.
                   <US>                1             <1F>(Optional)
                   <DI>                1             (Optional)Rely on <US>
                                                     <81>: Left-alignment display,
                                                     <82> :Center-alignment display,
                                                     <83>: Right-alignment display.
                                                     <84>: Left-alignment with line display.
                                                     <85>: Center-alignment with line display.
                                                     <86>: Right-alignment with line display.
                   [string]            Var.          String to be displayed. The encoding can be
                                                     ASCII or UTF-8.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                    Message Z2                     ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           If format error, return <EOT>.
                                                   <-
                                                           Otherwise display the given string

    Examples:
    1. <STX>Z2<SUB>PLEASE ENTER PIN<ETX>
    2. PIN Pad will display "PLEASE ENTER PIN" on the screen, but since this message is not listed in the
          prompt table, Z42 will be restricted to function key, and Z50 will be rejected, and return to idle
          prompt.
    3. <STX>Z2<SUB>ENTER<ETX> -> <STX>Z002<ETX> -> <STX>Z2ACCOUNT NUMBER<ETX>
    4. PIN Pad will display "ENTER" at the first line, then display "ACCOUNT NUMBER" on the second line
          of screen. Message Z42 and Z50 will be allowed because both strings are listed on the prompt
          table (ID 024 and 001).
    5. <STX>Z2<SUB>ENTER <ETX> -> <STX>Z002<ETX> -> <STX>Z2YOUR PIN<ETX>
    6. The first Z2 is matching prompt ID 024 but the second does not match anything.
    7. In this case, PIN Pad will revoke the authentication previously enabled by the first Z2, thus Z42 will
          be restricted to function key, and Z50 will be rejected and back to the idle prompt.
    8. <STX>Z2<SUB>YOUR PIN <ETX>               -> <STX>Z002<ETX> -> <STX>Z2PLEASE<ETX>
    9. The first Z2 does not match any prompt ID, but the second Z2 matches ID 085.
    10. In this case, PIN Pad will refuse the second Z2 (response <EOT>) because it violates usage rule.
    11. PIN Pad will return to idle prompt, and Z42 / Z50 will be rejected because no valid prompt is
          displayed.
```

```text
                       prompts for non-PIN entry. So message Z42 will be restricted to function key, and Z50

                       BACK" in three lines. Since line 1 matches ID 016, line 2 contains all digits, and line 3
                       matches ID 030, this message will be evaluated as authenticated for non-PIN entry.
                       Message Z42 and Z50 will be allowed.

                       rejected.

                       #<ETX>

                       ENTER ID #" in three lines. Line 1 matches ID 031 after stripping non-alphabet
                       characters, line 2 and line 3 also match other IDs. So this message will be evaluated
                       as authenticated, Z42 / Z50 will be allowed.

    5.                 <STX>Z32ENTER SSN<FS>OR PHONE #<ETX>
                       PIN Pad will reject this message (response <EOT>) because it tries to enter the
                       authenticated display mode without clearing screen.
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 11 - Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages
Source PDF page(s): 312-313
Format summary: <STX>Z3[op][id1]<FS>[id2]...[id7]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>Z3[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable 9 to 33 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message directs PIN pad to display up to seven authenticated prompts in rotation. The display changes prompts in 3-second intervals until the following situations: - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad. - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1). This message does not have <SUB> character because it will always clear the screen.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z3 - Display Line Prompts (Fixed Prompt ID)
    Format:             <STX>Z3[op][id1]<FS>[id2]...[id7]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                        <STX>Z3[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable 9 to 33 bytes.
    Usage:              This message directs PIN pad to display up to seven authenticated prompts in rotation.
                        The display changes prompts in 3-second intervals until the following situations:
                        - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad.
                        - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as
                        message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1).
                        This message does not have <SUB> character because it will always clear the screen.

    Message element:
              Z3 request frame (authenticated mode or PIN entry mode) (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field         Length                  Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   Z3                 2             Message ID
                   [op]               1             Defines which prompt table to be applied for
                                                    search:
                                                    <1D> (GS): data entry (non-PIN) prompt.
                                                    <1E> (RS): PIN entry prompt.
                                                    (In these 2 modes, A10-P will clear the screen
                                                    content.)
                   [Prompt ID1]       3             Prompt ID that corresponds to the fixed
                                                    prompt provided by the A10-P.
                                                    Decimal string: 001 ~ 999.
                   <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                   [Prompt            3             Prompt ID that corresponds to the fixed
                   ID2..7]                          prompt provided by the A10-P.
                                                    Decimal string: 001 ~ 999.
                                                    Note. <FS> is required between
                                                    prompt IDs.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                         Z3 response frame (authenticated mode) (A10-P to HOST)
                         Field            Length                Value and description

                    <STX>               1             <02>
                    Z3                  2             Message ID
                    [status]            1             '0': OK
                                                      '1': Prompt ID not supported.
                    <ETX>               1             <03>
                    [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST               Direction                      A10-P

                    Message Z3                         ->
                                                                 <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                       <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                                 <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                                 Message Z3
                                                       <-
                                                                   (response frame)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                    ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                                 Display string
                                                       <-
                                                                 <EOT> (if received <ACK>)
```

[157] COMMAND Z3 - Display Line Prompts with Authentication Code
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 11 - Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages

Format summary: <STX>Z3<FS>[KeyID][MAC][count][op][prompt1]<FS>[prompt2..7] <SUB><ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>Z3[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: This message directs PIN pad to display up to seven MAC authenticated prompts in rotation. The display changes prompts in 3-second intervals until the following situations: - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad. - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1). White spaces, punctuation marks and digits are excluded. - <FS> character if exists. - <SUB> character if exists. Padding '0' (0x30) to the m...

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z3 - Display Line Prompts with Authentication Code
    Format:            <STX>Z3<FS>[KeyID][MAC][count][op][prompt1]<FS>[prompt2..7]
                       <SUB><ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                       <STX>Z3[status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:             This message directs PIN pad to display up to seven MAC authenticated prompts in
                       rotation. The display changes prompts in 3-second intervals until the following
                       situations:
                       - User presses [CAN] key on the keypad.
                       - PIN pad receives another message that changes the display contents (such as
                       message 70), or returns to the idle prompt (message Z1).
                       The MAC value is calculated from the following data concatenated as byte array:
                       - [op] field.
                       - All alphabets ('A' to 'Z', 'a' to 'z') in the [string] field. White spaces, punctuation marks
                       and digits are excluded.
                       - <FS> character if exists.
                       - <SUB> character if exists.
                       Padding '0' (0x30) to the multiple of 8 bytes.
                       The algorithm is ISO 9797-1 algorithm 3.

    Note:              1. If Z3 (string with MAC) is used in combination with Z3 (fixed prompt), their [op]
                       character (GS / RS) must be the same; otherwise A10-P will reject the secondary Z3.
                       2. A10-P will temporarily turn off the date/timescreen for the first Z2 message it
                       received. The A10-P will return to the idle mode and show the date/time screen after
                       the following possible scenarios: The key entry message command is finished (Z42,
                       Z50 or Z60), the [CAN] is pressed, or the message 72 is received.

    Message element:
                                  Z3 with MAC, request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field          Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   Z3                  2             Message ID
                   <FS>                1             <1C>, field separator.
                   [KeyID]             1             'B' ~ 'E', key to verify the MAC value. The
                                                     specified key must have usage 'M3' and mode
                                                     'V'.
                   [MAC]               8             Message authentication code of the following
                                                     message (including <SUB> if exists).
                   [count]             1             '1' ~ '7', number of following prompts.
                   [op]                1             <GS> (0x1D) for Non-PIN entry.
                                                     <RS> (0x1E) for PIN entry.
                   [prompt1]           Var           First string to be displayed. (ASCII or
                                                     UTF-8).
                   <FS>                1             <1C>, field separator
                   [prompt N]          Var.          Second to last string to be displayed. Each
                                                     prompt is separated by a <FS>.
                   <SUB>               1             <1A> (optional)
                                                      If <SUB> exists, A10-P will clear     the
                                                     screen contents.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

                                  Z3 with MAC, response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field          Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   Z3                  2             Message ID
                   [status]            1             '0': OK
                                                     '1': MAC key ID error (out of 'B'~'E').
                                                     '2': MAC key attribute error.
                                                     '3': MAC value error.
                                                     '4': Packet format error.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                    A10-P

                    Message Z3                     ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Message Z3
                                                   <-
                                                            (response frame)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Display string
                                                   <-
                                                           <EOT> (if received <ACK>)

Example to use Z2 / Z3 with Authencation Code.
    [Example 1]
            a. Use message 02 (ANSI TR31 frame) to load the following key to position 'B':
                  BCDE90123456789ABCDE90123456789A, Usage = M3, Mode = V.
            b. Assume we want to clear the screen and display the following string for PIN entry: "AMOUNT
                  123456.78 ENTER YOUR PIN".
            c.    The data for MAC generation ('A' to 'Z', 'a' to 'z' and ISO8859-15 high page characters from
                  0xBC to 0xFF, padded with ASCII 0):
                  <RS>AMOUNTENTERYOURPIN<SUB>0000
                     1E414D4F554E54454E544552594F555250494E1A30303030
                  The white spaces and digits are not counted into the MAC. This feature enables the acquirer
                  to issue PIN entry prompts with different amounts, but keeps the same MAC value.
            d. Use the key specified in step a to calculate ISO9797-1 algorithm 3 MAC.
                  The result is: C51401D727D761E2.
                  Take leftmost 4 bytes as MAC value: C51401D7.
            e. Send <02>Z2<1C>BC51401D7<1E>AMOUNT 123456.78 ENTER YOUR PIN<1A><03> to
                  A10-P, Then message Z60 can be issued to request PIN entry.
            f.    Send <02>Z2<1C>BC51401D7 <1A>AMOUNT 123.45 ENTER YOUR PIN<03> to A10-P to
                  see the same MAC applies to different amounts.

    [Example 2]
     1.    Use message 02 (ANSI TR31 frame) to load the following key to position 'B':
           6AC292FAA1315B4D8234B3A3D7D5933A, Usage = M3, Mode = V.
     2.    Assume we want to clear the screen and display for the non-PIN entry: "MESSAGE ONE 1.0" and
           "MESSAGE TWO 2.0".
     3.    The data for the MAC generation (padded with ASCII 0):
           <GS>MESSAGEONE<FS>MESSAGETWO<SUB>0
                 1D4D4553534147454F4E451C4D45535341474554574F1A30
     4.    Use the key specified in    step 1 to calculate the ISO9797-1 algorithm 3 MAC.
           Take the leftmost 4 bytes as the MAC value: 22C0BAD9.
     5.    Send <02>Z3<1C>B22C0BAD92<1D>MESSAGE ONE 1.0<1C>MESSAGE TWO 2.0<1A><03> to
           the A10-P.
```

[158] COMMAND Z42 - Read Key Code
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 11 - Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages
Source PDF page(s): 318
Format summary: <STX>Z42[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable 7 to 9 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: Once A10-P receives this command, it begins polling the functional key array until time out happens as specified in [timeout]. If A10-P receives the Z2 / Z3 authenticated frame before message Z42, it will return any key pressed by the user as ASCII key codes via message Z43. Else it will return only the function key codes (F1, F2, F3, CAN, CLR, ENTER), and reject the numerical keys (0 to 9). Multiple key presses or combined key presses will be discarded. Abort input: Issue message 72 to abort the operation.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z42 - Read Key Code
    Format:            <STX>Z42[timeout]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable 7 to 9 bytes.
    Usage:             Once A10-P receives this command, it begins polling the functional key array until time
                       out happens as specified in [timeout].
                       If A10-P receives the Z2 / Z3 authenticated frame before message Z42, it will return
                       any key pressed by the user as ASCII key codes via message Z43. Else it will return
                       only the function key codes (F1, F2, F3, CAN, CLR, ENTER), and reject the numerical
                       keys (0 to 9). Multiple key presses or combined key presses will be discarded.
                       Abort input: Issue message 72 to abort the operation.
    Note:              Z2/Z3 required: Because Z42 will not show any message to prompt the user operation,
                       Z2 or Z3 should be issued before this command, or A10-P will send out <EOT> and
                       stops.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field         Length               Value and description

                    <STX>              1           <02>
                    Z42                3           Message ID
                    [timeout]          1 to 3      ASCII character from 1 to 255, for example
                                                   "10" means 10 seconds of timeout.
                    <ETX>              1           <03>
                    [LRC]              1           Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST             Direction                  A10-P

                    Message Z2 or Z3                ->
                                                              <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                              <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                              Show prompt message
                    Message Z42                     ->
                                                              <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                              <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                    <-         Message Z43
                    <ACK>/<NAK>/<EOT>               ->
```

[160] COMMAND Z50 - String Entry Request
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 11 - Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages
Source PDF page(s): 320-322
Format summary: <STX>Z50[echo flag][timeout][max entry]<US><DI>[<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable 10 to 12 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message requests a string of key inputs to be entered from the PIN pad. The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of the following criteria happens: - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71. - [CAN] key pressed; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>. - Message 72 received; PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT> - Times out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds).

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Z50 - String Entry Request
    Format:            <STX>Z50[echo flag][timeout][max entry]<US><DI>[<ETX>[LRC]
                       (request frame)

    Message length: Variable 10 to 12 bytes.
    Usage:             This message requests a string of key inputs to be entered from the PIN pad.
                       The PIN pad polls for keypad inputs until one of the following criteria happens:
                       - [ENTER] key pressed; PIN pad validates input and sends message 71.
                       - [CAN] key pressed;         PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>.
                       - Message 72 received;       PIN pad aborts PIN entry and sends <EOT>
    -                  Times out (session or single key idle for 60 seconds).
    Note:-             To enable Z50 input session, send message Z2 or Z3 authenticated for data entry, (Z2
                       / Z3 with <GS> operand). Otherwise PIN pad will send <EOT> and return to idle state.
    -                  If input character count reaches [max entry], the PIN pad will stop collecting key input
                       and make error beeps. User can press [ENTER], [CLR], or [CAN].Request the user to
                       input a string from the keypad.
                       A10-P will wait for the keypad input and store the alphabet data string into the internal
                       buffer. The maximum length of the internal buffer is up to 49 characters.
                       User can press [CLR] to clear the input buffer and start over the input , or press [CAN]
                       to cancel the input.
                       Using [0] and [MENU] for the period symbol and white space entries.
                       .Abort input: Issue message 72 to abort the operation.
    Note:              A message Z2 or Z3 with authenticated frame must be issued before sending message
                       Z50. Otherwise the A10-P will refuse to execute.

    Message element:
                                        Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field        Length                  Value and description

                   <STX>            1             <02>
                   Z50              3             Message ID
                   [echo flag]      1             '0': echo input as '*'
                                                  '1': echo input as is
                                                  '2': do not echo
                   [timeout]        3             ASCII characters from 1 to 255 to set the
                                                  timeout for each keypress. For example "010"
                                                  means 10 seconds of timeout after the last
                                                  keypress.
                   [max entry]      1 or 2        (optional) Maximum entry counts.
                                                  Range from 00 to 49 (or 0 to 49)
                   <US>             1             <1F>(Optional)
                   <DI>             1             (Optional)Rely on <US>
                                                  <81>: Left-alignment display,
                                                  <82> :Center-alignment display,
                                                  <83>: Right-alignment display.
                                                  <84>: Left-alignment with line display.
                                                  <85>: Center-alignment with line display.
                                                  <86>: Right-alignment with line display.
                   <ETX>            1             <03>
                   [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                    Message Z2 or Z3               ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Show the prompt message
                    Message Z50                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Message Z51
                                                   <-       (or <EOT> when input is
                                                           cancelled)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

```text
Section 12            ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading
Messages
    Messages listed in this section are used to:
    - Access IC card, SAM card directly (EMV power-up, power-down, APDU exchange.)
    - Read magnetic stripe card.
    - Read contactless smart card and output MSR track equivalent data.
    NOTE: By default, the MSR function is turned off until the user issues the Q4 command to enable it.

    I00 ~ I07: IC card manipulation.
    I11 ~ I17: SAM card manipulation.
    Q1 ~ Q7: Read magnetic stripe card and output control.
    Q8 ~ QJ: Read contactless smard card (MSR emulation) and output control.
    QK: Multiple interface (MSR, ICC, Contactless) card detection and reading.
    81: MSR data output
    83: Contactless MSR emulation data output.

    Depend on the firmware configuration (PTS only or PTS + SRED), the clear text data output is not
    available.

    PTS Only Configuration
    - I01 ~ I06 (ICC manipulation) is available.
    - Q6 (MSR operation control) does NOT support options for data encryption.
    - 81 (MSR card data) outputs clear text track data.
    - 83 (Contactless card data) outputs clear text track equivalent data.

    PTS + SRED Configuration
    - I01 ~ I06 (ICC manipulation) is NOT available.
    - Q6 (MSR operation control) supports data encryption (MK/SK and DUKPT) option.
    - QD (Contactless)
    - 81 (MSR card data) outputs encrypted (and optionally obfuscated) track data.
    - 83 (Contactless card data) outputs encrypted (and optionally obfuscated) track equivalent data.
```

[165] COMMAND I00 - Query Primary Smart Card Presence
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 328
Format summary: <STX>I00<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>I00[response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Fixed 6 bytes (request frame) / 7 bytes (response frame).
Purpose/usage summary: Upon receiving a query card packet, A10-P will check whether the card is present in the primary card reader or not. If a card exists in the reader, A10-P will reply with the code 'F'. Otherwise, the code '0' is used instead.

```text

    Format:               <STX>I00<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                          <STX>I00[response]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Usage:                Upon receiving a query card packet, A10-P will check whether the card is present in
                          the primary card reader or not. If a card exists in the reader, A10-P will reply with the
                          code 'F'. Otherwise, the code '0' is used instead.

    Message element:
                                           Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field          Length                Value and description

                    <STX>              1             <02>
                    I00                3             Message ID
                    <ETX>              1             <03>
                    [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                          Field          Length                Value and description

                    <STX>              1             <02>
                    I00                3             Message ID
                    [Response]         1             0: Smart card not exists.
                                                     F: Smart card exists
                    <ETX>              1             <03>
                    [LRC]              1             Checksum

    Message flow:
```

[171] COMMAND I08 - Smart Card Offline PIN Verification (EMV)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 334-335
Format summary: <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear-text mode) <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<FS>RSA public Exp]<FS>[RSA public Modulus]<ETX>[LRC] (Cipher-text mode)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: User could apply message I01 ~ I06 to implement his EMV transaction flow. In EMV transaction flow, user could apply this message to implement the offline PIN verification operation defined by EMV Co. User applies this message to make PIN pad ask cardholder enter his PIN on PIN pad and then PIN pad will send the PIN block (in clear -text or cipher-text) to IC card. For secure consideration, user will not get any information about cardholder's PIN, user can only get the PIN verification result from PIN pad. In PIN verification operation, PIN pad will issue "Get Challenge" command to get random number from smart card for PIN encryption.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message I08 - Smart Card Offline PIN Verification (EMV)
    Format:           <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear-text mode)
                      <STX>I08[Mode]<FS>[Prompt & Amount]<FS>RSA public Exp]<FS>[RSA
                      public Modulus]<ETX>[LRC] (Cipher-text mode)
    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:            User could apply message I01 ~ I06 to implement his EMV transaction flow. In EMV
                      transaction flow, user could apply this message to implement the offline PIN
                      verification operation defined by EMV Co. User applies this message to make PIN pad
                      ask cardholder enter his PIN on PIN pad and then PIN pad will send the PIN block (in
                      clear -text or cipher-text) to IC card. For secure consideration, user will not get any
                      information about cardholder's PIN, user can only get the PIN verification result from
                      PIN pad. In PIN verification operation, PIN pad will issue "Get Challenge" command to
                      get random number from smart card for PIN encryption.
    NOTE: This message is not available in the PTS + SRED configuration.

    Message element:
                                        Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field        Length                Value and description

                    <STX>              1            <02>
                    I08                3            Message ID
                    [Mode]             1            0: Clear PIN mode
                                                    1: Cipher PIN mode
                    <FS>               1            <1C>
                    [Prompt       &    var          ASCII string. The data in this filed is used to
                    Amount]                         present to cardholder. The length of this filed
                                                    could be 1 ~ 32. Ex. Amount: 12.345
                                                    PIN pad will append messages on line 3 and
                                                    4 to inform user to make a confirmation.
                    <FS>               1            <1C> (Optional, if Mode is 1)
                    [RSA public        1            (Optional, if Mode is 1)
                    Exp]                            1: 3
                                                    2: 2^16 + 1
                    <FS>               1            (Optional, if Mode is 1)
                                                    <1C>
                    [RSA public        Var.         Hex string. RSA modulus. (Optional, if
                    Modulus]                        Mode is 1)
                    <ETX>              1            <03>
                    [LRC]              1            Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                A10-P

                    Message I08                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Communication with card.
                                                   <-
                                                           Message I09 or I0F
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

```text
                          recommended that terminal applies next CVM if get response equal to 'C', 'E', and 'S',
                          terminates EMV transaction if get response equal to 'D' and 'F'.

                          Field          Length                Value and description

                    I09                3             Message ID
                     [Response]            1          ASCII character.
                                                      A: PIN is verified successfully.
                                                      C: Cardholder bypass PIN.
                                                      D: Communication failed (with smart card).
                                                      E: Exceed PIN try limit
                                                      S: No random number from

        Refer to message I08.
```

[173] COMMAND I0F - Error Codes
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 337
Format summary: <STX>I0F[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)
Message length: Fixed 8 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This message contains the error code indicating what's going on with the erroneous situation. The error code list is as follows: "01" - ATR error or NO smart card. "02" - APDU data length is not enough. "03" - ICC/SAM card not powered yet, use I01 first. "04" - The alphanumeric value in the APDU data unit is out of range. "05" - Current smart card reader doesn't have card in. "06" - Smart card interface switch failed. "07" - A10-P Smart card module timed out. "08" - Smart card APDU command failed. "09" - This parameter is not supported by A10-P. "0A" - This unit does not have the corresponding peripheral (ICC reader or SAM).

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message I0F - Error Codes
    Format:               <STX>I0F[error code]<ETX>[LRC] (error frame)

    Message length: Fixed 8 bytes.
    Usage:                This message contains the error code indicating what's going on with the erroneous
                          situation. The error code list is as follows:
                          "01" - ATR error or NO smart card.
                          "02" - APDU data length is not enough.
                          "03" - ICC/SAM card not powered yet, use I01 first.
                          "04" - The alphanumeric value in the APDU data unit is out of range.
                          "05" - Current smart card reader doesn't have card in.
                          "06" - Smart card interface switch failed.
                          "07" - A10-P Smart card module timed out.
                          "08" - Smart card APDU command failed.
                          "09" - This parameter is not supported by A10-P.
                          "0A" - This unit does not have the corresponding peripheral (ICC reader or SAM).

    Message element:
                                            Error frame (A10-P to HOST)
                           Field         Length                Value and description

                    <STX>               1            <02>
                    I0F                 3            Message ID
                    [Error code]        2            Error code
                    <ETX>               1            <03>
                    [LRC]               1            Checksum

    Message flow:
        Refer to I00 to I07.
```

[180] COMMAND Q1 - Start MSR Reading
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 344
Format summary: <STX>Q1<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 5 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: The A10-P arms the MSR for read and displays the "SWIPE CARD" prompt on its LCD until a card is swiped through the reader slot, or message Z1 (reset state) is received, or message 72 is received, or the CAN key is pressed. After the magnetic stripe card is swiped, A10-P will collect and decode the card data and do formatting designated by message Q6. The data will be output to the host by message 81 and the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" message is displayed.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Q1 - Start MSR Reading
    Format:              <STX>Q1<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 5 bytes.
    Usage:               The A10-P arms the MSR for read and displays the "SWIPE CARD" prompt on its
                         LCD until a card is swiped through the reader slot, or message Z1 (reset state) is
                         received, or message 72 is received, or the CAN key is pressed.
                         After the magnetic stripe card is swiped, A10-P will collect and decode the card data
                         and do formatting designated by message Q6. The data will be output to the host by
                         message 81 and the "PIN PAD PROCESSING" message is displayed.
    NOTE: For first time use of the A10-P, issue message Q4 to enable the MSR tracks before issuing Q1.

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length               Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    Q1                2             Message ID
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST               Direction                  A10-P

                    Message Q1                       ->
                                                               "SWIPE CARD" displayed on the
                                                               LCD
                                                               <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                               <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                               (User swipes the magnetic card)
                                                     <-
                                                               Message 81
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     ->
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)
```

[184] COMMAND Q5 - Set MSR Retry Count
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 348
Format summary: <STX>Q5[RetryCount]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
Purpose/usage summary: This command sets a retry count for the MSR swipe initiated by message Q1. If A10-P cannot decode any data from the latest swipe, the retry count is larger than "0", and the timeout has not reached yet, the A10-P will show "BAD READ" on the LCD and waits for the next swipe, until times out or the retry counter reaches the maximum. This setting will be kept in the battery powered memory and is effective all the time.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message Q5 - Set MSR Retry Count
    Format:              <STX>Q5[RetryCount]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Fixed 6 bytes.
    Usage:               This command sets a retry count for the MSR swipe initiated by message Q1.
                         If A10-P cannot decode any data from the latest swipe, the retry count is larger than "0",
                         and the timeout has not reached yet, the A10-P will show "BAD READ" on the LCD
                         and waits for the next swipe, until times out or the retry counter reaches the maximum.
                         This setting will be kept in the battery powered memory and is effective all the time.

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length                Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    Q5                2             Message ID
                    RetryCnt          1             '0' to '9', MSR retry count.
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                               HOST              Direction                   A10-P

                    Message Q5                       ->
                                                               <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                               <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                               Save the setting or display an error
                                                               message    if the RetryCnt is out of
                                                               range.
```

```text
                  [control]              1            '0': Ready for next packet, [DOL] is ignored.
                                                      '1':Get contactless tag data. (optional)

                  <ETX>                  1            <03>

                                                           (if pkt No. is not total pkt )

                    Message QI0                    ->
                                                           <ACK> (Good LRC)

                                                           <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                           Get Contactless Tag Data
                                                           Response.
                                                   <-
                                                           Message QJ
                                                           (if pkt No. is not total pkt )

                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                    ..............                         .....     ..............
                                                           Get Contactless Tag Data
                                                           Response.
```
