[197] COMMAND QJ - Get Contactless Tag Data Response
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 366-367
Format summary: <STX>QJ[Pkt NO.][Total Pkt]<FS>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame) <STX>QJ[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame).
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: The message contains the contactless tag data to be sent to the host as a response.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message QJ - Get Contactless Tag Data Response
    Format:             <STX>QJ[Pkt NO.][Total Pkt]<FS>[DO]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
                        <STX>QJ[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame).

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:              The message contains the contactless tag data to be sent to the host as a response.

    Message element:
                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                        Field            Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   QJ                  2             Message ID
                   [Pkt NO.]           1             Decimal. Packet sequence number (1 ~ 9).
                   [Total Pkt]         1              Decimal. Total packets (1~9).
                   <FS>                1             <1C>
                   [DO]                Var.          Data Object, each data object is expressed in
                                                     TLV format with an <FS> delimit in each
                                                     field, and <SUB> is used to delimit each
                                                     object. For example:
                                                     9F12<FS>0F<FS>CREDITO DE
                                                     VISA<SUB>9A<FS>06<FS>050806<SUB>
                                                     .......
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    OR
                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                        Field            Length                Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   QJ                  3             Message ID
                   [Status]            1             F: Query failed or data empty.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
                   [LRC]               1             Checksum

    Data Object:
    A10-P will return series of data objects that list on the [DOL] field in the message QJ with TLV (tag ||
    length|| value) format as below:

    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value] <SUB>
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value] <SUB>
    ........
    [EMV Tag Number (2 ~ 8 byte)] <FS> [Length (2byte)] <FS> [Value].

    Note:       When A10-P responds these data objects, it will convert these values from binary value to
    hex decimal string if the data object format is "b" or "cn" or "n".

    Message flow:
        Refer to message QI.
```

[198] COMMAND QK - Start Multiple Interface Detection (MSR, ICC, PCD)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 368-369
Format summary: <STX>QK<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>QK[Res][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Fixed 5 bytes for request, 6 or 7 bytes for response.
Purpose/usage summary: This command will poll MSR/ICC/PCD, until detected, 72 message or Z1 message (reset state) received or CAN key pressed. If A10-P detects MSR/ICC/PCD, it will send the message to the host as a response. If Res is '1', then send message Q1 to read the track data. If Res is '2', then send message T11 to start an ICC EMV transaction. If Res is '3', then send message Q8 to read the track equivalent data or send message T61 to start a PCD EMV transaction.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message QK - Start Multiple Interface Detection (MSR, ICC, PCD)
    Format:             <STX>QK<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                        <STX>QK[Res][Err Msg]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Fixed 5 bytes for request, 6 or 7 bytes for response.
    Usage:              This command will poll MSR/ICC/PCD, until detected, 72 message or Z1 message
                        (reset state) received or CAN key pressed.
                        If A10-P detects MSR/ICC/PCD, it will send the message to the host as a response.
                        If Res is '1', then send message Q1 to read the track data.
                        If Res is '2', then send message T11 to start an ICC EMV transaction.
                        If Res is '3', then send message Q8 to read the track equivalent data or send message
                        T61 to start a PCD EMV transaction.

    Message element:
                                          Request fame (HOST to A10-P)
                        Field           Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   QK                 2             Message ID
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                          Response fame (A10-P to HOST)
                        Field           Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   QK                 2             Message ID
                   [Res]              1             '0' : Fatal Error.
                                                    '1' : Detect MSR.
                                                    '2' : Detect ICC.
                                                    '3' : Detect PCD.
                   [Err Msg]          1             (optional), If Res is '0'.
                                                    '0' : Enable MSR fail.
                                                    '1' : Get ICC status fail.
                                                    '2' : Enable antenna fail.
                                                    '3' : Cancel polling.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                                HOST            Direction                A10-P

                    Message QK
                                                    ->
                    (request)
                                                            <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                    <-       <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                            <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                            Message QK
                                                    <-
                                                            (response)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                 ->
                    <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
```

[199] COMMAND 81 - MSR Card Data
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 12 - ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 370-377
Format summary: <STX>81.[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<FS> [BIN record]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear text / encrypted data) <STX>81$[IV]<ETX>[LRC] (MK/SK Initial Vector) <STX>81#[KSN] <ETX>[LRC] (DUKPT Key serial number) <STX>81@[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<FS> [BIN record]<ETX>[LRC] (Obfuscated track data) <STX>81&[Check PAN result 1]<FS>[Check PAN result 2]<ETX>[LRC] (PAN Validation result)
Message length: Variable, depending on the card image in buffer.
Purpose/usage summary: A10-P uses this message to send back the information read from the last card swipe. The card data is transmitted in ASCII string as defined by the ISO 7811 format specification. Under different types, the A10-P returns the card data in different formats. If message Q4 is issued and the A10-P is set as track 2 only, the returned message 81 will only contain track 2 data without a field separator. For PTS only firmware, the track data is always in clear text. For PTS + SRED firmware, the track data will be encrypted, except those PAN number listed in the BIN exception table. Refer to "account data security" for the obfuscation and encryption...

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message 81 - MSR Card Data
    Format:           <STX>81.[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<FS>
                      [BIN record]<ETX>[LRC] (Clear text / encrypted data)
                      <STX>81$[IV]<ETX>[LRC]
                           (MK/SK Initial Vector)
                      <STX>81#[KSN] <ETX>[LRC]
                           (DUKPT Key serial number)
                      <STX>81@[trk1 data]<FS>[trk2 data]<FS>[trk3 data]<FS>
                      [BIN record]<ETX>[LRC]
                           (Obfuscated track data)
                      <STX>81&[Check PAN result 1]<FS>[Check PAN result 2]<ETX>[LRC]
                           (PAN Validation result)
    Message length: Variable, depending on the card image in buffer.
    Usage:            A10-P uses this message to send back the information read from the last card swipe.
                      The card data is transmitted         in ASCII string as defined by the ISO 7811 format
                      specification. Under different types, the A10-P returns the card data in different formats.
                      If message Q4 is issued and the A10-P is set as track 2 only, the returned message 81
                      will only contain track 2 data without    a field separator.
                      For PTS only firmware, the track data is always in clear text. For PTS + SRED
                      firmware, the track data will be encrypted, except those PAN number listed in the BIN
                      exception table. Refer to "account data security" for the obfuscation and encryption
                      algorithms. If encryption fails, A10-P will return NULL track data.
                      If BIN record search is successful, the BIN will be attached in the end of the magnetic
                      strip card data.

    Notes:              Packets for different operation mode:
                        Please refer to message Q6 for operation type information.
                        Mode 0 and 2             1 Packet      PIN pad will only return one "81." message., if swiped card
                        (Clear text)                           is gift card, [trk2 data] would be replaced by gift card
                                                               number which is Prepaid gift card standard defined by First
                                                               Data Corporation.
                        Mode 1, and 3            2 Packet      PIN pad returns "81$" for MK/SK initial vector, then "81."
                        (MK/SK encrypted)                      for encrypted card data.
                        Mode 4 and 5:            4 Packets     PIN pad returns "81$" for MK/SK initial vector then
                        (MK/SK encrypted                       returns "81." for encrypted card data, then returns "81@"
                        + obfuscated)                          for obfuscated data, and finally returns "81&" to indicate if
                                                               the PAN in track 1 / track 2 is valid.
                        Mode 6 and 7:            2 Packets     PIN pad returns "81#" for DUKPT key serial number, then
                        (DUKPT encrypted)                      "81." for encrypted card data.
                        Mode 8 and 9:            4 Packets     PIN pad first returns "81#" for DUKPT key serial number,
                        (DUKPT encrypted                       then returns "81." for encrypted card data, then returns
                        + obfuscated)                          "81@" for obfuscated data, and finally returns "81&" to
                                                               indicate if the PAN in track 1 / track 2 is valid.

    Message element:
                                             (Clear text / encrypted data)
                         Field          Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>                1           <02>
                   81                   2           Message ID
                   .                    1           <2E>
                   [trk1]               N           Variable length, data of track 1. (*)
                   <FS>                 1           <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [trk2]               N           Variable length, data of track 2.
                   <FS>                 1           <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [trk3]               N           Variable length, data of track 3. (*)
                   <FS>                 1           Optional
                                                    <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [BIN record]         16          Optional
                                                    Hex string. If BIN processing is enabled
                                                    and a match record is found.
                   <ETX>                1           <03>
                   [LRC]                1           Checksum
                            (*): If MSR is set to Tk2 output only, this field is omitted

                                                  (MK/SK Initial Vector)
                          Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   81                 2             Message ID
                   $                  1             <24>
                   [IV]               16            Hex string. MK/SK initial vector.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                           (DUKPT Key Serial Number)
                          Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   81                 2             Message ID
                   #                  1             <23>
                   [KSN]              20            Hex string. DUKPT key serial number.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                                 (Obfuscated data)
                          Field         Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   81                 2             Message ID
                   @                  1             <40>
                   [trk1]             N             Variable length, data of track 1. PAN is
                                                    partially masked. (*)
                   <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [trk2]             N             Variable length, data of track 2. PAN is
                                                    partially masked.
                   <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [trk3]             N             Variable length, data of track 3. (*)
                   <FS>               1             Optional
                                                    <1C>, field separator. (*)
                   [BIN record]       16            Optional
                                                    Hex string. If BIN processing is enabled
                                                    and a match record is found.
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum
                            (*): If MSR is set to Tk2 output only, this field is omitted

                         Field          Length                Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>

                    &                 1             <26>

                                                    '0': Invalid PAN
                                                    '1': Valid PAN
                                                    '2': No PAN exists
                    <FS>              1             <1C>, field separator. (*)
                    [RES2]            1             PAN checking result of track 2.
                                                    '0': Invalid PAN
                                                    '1': Valid PAN
                                                    '2': No PAN exists
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum

                                                               <EOT> (after 3 NAKs)
                                                               (User swipes the magnetic card)
                                                     <-
                                                               Message 81 (81.)
                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     ->
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)

                           Clear Text of MK/SK encrypted data (Mode 0, 1, 2, 3)
                            HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                   Message Q1 or Q9                ->
                                                           "SWIPE CARD" displayed on
                                                           LCD
```

[203] COMMAND BB - Screen Saver Setting
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 13 - Display Functionality Messages
Source PDF page(s): 383-384

Purpose/usage summary: A10-P has the screen saver functionality. This message is used to select one of screen savers and set the waiting time. Message BD is called to enable the screen saver. While A10-P is in idle (without receiving messages, keystrokes, or screen touch) passing the period of time specified in [Waiting Time], the screen saver will be activated. The minimum waiting time should be greater than or equal to 5 seconds. Screen saver - Jpeg Show: display all jpeg pictures in rotation (at least one JPEGimage should be loaded into the A10-P).Screen saver will be launched each time in rotation.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:

```text
                         While A10-P is in idle (without receiving messages, keystrokes, or screen touch)
                         passing the period of time specified in [Waiting Time], the screen saver will be
                         activated. The minimum waiting time should be greater than or equal to 5 seconds.

    Screen saver - Jpeg Show: display all jpeg pictures in rotation (at least one JPEGimage should be
    loaded into the A10-P).Screen saver will be launched each time in rotation.

                    Time]
                    [Screen Saver     1             '1': Jpeg show
                    Type]
```

```text
Section 14            JPEG File Operation Messages
    A10-P supports several JPEG file operation messages. Customers can use the UIC provided JPEG Tool
    to query the A10-P to retrieve the JPEG file table. From that the user can delete the existed JPEG files
    from the A10-P or select the JPEG files for display. In addition, customers can download a JPEG file into
    the A10-P or upload a JPEG file from the A10-P. Below are the JPEG file operation messages A10-P
    supports:

       J0       JPEG File Table Initialization
       J1       Query JPEG File Table
       J2       Select JPEG File
       J3       Delete JPEG File
       J4       Download JPEG File
       J5       Upload JPEG File
       J6       Play JPEG File
       J7       Set JPEG File As Idle Prompt
       J8       Enable/Disable Idle Logo Functionality
       J9       Show JPEG File
       JA       Setup Boot Logo
```

[210] COMMAND J4 - Download JPEG File
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 14 - JPEG File Operation Messages
Source PDF page(s): 395-397
Format summary: <STX>J4[PktType][SeqNo][Force]<FS>[FileName]<FS>[Size] [Data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame) <STX>J4[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)
Message length: Variable 22 to 538 bytes for the request frame, and fixed 6 bytes for the response frame.
Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to download a JPEG file from the terminal.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message J4 - Download JPEG File
    Format:             <STX>J4[PktType][SeqNo][Force]<FS>[FileName]<FS>[Size]
                        [Data]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
                        <STX>J4[Status]<ETX>[LRC] (response frame)

    Message length: Variable 22 to 538 bytes for the request frame, and fixed 6 bytes for the response
                        frame.
    Usage:                 This message is used to download a JPEG file from the terminal.

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                         Field          Length                  Value and description

                   <STX>              1             <02>
                   J4                 2             Message ID
                   [PktType]          1             '0' = first or middle of multiple packets.
                                                    '1' = last or only packet.
                   [SeqNo]            3             '000' to '999'; for onetime only packet, set to
                                                    '000'.
                   [Force]            1             '0' = ask before overwrite, '1' = forced
                                                    overwrite
                   <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                   [FileName]         0-15          JPEG file name (optional)
                   <FS>               1             <1C>, field separator
                   [Size]             3             '000' to '523', size of [ImgData] in bytes
                   [ImgData]          0-523         Base 64 format data (optional)
                   <ETX>              1             <03>
                   [LRC]              1             Checksum

                                         Response frame (A10-P to HOST)
                        Field            Length                 Value and description

                   <STX>               1             <02>
                   J4                  2             Message ID
                   [Status]            1             '0': Ready for the next J4 packet.
                                                     '1': [PktType] has invalid value.
                                                     '2': [SeqNo] has invalid value.
                                                     '3': [Force] has invalid value.
                                                     '4': [FileName] has invalid value.
                                                     '5': [Size] has invalid value.
                                                     '6': [ImgData] has invalid value.
                                                     '7': Number of <FS> is wrong.
                                                     'A': File size is zero or too large.
                                                     'B': Null file name.
                                                     'C': File name is too long or user abort.
                                                     'D': No more space.
                                                     'E': File is too large to store
                                                     'F': Download Success.
                   <ETX>               1             <03>
```

[217] COMMAND ED - Load BIN Exception Table
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 15 - White List Configuration Messages
Source PDF page(s): 406-407
Format summary: <STX>ED.[Signature data]<FS>[BIN Exception Table]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: This message is used to load the BIN exception table (white list that excludes from encryption) to the reader. The reader will create a temporary buffer to collect all data, and then use the application public key to verify the signature. (Since the application public key is issued by the UIC, the acquirer needs to request UIC to sign the BIN exception table.) If verification succeeds, reader will replace the original BIN Exclusion Table; if verify failed, reader will abandon this data and return error code in the EE packet.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message ED - Load BIN Exception Table
    Format:              <STX>ED.[Signature data]<FS>[BIN Exception Table]<ETX>[LRC]
                         (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:               This message is used to load the BIN exception table (white list that excludes from
                         encryption) to the reader.
                         The reader will create a temporary buffer to collect all data, and then use the
                         application public key to verify the signature. (Since the application public key is issued
                         by the UIC, the acquirer needs to request UIC to sign the BIN exception table.)
                         If verification succeeds, reader will replace the original BIN Exclusion Table; if verify
                         failed, reader will abandon this data and return error code in the EE packet.

    Note:                To clear the whole white list, just send an empty entry to the reader: <STX>ED. <ETX>

    Message element:
                                          Request frame (HOST to A10-P)
                          Field         Length                 Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    ED                2             Message ID
                    .                 1             <2E>, delimiter.
                    [Signature        Var.          Base64 encoded signature of BIN exception
                    data]                           table entries.
                    <FS>              1             <1C> as field separator.
                    [BIN              Var.          ASCII string, refer to BIN Exception Rules
                    exception                       for detailed data format.
                    table]                          Maximum 50 entries are allowed.
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST               Direction                 A10-P

                    Message ED                       ->
                                                             <ACK> if LRC ok.
                                                     <-       <NAK> if LRC error.
                                                             <EOT> if LRC error after 2 retries.
                                                     <-       Message EE
                    <ACK> if LRC ok.
                    <NAK> if LRC error.
                                                     ->
                    <EOT> if LRC error
                    after 2 retries.
```

```text
Section 16                  Remote Key Loading Messages

    Remote Key Loading module allows the PIN Pad device to download and replace the key remotely from
    the HOST. The PIN Pad and HOST shall verify each other base on PKI (Public Key Infrastructure).                 The
    PIN Pad shall communicate with the Payment Terminal Application through USB or COM port and all the
    communications between the PIN Pad and HOST shall be passive and controlled by the POS.

    The details of the RKL module are listed in Appendix I.

    Terminology
    The following table lists the definitions of certificates, keys, and data to be exchanged in the RKL
    functions.

    1. Certificates and keys at HOST side:
           Certificates                 Related Keys                                Description
                                                             The CA root public key. This will be used to verify the
                                   PKRoot, CA                new CERHOST, intermediate. This root key shall be sent to UIC
                                                             and then hard coded into PIN Pad firmware.
                                                             The host's CA public key certificate, signed by the host's
    CERHOST, intermediate          PKHOST, intermediate      CA root Private Key. This will be pre-loaded into PIN
                                                             Pad and used to verify the CERHOST, RKL.
                                                             The host CA private key, used to sign CERHOST, RKL. It's
                                   SKHOST, intermediate
                                                             stored at the host side and is never exposed.
                                                             The host public key's Certificate, signed by the host's CA
    CERHOST, RKL                   PKHOST, RKL               Private Key. This will be used to verify the
                                                             acknowledgement from the host in RKL process.
                                                             The host private key. This key is used to sign the TDES
                                   SKHOST, RKL               key during the remote key loading. And it is stored at the
                                                             host side and is never exposed.

    2. Certificates and keys in the PIN pad side:
          Certificates                Related Keys                                  Description
                                                             UIC CA public key. This will be used to verify the
                                                             acknowledgement of CERPINPad, RKL when the host
                                  PKUIC
                                                             receives the certificate from PIN Pad in RKL process.
                                                             The host shall have an interface to pre-load it.
                                                             The UIC CA private key. This is only used inside of UIC
                                  SKUIC                      to sign the PKPINPad and generate CERUIC,CA. This private
                                                             key will never be exposed.
                                                             PIN Pad public key certificate, signed by UIC CA Private
    CERPINPad, RKL                PKPINPad, RKL              Key, SKUIC. The expiration date of the certificate should
                                                             be beyond the life cycle of the PIN Pad.
                                                             PIN Pad private Key. This key is preloaded to PIN Pad
                                  SKPINPad, RKL              during manufacturing and will be used to decrypt the
                                                             enciphered TDES key.

    3. Key to be injected:
             Element                                                Description
                                TDES cryptogram data (16 bytes binary data), generated by HOST and will be injected
                                into PIN Pad in Remote Key Loading process. The key is used to do the PIN encryption
    CI
                                or in other encryption algorithm like MAC. Each key only has its unique purpose for
                                secure consideration.
    B                           Key block of TDES Key encrypted by PKPIN Pad. B = (SNHOST // CI)PKPINPad

    4. Data for verification:
             Element                                                Description
    SNPINPad                    The serial number of the PIN Pad.
    SNHOST                      The serial number of the host RKL certificate, CERHOST, RKL.
    RA & RB                     8-byte Random numbers which are generated by PIN Pad (RA) and HOST (RB).

    5. Signed message and thumb print.
                  Element                                                 Description
    TP(CERHOST)                              Thumb print of the HOST's Certificate in PKCS#7 encoded in base64.
                                             RA, RB, Pin Pad Serial Number and B which are signed by private key of
                                             the host, SKHOST, RKL. It is a PKCS#7 format encoded in base64. The
    (RA//RB//SNPINPad//B)SKHOST
                                             literal sequence in PKCS#7 is RA, RB, SNPINPad, and B and SHA-1 for the
                                             integrity.
                                             The signature of RA//RB//SNHOST which is signed by private key of the
    (RA//RB//SNHOST)SKPINPad
                                             PIN Pad, SKPINPad, RKL. It is a PKCS#7 format encoded in base64.

    Command Flow
    The payment terminal needs to initiate the Remote Key Loading process. The following is the command
    flow:
```

[220] COMMAND R1 - Exchange Certificate Request
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section: Section 16 - Remote Key Loading Messages
Source PDF page(s): 414
Format summary: <STX>R1[CER]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)
Message length: Variable.
Purpose/usage summary: Initiate the certificate exchange by sending CERHOST, RKL to PIN pad. The certificate is RSA PKCS#7 enveloped PEM (data is base 64 encoded with the "-----BEGIN PKCS7-----" and "-----END PKCS7-----" marks). This command will initialize an "RKL session". During RKL session, only R series command and "72" command can be accepted by PIN pad.

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message R1 - Exchange Certificate Request
    Format:              <STX>R1[CER]<ETX>[LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:               Initiate the certificate exchange by sending CERHOST, RKL to PIN pad. The certificate is
                         RSA PKCS#7 enveloped PEM (data is base 64 encoded with the "-----BEGIN
                         PKCS7-----" and "-----END PKCS7-----" marks).
                         This command will initialize an "RKL session". During RKL session, only R series
                         command and "72" command can be accepted by PIN pad.

    Message element:

                         Field          Length               Value and description

                    <STX>             1             <02>
                    R1                2             Message ID
                    [CER]             Var.          RSA PKCS#7 eneveloped CERHOST,RKL in
                                                    PEM format.
                    <ETX>             1             <03>
                    [LRC]             1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                              HOST               Direction                  A10-P

                    Message R1                       ->
                                                               <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                     <-         <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                               (<EOT> after 3 NAKs)

                    <ACK> (Good LRC)
                    <NAK> (Bad LRC)                  ->
                    (<EOT> after 3 NAKs)
```

Full field-level specification and flow notes:
```text
Message R5 - Remote Key Loading Request
    Format:             <STX>R5[Key ID][Signed data][LRC] (request frame)

    Message length: Variable.
    Usage:              Send Remote Key Loading request with validation information.
                        This command must be issued in RKL session..

    Message element:
                                        Request fame (HOST to A10-P)
                        Field         Length                    Value and description

                   <STX>            1             <02>
                   R5               2             Message ID
                   [Key ID]         1             '0' to '9', 'B' to 'F'. ('A' is not available.)
                   [Signed data]    Var.          RSA PKCS#7 "signed data" structure in PEM
                                                  format.
                                                  (RA//RB//SNPINPad//B//key ID//usage//mode)
                                                  signed by SKHOST
                                                  RA: Random number generated by PIN Pad.
                                                  RB: Random number generated by Host.
                                                  SNPINPad: Serial number of PIN Pad.
                                                  B: (SNHOST//CI) encrypted by PKPINpad
                                                  -         SNHOST: Serial number of the Host
                                                  certificate
                                                  -         CI: TDES key data.
                                                  Key ID: the same with [Key ID] field
                                                  Usage: ANSI TR-31 usage of the key
                                                  Mode: ANSI TR-31 mode of the key
                   <ETX>            1             <03>
                   [LRC]            1             Checksum

    Message flow:
                            HOST               Direction                  A10-P

                     Message R5                    ->
                                                            <ACK> (Good LRC)
                                                   <-        <NAK> (Bad LRC)
                                                            (<EOT> after 3 NAKs)
                                                   <-        Message R6
                     <ACK> (Good LRC)
                     <NAK> (Bad LRC)               ->
                     (<EOT> after 3 NAKs)

    PKCS#7 Data structure of [Signed data] (ASN.1 annotation):
    ContentInfo ::= SEQUENCE {
                contentType                 ContentType,
                content                            [0]     EXPLICIT      ANT   DEFINED    BY   contentType
    OPTIONAL
    }
    ContentType ::= OBJECT IDENTIFIER                       -- value={pkcs-7 1}

    The content of PKCS#7-1 data defined as following
    Data ::= SEQUENCE {
                keyAndAuthData              KeyAndAuthData,        -- See definition below
                signature                   BIT STRING      -- PKCS#1 signature of keyAndAuthData
    }
    KeyAndAuthData ::= SEQUENCE {
                rA                          OCTET STRING           -- 8 bytes random A
                rB                          OCTET STRING           -- 8 bytes random B
                sn_PinPad         Printable String          -- 12 bytes serial # of PIN pad
                b                           OCTET STRING           -- encrypted TDES master key and
    SNHOST
                key_id                      INTEGER                -- 1 byte key id from 0~9, 11~15
                usage             Printable String          -- 2 bytes key usage
                mode              Printable String          -- 1 byte key mode
    }

    Encryption detail of TDES master key data "b":
    Clear text data (according to RSA PKCS#1 v1.5) = 0x00 | 0x02 | PS | 0x00 | DATA
    Where PS = non-zero random data of 256 - 3 - (length of DATA) bytes,
    DATA = ASN.1 DER encoding of following structure
    {sn_Host               OCTET STRING,
    key_value              OCTET STRING}
```

Message format, control codes, LRC, ACK/NAK/EOT behavior (PDF page 33-34)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```text
Section 4           Message Format
    This chapter provides the details of the format of messages exchanged between the host application and
    the A10-P.

Notation Conventions
    The following conventions are used to make the description of messages more readable:

    Control Codes
    Control codes (non-displayable codes) are represented by two to three capital letters enclosed in angled
    brackets "<>". This A10-P uses a total of 12 control codes. The actual code, when referenced, is
    represented by two hex digits enclosed in angled brackets, <0F> for example. The following table lists
    their usage and hex code values.

                 CODE        HEX VALUE                                USAGE

                  STX              02          Denotes the beginning of a message frame
                  ETX              03          Denotes the ending of a message frame
                  ACK              06          Acknowledge of message received
                  SO               0E          Denotes the ending of a message frame
                 NAK               15          Indicates invalid message received
                  SUB              1A          Message parameter follows
                   FS              1C          Field separator
                  GS               1D          Message ID follows
                  DC1              11          Used for Z2 message, enable the inverse mode.
                  DC2              12          Used for Z2 message, disable the inverse mode.

    [LRC]
    Each message frame transmitted is appended with an LRC byte to detect communication error. This byte
    should be regarded as part of the message frame but comes after the ending delimiter character. [LRC]
    is used in each message frame description to represent this LRC byte.
    LRC is calculated as an XORed value of every byte after the start code (<STX> or <SI>) in the message
    frame, all the way to and including the end code (<ETX> or <SO>).

    [item]
    A descriptive item name is enclosed in bracket. It denotes a string or data byte that has no fixed value.

Message frame summary
    The data exchanged between the A10-P and the host is grouped into "message frames". Each
    message frame has one of the two possible frame formats listed below:
    - <STX>[message ID][data]<ETX>[LRC]
    - <SI>[message ID][data]<SO>[LRC]
    Each type of message has a unique value in its message ID field. In the following texts, we refer a
    message type by its message ID value, e.g. "message 70".

    Message type
    Messages exchanged between the A10-P and the host can be divided into two categories.
    One category is for administration and maintenance. In general administrative messages have the <SI>
    packet header and its return message sent back to the host is using the same message ID.
    The other category is for various transactions In general transaction messages are using the <STX>
    packet header. The messages work in pair. The odd number message sends the command and data to
    the A10-P, and the even number message returns the result.

    Time-out
    Whenever the A10-P sends out a message, a response (<ACK> character for acknowledgement or
    <NAK> character if LRC error occurs) from the host is expected. If the A10-P does not receive a
    response within 5 seconds, it will retransmit the last packet. If the A10-P does not receive <ACK> or
    <NAK> after two retransmit attempts, it will send out the <EOT> character and this communication
    session will be terminated.

    Transmission Error
    When the host decides that an invalid frame is received, it will send out the <NAK>. When the A10-P
    receives a <NAK>, it will retransmit its last message. If the message retransmitted is invalid again, then a
    <NAK> is sent by the host to request for another try. The A10-P will keep on retransmitting the message
    until an <ACK> or <EOT> is received.

    Packet Error
    When the A10-P receives a good transmission but an invalid packet (wrong message id), it will ignore the
    packet. If the received packet has an acceptable message id but having a wrong format, the A10-P will
    send out <EOT> as the error message. It will send out more detailed error codes if the messages are
    PIN entry functions.
```

Security and account-data rules relevant to card data output (PDF page 23-28)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```text
    Asymmetric Keys
      Key Name                         Algorithm / Size (bits)             Purpose / Usage
      EMV CA public keys               RSA: 1024 ~ 1984                    Verifies Issuer and ICC public key
                                                                           certificates.

    Security policy for key management
    1. The acquirer should manage the KTK and other secret keys in compliance with PCI security
          requirements. Improper use of the key management system will invalidate PCI approval to the
          A10-P.
    2. Use FIPS 140-2 validated HSM to store secret keys to achieve proper security.
    3. Keep "dual control" and "spilt of knowledge" principles for key injection or transportation.
    4. Maintain KTK, passwords, and secret keys to be unique for each A10-P unit.
    5. A10-P not only will reject the incorrect key bundle but also reject the insecure key update request
          defined by the PCI secure requirement:
          -     Key length larger than KTK.
          -     Repeated key value. (In other words, all symmetric keys in the A10-P should have different
                values, no matter what the key is.)
    6. Any key should be replaced with a new key whenever the compromise of the original key is known or
          suspected; and whenever the time deemed feasible to determine the key by exhaustive attack
          elapses.

PIN security
    A10-P protects user's PIN in accordance with the PCI PTS security requirements.
    - A10-P supports ISO9564 format 0, 2, 4 PIN blocks. Refer to Appendix B for detailed information.
    - A10-P deters the use of the device for exhaustive PIN determination: When doing transactions using
          the MK/SK scheme, the firmware of A10-P applies a DES calculation count limiter (only 10
          transactions are allowed in 5 minutes period.) to comply with the PCI PED security requirement
          (average one transaction per 30 seconds.)

Account data security
    A10-P provides two software configurations that have different account data security implementation,
    which can be confirmed from the firmware version string:
    1. PCI PTS Only
         Account data output messages (81, 83, QJ, T22, T26, T28, T2I, T64, T66) will output clear text
         account data. The IC card direct access messages (I01 ~ I07) are available. The MSR and RFID
         operation control messages (Q6 / QD) will not allow user to set encryption options.
    2. PTS + SRED configuration
         A10-P will obfuscate and encrypt the following data elements (that are not listed in the BIN exception
         table) from the MSR, ICC, and RFID before output.

            -     Primary account number (PAN), apply to EMV tag 0x5A
            -     Magnetic stripe track 1 data (TK1), apply to EMV tag 0x562
            -     Magnetic stripe track 2 data (TK2), apply to EMV tag 0x57
            -     Magnetic stripe track 3 data (TK3)

Payment Track Identification Rules
      The following section defines how a track is considered a "payment card" track. If a track is not a
      payment card track, or if it is a payment card with a PAN that falls into the loaded BIN exception ranges,
      there is no obfuscation or encryption performed.

      A given card could contain tracks that are both payment and non-payment - this could be indicative of
      incorrect or unexpected card encoding. We want to ensure if a payment card has had a track miscode
      (e.g., a single letter) we still protect what looks like payment data.

      Note: The AAMVA card number range will not be identified as payment track.

      Track 1
      First byte in the track (after sentinel) is a 'B'
      Next, there are 12-19 digits (or spaces) followed by a '^' separator
      Next, there are 0 - 26 alphanumeric characters followed by a second '^' separator
      Next, there are 4 digits (expiration date)
      Remainder of track can be any data of any length
      Examples of payment card track 1:
      %B6011000993000201999^YOUR NAME GOES HERE^131200033ABCDEFG123232?
      %B000000000000^^1312?

      Track 2 and Track 3
      Track starts (after sentinel) with 12-19 numeric characters followed by a '=' separator
      Next, there are 4 digits (expiration date)
      Remainder of track can be any data of any length
      Examples of payment card track 2/3:
      ;6011000993000201999=13120003334567890?
      ;000000000000=1312?

BIN Exception Rules
      BIN (Bank Identification Number) refers to the leftmost 6 digits of PAN that identifies the issuer bank.
      A10-P retains a 50-entry white list that can exclude specific PAN range from account data encryption.

2
    Not every IC card contains 0x56 or sufficient information to composite track 1 equivalent data.
    The algorithm is:
    IF (card has valid payment track) AND (PAN is within the range of any BIN exception entry)
    THEN (output the track data in clear text form).
    This feature can be used to exclude driver licenses, gift cards, or royalty cards from being encrypted.

    The time stamp format of the BIN exception table is:
    YYMMDDhhmmss<CR><LF> (First line as time stamp)
    The data format of the white list entry is:
    [Minimum PAN].[Maximum PAN]<CR><LF>
    Each PAN field must have 12 digit numbers.
    Example:
    400000000000.499999999999
    510000000000.559999999999
    352800000000.358999999999
    601100000000.601199999999
    622126000000.622925999999
    502244000000.502244999999

    The above data will make A10-P exclude the following account numbers from encryption:

        Entry           Min PAN                           Max PAN

        Line 1          400000000000                      4999999999999999999

        Line 2          510000000000                      5599999999999999999

        Line 3          352800000000                      3589999999999999999

        Line 4          601100000000                      6011999999999999999

        Line 5          622126000000                      6229259999999999999

        Line 6          502244000000                      5022449999999999999

MSR Track Obfuscation Rules
    A valid payment track that does not fall into the loaded BIN exception ranges will be obfuscated by
    following rules:

    Track 1
    Start sentinel (%) and end sentinel (?) are present.
    Spaces in the PAN before the first ^ delimiter remain as-is. These spaces should not be masked or
    obfuscated.
    Any digits in PAN between first 6 and last 4 before first ^ delimiter are replaced by zeroes.
    The 7th digit is changed to a 1 only if necessary to ensure the card number fails a Luhn check.
    Any digits after the expiration date and service code (7 digits immediately after the second ^ delimiter)
    are replaced by zeroes.
    Example:
    Cleartext:             %B3727 006 9925 1018^AMEX TEST CARD^2512990502700?
    Obfuscated:            %B3727 000 0000 1018^AMEX TEST CARD^2512990000000?

    Track 2 and Track 3
    Start sentinel (;) and end sentinel (?) are present.
    Any digits in PAN between first 6 and last 4 before the first = delimiter are replaced by zeroes.
    The 7th digit is changed to a 1 only if necessary to ensure the card number fails a Luhn check.
    Any digits after the expiration date and service code (7 digits immediately after the = delimiter) are
    replaced by zeroes.
    Example:
    Cleartext:             ;372700699251018=2512990502700?
    Obfuscated:            ;372700000001018=2512990000000?

MSR Track Encryption Rules
    A valid payment track that does not fall into the loaded BIN exception ranges will be encrypted by the
    following rules:
    Track 1 and 2
    - Start sentinel (%) and end sentinel (?) are present.
    - The byte array that contains track data will be padded by the rule in the specification chapter 6.1.1 or
          value with 0xFF to make the stream length divisible by 8 bytes.
          For example, if the clear text track data is ;372700699251018=2512990502700? (31 bytes), so
          the padded data, express in hexadecimal form, will be:
          3B3337323730303639393235313031383D323531323939303530323730303F01
          (The last 01 is the padding byte in this case).
                                                            Or
          3B3337323730303639393235313031383D323531323939303530323730303FFF
          (The last FF is the padding byte in this case).

    - Each padded track data is encrypted by a designated MSR working key (should be 24 bytes in
          length) , the initial vector (IV) is 8 bytes random number ;or DUKPT current key (data encryption
          variant) in code block chaining (CBC) mode, the initial vector (IV) is 0000000000000000.
    - The encrypted track will be encoded into hexadecimal string (e.g. "3C" represents 0x3C) for all kinds
          of the output packets.
    - All tracks in a single swipe shares the same data encryption key and the KSN.
    - Data encryption and decryption can only be performed ten times in 300 seconds.
    Track 3
    The track 3 will not be encrypted (only obfuscated data will be output).

ICC Data Obfuscation Rules
    For EMV transaction, A10-P TransArmor version will put obfuscated data into the following tags:

        Tag            Description         Obfuscation Rule

        0x5A           Primary Account Any digits in PAN between first 6 and last 4 are replaced by
                       Number (PAN)        zeroes. The 7th digit is changed to a 1 only if necessary to
                                           ensure the card number fails a Luhn check.
                                           For example:
                                           PAN = 372700699251018
                                           Obfuscated = 372700000001018
                                           Tag 5A formatted = 37 27 00 00 00 01 01 8F

        0x9F1F         Track 1             All digits are replaced by zero.
                       discretionary       For example:
                       data                Tk1 discretionary data = 502700
                                           Obfuscated = 000000
                                           Tag 9F1F formatted = 30 30 30 30 30 30

        0x9F20         Track 2             All digits are replaced by zero.
                       discretionary       For example:
                       data                Tk1 discretionary data = 502700
                                           Obfuscated = 000000
                                           Tag 9F20 formatted = 00 00 00

        0x56           Track 1             The same with MSR track 1.
                       equivalent data     For example:
                                           Tk1 = B372700699251018^AMEX TEST
                                           CARD^2512990502700
                                           Obfuscated = B372700000001018^AMEX TEST
                                           CARD^2512990000000
                                           Tag 56 formatted data is the same ASCII string.

        0x57           Track 2             The same with MSR track 2.

                       equivalent data       For example:
                                             Tk2 = 372700699251018=2512990502700
                                             Obfuscated = 372700000001018=2512990000000
                                             Tag 57 formatted = 37 27 00 00 00 01 01 8D 25 12 99
                                             00 00 00 0F
                                             (The right nibble 'D' of the 8th byte represents the field
                                             separator, the last 'F' is the padding nibble.)

ICC Data Encryption Rules
    Track 1 and 2 equivalent data
    - The tag 56 (Track 1 equivalent data) and tag 57 (Track 2 equivalent data) will be converted to ASCII
          strings. Replace the track 2 field separator from 0xD to '=', and apply the same encryption rule with
          the MSR.
    - The start and end sentinels like MSR will be added to the track equivalent data.
    - The plaintext track equivalent data will be padded by PKCS#5 rule or value with 0xFF, then
          encrypted by the designated MSR working key (should be 24 bytes in length). The initial vector (IV)
          is 8 bytes random number ; or DUKPT current key (data encryption variant) in code block chaining
          (CBC) mode, the initial vector (IV) is 0000000000000000.
    - The encrypted track + MAC will be encoded into hexadecimal string (e.g. "3C" represents 0x3C) for
          all kinds of the output packets.
    - Data encryption and decryption can only be performed ten times in 300 seconds
```

Contact EMV Level 2 section notes before first command (PDF page 82-84)

```text
Section 6           Contact EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
EMV Level2 transaction messages are divided into 2 groups. One group are the EMV-configuration data
operation messages (T01, T03, T05, T07, T09, T0B) and the other group are the EMV-transaction messages
(T11, T13, T15, T17, T19, T1C, T21, T25, T27, T29).

The issuing sequence of the ICC EMV transaction messages is controlled by the A10-P.                An invalid
sequence will terminate that ICC EMV transaction. In the beginning of an ICC EMV transaction, the user has
to issue message T11 to make the A10-P to negotiate with the card and generate a candidate list of
EMV-applications that are supported both by the A10-P and the card.       It will then automatically select the
application with the highest priority or the one selected by the user (according to the terminal configuration
data installed in the A10-P), and then return the EMV-application name. Message T15 is used for the
terminal-side to transmit transaction information such as the amount to be used by the A10-P to complete the
transaction with the card if the transaction does not need to be authorized online. The terminal can issue
message T1D to transmit additional transaction data to the A10-P for ICC EMV transaction.       Examples are
online response data and magnetic stripe card track data. Message T17 is applied if the transaction needs to
be authorized online. The terminal-side will transmit necessary information via this message to the A10-P to
complete the rest of transactional steps. If the response from the host contains issuer script (see EMV), the
terminal-side will issue message T19 to send these scripts into the A10-P. Then the A10-P will issue these
scripts at appropriate time to the card. Message T1C is used to terminate an ICC EMV transaction. Finally,
message T21 is used for terminal-side to get the transaction information throughout the EMV transaction.

The terminal can apply the same set of Txx messages for handling a complete ICC EMV transaction but for
turning out the transaction must be changed to magnetic stripe card processing. According to EMV rule, if the
terminal fails to read the IC card, the transaction could be switched to the magnetic stripe card transaction.
Because of the different types of magnetic stripe cards, the magnetic stripe card processing should be taken
by the terminal. The terminal can issue message Q1 provided by the A10-P to let the user to swipe his card
and then issue message 70 to complete a magnetic stripe card transaction. In this situation, the terminal will
get the T11 response message that indicates a failed IC card read. The terminal should then issue message
T1D, T15 and T17 to the A10-P for batch data capture. The flow chart for changing to magnetic stripe card
processing can be found in the "Overall Contact EMV level 2 transaction flow reference" section.

The meanings of the error codes in the [Err Message] are listed below:
    Error Code                                                Error Description
00000003            Service not accepted.
00000004            POS execution.
00000008            Application selection.
00000F9B            Store configuration data error.
80000001            General error.
80000003            No information.
80000005            Timeout.
8000000C            Initial application error.
8000000E            Application not initial.
80000016            ICC function not supported.
80000019            Invalid terminal data.
```

```text
Section 7             Contactless EMV Level 2 Transaction Messages
Contactless EMV Level2 transaction messages are divided into 2 groups. One group are the
EMV-configuration data operation messages (T51, T53, T55, T75, T77) and the other group are the
EMV-transaction messages (T61, T63, T65, T6C, T71 and T73).

The issuing sequence of the PCD EMV transaction messages is controlled by the A10-P. An invalid
sequence will terminate that PCD EMV transaction. Message T61 is used for the terminal-side to transmit
transaction information such as the amount to be used by the A10-P to complete the transaction with the card
if the transaction does not need to be authorized online. Message T71 is applied if the transaction needs to
be authorized online. The terminal-side will transmit necessary information via this message to the A10-P to
complete the rest of transactional steps. If the response from the host contains issuer script (see EMV Book),
the terminal-side will issue message T73 to send these scripts into the A10-P. Then the A10-P will issue
these scripts at appropriate time to the card. Message T6C is used to terminate an EMV transaction. Finally,
message T65 is used for terminal-side to get the transaction information through out the PCD EMV
transaction. The transaction flow can be referred in the "Overall Contactless EMV level 2 transaction flow
reference" section.
```

Prompt control Z2/Z3 mode notes (PDF page 299)

```text
Section 11             Prompt Control and Data Entry Messages
The display prompts of the A10-P are built-in and digitally signed with the A10-P application to ensure it's
integrity and authenticity.
These commands have fixed display prompts:
-    Start IC card transaction (T11, T15, T33)
-    Start RFID transaction (T61, Q8)
-    Swipe Magnetic Stripe Card (Q1)
-    Combined card transaction (Q9, QK)
-    Standard PIN entry (70)
These commands have selectable display prompts:
-    Non-PIN data entry (Z42, Z50): The prompt can be selected from Appendix G (Z2/Z3 authenticated
     mode)
-    PIN entry with external prompts (Z60)
-    PIN entry with customized prompts (Z62)
The host application can also command A10-P to display any string on the LCD, but if the prompt string is not
MAC authenticated, the PIN entry or data entry function will be disabled.

Z2 / Z3 Authenticated mode with fixed prompt
    To enable messages Z42 and Z50, the user has to issue Z2 / Z3 messages with a prompt ID supported
    by the A10-P (See Appendix G). These prompts are verified to make sure users will not expose sensitive
    information (such as PIN) accidentally.

    For security reason, to issue the authenticated frame of Z2 / Z3 at the first time, the <SUB> flag is
    mandatory. After the Z2 authenticated mode is entered, the A10-P will accept two kinds of Z2 packet:
    1. Z2 packet in normal mode, without the <SUB> flagand contains only digits (0~9)
    2. Z2 packet in authenticated mode, without the <SUB> flag.
    For example, issuing Z2<GS>005<SUB> and Z2<GS>016 will show "PLEASE ENTER DRIVER
    LICENSE" on the screen.

Z2 / Z3 PIN entry mode with fixed prompt
    To enable message Z60, the user has to issue Z2 / Z3 messages with a prompt ID supported by the
    A10-P dedicated for PIN entry (See Appendix H). These prompts are verified to make sure users will not
    misunderstand the PIN entry request message as other non-sensitive data. Also prompt1 and prompt2 of
    message Z62 will be checked to see if they are listed in this prompt table. If not, the A10-P will reject
    message Z62.

    Messages other than Z2, Z3, Z42, Z50, and Z60, or any unsuccessful Z2 / Z3 messages (wrong prompt
    ID, format error, Z2 message including non decimal characters), will make the A10-P leaving the Z2 / Z3
    authenticated mode to avoid attack.
```

ICC/SAM/MSR/PCD section notes (PDF page 327)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```text
Section 12            ICC, SAM, MSR, and PCD Track Reading
Messages
    Messages listed in this section are used to:
    - Access IC card, SAM card directly (EMV power-up, power-down, APDU exchange.)
    - Read magnetic stripe card.
    - Read contactless smart card and output MSR track equivalent data.
    NOTE: By default, the MSR function is turned off until the user issues the Q4 command to enable it.

    I00 ~ I07: IC card manipulation.
    I11 ~ I17: SAM card manipulation.
    Q1 ~ Q7: Read magnetic stripe card and output control.
    Q8 ~ QJ: Read contactless smard card (MSR emulation) and output control.
    QK: Multiple interface (MSR, ICC, Contactless) card detection and reading.
    81: MSR data output
    83: Contactless MSR emulation data output.

    Depend on the firmware configuration (PTS only or PTS + SRED), the clear text data output is not
    available.

    PTS Only Configuration
    - I01 ~ I06 (ICC manipulation) is available.
    - Q6 (MSR operation control) does NOT support options for data encryption.
    - 81 (MSR card data) outputs clear text track data.
    - 83 (Contactless card data) outputs clear text track equivalent data.

    PTS + SRED Configuration
    - I01 ~ I06 (ICC manipulation) is NOT available.
    - Q6 (MSR operation control) supports data encryption (MK/SK and DUKPT) option.
    - QD (Contactless)
    - 81 (MSR card data) outputs encrypted (and optionally obfuscated) track data.
    - 83 (Contactless card data) outputs encrypted (and optionally obfuscated) track equivalent data.
```

```text
Section 16                  Remote Key Loading Messages

    Remote Key Loading module allows the PIN Pad device to download and replace the key remotely from
    the HOST. The PIN Pad and HOST shall verify each other base on PKI (Public Key Infrastructure).                 The
    PIN Pad shall communicate with the Payment Terminal Application through USB or COM port and all the
    communications between the PIN Pad and HOST shall be passive and controlled by the POS.

    The details of the RKL module are listed in Appendix I.

    Terminology
    The following table lists the definitions of certificates, keys, and data to be exchanged in the RKL
    functions.

    1. Certificates and keys at HOST side:
           Certificates                 Related Keys                                Description
                                                             The CA root public key. This will be used to verify the

                                                             and then hard coded into PIN Pad firmware.
                                                             The host's CA public key certificate, signed by the host's
    CERHOST, intermediate          PKHOST, intermediate      CA root Private Key. This will be pre-loaded into PIN
                                                             Pad and used to verify the CERHOST, RKL.
                                                             The host CA private key, used to sign CERHOST, RKL. It's
                                   SKHOST, intermediate
                                                             stored at the host side and is never exposed.
                                                             The host public key's Certificate, signed by the host's CA
    CERHOST, RKL                   PKHOST, RKL               Private Key. This will be used to verify the
                                                             acknowledgement from the host in RKL process.
                                                             The host private key. This key is used to sign the TDES
                                   SKHOST, RKL               key during the remote key loading. And it is stored at the
                                                             host side and is never exposed.

    2. Certificates and keys in the PIN pad side:
          Certificates                Related Keys                                  Description

                                  PKUIC

                                                             key will never be exposed.

    CERPINPad, RKL                PKPINPad, RKL              Key, SKUIC. The expiration date of the certificate should

                                                             PIN Pad private Key. This key is preloaded to PIN Pad
                                  SKPINPad, RKL              during manufacturing and will be used to decrypt the

             Element                                                Description

    B                           Key block of TDES Key encrypted by PKPIN Pad. B = (SNHOST // CI)PKPINPad

    (RA//RB//SNPINPad//B)SKHOST
                                             literal sequence in PKCS#7 is RA, RB, SNPINPad, and B and SHA-1 for the
                                             integrity.
                                             The signature of RA//RB//SNHOST which is signed by private key of the

                                             PIN Pad, SKPINPad, RKL. It is a PKCS#7 format encoded in base64.
```
